Since the manifestation of the fire of Time first arises from the hells,
the Lord, although situated below, is all-pervading: such is the view of the venerable <s>Raurava</s>.
In the ashes blown away by <s>Brahmā</s>'s exhalation, with the water of his sweat,
the universe, drenched by that water of his, remains until the arrival of night.
During that limit of night, all <s>pudgalas</s> (individual beings), having gone into subtle bodies,
driven by the force of fire, become, in the world of beings, merely dissolved.
But the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, <s>Hāṭakas</s>, and the rest sport in the great abode.
At the end of the night, again, one overcome by darkness brings forth creation.
At the end of his own hundred years there is his destruction; that is the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> day.
And the night is just as long; thus the periods called hundreds of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Rudra</s>,
in sequence, at the ends of their own hundreds of years, perish here through the dissolution of the cosmic egg.
From water and the rest up to the unmanifest tattva, in this way, by a hundred years in sequence,
there is a division of day and night according to the measure of each one's own hundred-year lifespan.
But by the thirty-six thousand surges of <s>Brahmā</s>'s dissolution,
for the <s>Rudras</s> who dwell in the unmanifest there is a day, and the night is just as long.
Then <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> himself is the lord, directly the agent of dissolution.
So too all the <s>Rudras</s> at the root, office-holders within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>,
remain in what is called the unmanifest, from <s>Viriñci</s> onward, together with <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.
For <s>Brahmā</s>, whose action below <s>Nivṛtti</s> has ceased, is there below, belonging to the lower level of cognition.

children.text: na bhoktā jño 'dhikāre tu vṛtta eva śivībhavet
children.translated_text: He is not an enjoyer but a knower; when his office has been completed, he becomes <s>Śiva</s>.
This is the intermediate dissolution; when it has ended, creation is said to occur.
At the dawn of that day, <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> again creates those perfected through <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the <s>Veda</s>, and the like.
Therefore this sort of thing is not complete liberation.
The day and night that belong to <s>Pradhāna</s>, and the hundred years born from that,
are the lifespan of the lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>; and this is a day for those dwelling in the <s>kañcukas</s>.
Following that order, these, namely <s>Niyati</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Rāga</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, and <s>Kalā</s>,

children.text: yāntyanyonyaṃ layaṃ teṣām āyur gāhanikaṃ dinam ||
children.translated_text: pass into dissolution one into another; their lifespan is a day of the <s>Gahana</s> level.
At the exhaustion of that day, the universe dissolves into <s>Māyā</s>.
When the night, just as long, has been exhausted, <s>Gahaneśa</s> creates again.
Thus one should reckon the time of the unmanifest by ten <s>parārdhas</s>.
The night extending to the hand of <s>Māyā</s> would be such; this is that dissolution.
Multiplying the time of <s>Māyā</s> by a hundred <s>parārdhas</s>,
the <s>Aiśvara</s> day is <s>Nāda</s>; here, as <s>Prāṇa</s>, it creates the world.
And the <s>Aiśvara</s> night is just as long, in which <s>Prāṇa</s> comes to rest.
Even the universe that is lodged in the womb of <s>Prāṇa</s> here, by the path of <s>Suṣumnā</s>,
when <s>Prāṇa</s> is stilled in the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>, remains only as consciousness.
From the relation of part and possessor of parts, there is a dissolution subtler and subtler even than this.
Multiplying the <s>Aiśvara</s> time by a hundred <s>parārdhas</s>,
there is the <s>Sādāśiva</s> day and night, and the great dissolution as well.
<s>Sadāśiva</s>, at the end of his own time, having passed through <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Ardhendu</s>, and <s>Nirodhikā</s>,
dissolves into <s>Nāda</s>, taking with him all that moves and does not move.

children.text: nādo nādāntavṛttyā tu bhittvā brahmabilaṃ haṭhāt
children.translated_text: <s>Nāda</s>, through the activity of <s>Nādānta</s>, breaks through the aperture of <s>Brahman</s> by force
and, at the expiration of its own time, goes to dissolution in the <s>Śakti</s> tattva.
This much indeed should be understood as the day and night in the <s>Śakti</s> tattva.
At the dissolution of her own time, <s>Śakti</s> again dissolves into <s>Vyāpinī</s>.
For <s>Vyāpinī</s> there is that day and night; she too dissolves into <s>Anāśrita</s>.
Even after multiplying the time of <s>Śakti</s> by a crore of <s>parārdhas</s>, in <s>Anāśrita</s>,
there is a day and night; and when that time too is multiplied by a <s>parārdha</s>,

children.text: so 'pi yāti layaṃ sāmyasaṃjñe sāmanase pade ||
children.translated_text: that too goes to dissolution in the <s>Sāmanasa</s> state called <s>Sāmya</s>.
That time is called <s>Sāmya</s>; it is eternal, without divisible measure, and yet of the nature of measure.
That form which is <s>Sāmanasa</s> is <s>Sāmya</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> that pervades the universe.
Therefore, from <s>Sāmanasa</s> time, in only the measure of a closing and opening of the eyes,
she produces the fixed series here, from <s>tuṭi</s> and the rest up to <s>parārdha</s>.
Ten, hundred, thousand, <s>ayuta</s>, <s>lakṣa</s>, <s>niyuta</s>, <s>koṭi</s> together with <s>arbuda</s>, and <s>vṛnda</s>,
<s>kharva</s>, <s>nikharva</s>, <s>śaṅkha</s>, <s>abja</s>, <s>jaladhi</s>, <s>madhya</s>, <s>anta</s>, and then <s>parārdha</s>:

children.text: ityekasmātprabhṛti hi daśadhā daśadhā krameṇa kalayitvā
children.translated_text: thus, beginning from one and calculating tenfold and tenfold in succession,
one should state their position among the eighteen numbers ending with one and <s>parārdha</s>.

children.text: catvāra ete pralayā mukhyāḥ sargāśca tatkalāḥ
children.translated_text: These four dissolutions are principal, and so too are the creations whose phases correspond to them.
They stand at earth, root, night, and <s>Śakti</s>; that is the fourfold cosmic egg.
<s>Kālāgni</s> is the destroyer on earth; at the end of <s>Māyā</s> it is the king of the <s>Kāla</s> tattva.
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, at the root, is singly the agent of creation and dissolution.
Its dissolution is intermediate; therefore one lord governs creation and dissolution.
The glorious <s>Aghora</s> is the destroyer at the end of <s>Śakti</s>, and he too is the creator.
Since in his creation the creations and dissolutions of countless worlds
are included, therefore the great <s>Śāktī</s> creation is declared.
At dissolution, hundreds of <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Haris</s>, and <s>Rudras</s>, in groups of eight and five,
successively go into dissolution, one into another, along the path whose end is <s>Māyā</s>.
But at the dissolution of the <s>Māyā</s> tattva, these attain the supreme state.
Those who are above <s>Māyā</s> and stand on the white path dissolve into <s>Paramaśiva</s>.
Even there, because of distinctions due to limiting conditions, the wise know distinctions in dissolution.

children.text: evaṃ tāttveśvare varge līne sṛṣṭau punaḥ pare ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the class of tattva-lords has dissolved, and creation again proceeds from the Supreme,
their practitioners, or those dear to <s>Śiva</s>, take charge of those stations.

children.text: brāhmī nāma parasyaiva śaktistāṃ yatra pātayet ||
children.translated_text: The power of the Supreme itself, named <s>Brāhmī</s>, wherever he casts it,
there he is <s>Brahmā</s>; by <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> and the others, in sequence, he is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and so on.

children.text: śaktimantaṃ vihāyānyaṃ śaktiḥ kiṃ yāti nedṛśam ||
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the possessor of power, does <s>Śakti</s> go to another? This is not so.
Likewise, <s>Śiva</s> alone is power, covering and manifesting all things.
Thus emanations and dissolutions, and <s>Prāṇa</s>, are established in one place.
That too is in consciousness, and consciousness is in mere awareness, devoid of anything knowable.

children.text: cinmātrameva devī ca sā parā parameśvarī ||
children.translated_text: And the goddess, the supreme <s>Parameśvarī</s>, is nothing but pure consciousness.
And the thirty-eighth reality is the heart, that supreme-and-non-supreme principle.
Therefore this is simply consciousness itself, vibrating by its own nature.
Because of dissolution and arising, the arising of the sixty-year cycle is taught in the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath).
This discussion of the variety of action rests merely upon will.
From that there is the power of time outwardly; this has no fixed form.
In a dream within a dream, and likewise in dream, sleep, and the field of imagination,
and in <s>samādhi</s>, when discerning the sequence of the universe's dissolution and creation,
even a limited portion of time appears, so to speak, as extended.
When there is a difference of subjects, or a difference in cognition, this same time attains a varied extension.
Thus, just as time in the <s>prāṇa</s> is born from the power of diverse action,
so too it is in the <s>apāna</s>, which spreads from the heart to the root-seat.
In the contraction and expansion of the great seat called the root,
it gathers up the creations and dissolutions of those from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the Unresting principle.
Although this <s>apāna</s> always flows in this way, nevertheless it
is worshiped by yogins with effort, even though its effort is not an object of ordinary cognition.
Those who extend through the twelve-end, through the contraction and expansion of the bliss of the heart-bulb,
from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the Unresting principle, are served here by excellent yogins.
And these, because they are powers of the supreme Lord, exist throughout the universe.
Since they also pervade the body, they are causes; so it is said in the <s>Kāmika</s>.
In childhood, youth, old age, death, rebirth,
liberation, and embodiment, those beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> are the makers of the six stations.

children.text: tasyānte tu parā devī yatra yukto na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: But at its end is the supreme goddess, where one who is united is not born again.
By merely knowing this, one becomes capable of granting initiation and grace.
For when the state in which all causes unfold is well known,
one finds causeless <s>Śiva</s>, who is the cause of this universe.
This downward-facing power utterly destroys the sole stain of duality.
Through worship of it, the display of upper and lower is exhausted.
Here, at the arising of <s>apāna</s>, one should apply, as before, the scheme of the sixty-year arising,
from the <s>tuṭi</s> onward, according to the division of connected <s>aṅgulas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ samāne 'pi vidhiḥ sa hi hārdīṣu nāḍiṣu ||
children.translated_text: So too in the <s>samāna</s> the rule applies, for it moves through the heart-nāḍīs
and is to be contemplated as tenfold, facing all directions.
Filling the ten principal great <s>nāḍīs</s>, this breath, situated in them,
successively pervades the nāḍīs that depend on other nāḍīs, establishing equilibrium in the body.
As it moves through the eight directional petals, in the sequence of the lords of those directions,
it appears as both fierce and gentle, imitating their activities.
The same breath, in the triad of nāḍīs situated on the left, right, and middle,
moves in the principal channels made of moon, sun, and fire, and remains there day and night.
For as long as it remains through two and a half <s>nālīs</s> and nine hundred breaths,
for that long, carrying them through the day and night, it proceeds in twenty-four divisions.

children.text: viṣuvadvāsare prātaḥ sāṃśāṃ nālīṃ sa madhyagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the equinoctial day, in the morning, it is in the middle, through a <s>nālī</s> with its fractions,
and then through left, other, north, left, and the rest, up to the five transitions.
Thus, when nearly fourteen <s>nālīs</s> have diminished, lacking a quarter,
at midday, at the right equinox, it carries nine hundred breaths.
Through right, north, other, north, and right, there is again the set of five transitions.
In the nine divisions there is a hundred each; thereafter comes the northern equinox.
When each set of five has passed, outside the equinox and transition,
just as it is outside, so within there is a transition of nine hundred breaths.
Thus also at night; and in this way, beginning from the equal equinoctial day,
this breath also passes through the transitions of increase and decrease of day and night.
The final part of night and the first part of day, midday, the waning of day,
and the rise of night are the middle; such is the northern course at the equinox.

children.text: vyāptau viṣer yato vṛttiḥ sāmyaṃ ca vyāptirucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because the root viṣ means pervasion, and equality too is called pervasion,
the time that deserves that name is here called <s>viṣuvat</s> (equinox).
The decreases and increases of day and night that begin from the equinox
are, in that very sequence, the decreases and increases of the transitions of day and night.
Thus the two-year conception belongs to the wind called <s>samāna</s>.
This is a course in one place; here there is no discussion of inhalation and exhalation.
In <s>samāna</s> too, before the <s>tuṭi</s>, up to the domain of the sixty-year cycle,
the reckoning of time, proceeding in a single extremely subtle course, is counted by the wise.
What is called twilight, forenoon, midday, midnight, and so forth
is to be understood as occurring in the internal transition; that is primary, because from it the result arises.

children.text: uktaḥ samānagaḥ kāla udāne tu nirūpyate ||
children.translated_text: The time belonging to <s>samāna</s> has been taught; now it is explained in <s>udāna</s>.
What was stated regarding the pervasion of <s>prāṇa</s> applies here also to <s>udāna</s>, only
with the place being the region above the <s>brahmarandhra</s>, at the two ends of the nasal power.
Therefore in this <s>udāna</s> one should examine the whole time, from the heart to the head and up to the twelve-end,
from the <s>tuṭi</s> onward to the end of the sixty years.
But in the <s>vyāna</s>, which is all-formed, all-pervasive, and free from sequence,
time is established as merely an exceedingly subtle, flashing form.
Since creation, dissolution, stability, withdrawal, and grace occur from it,
one should therefore resort to each respective form of time in <s>prāṇa</s> and the others in sequence.
Here, in the course of <s>prāṇa</s>, the arising of phoneme, word, and mantra is established.

children.text: yatnajo 'yatnajaḥ sūkṣmaḥ paraḥ sthūlaḥ sa kathyate ||
children.translated_text: It is said to be effort-born and not effort-born, subtle, supreme, and gross.
There is one phoneme whose nature is sound, containing the undivided totality of all phonemes.
Because its form never sets, it is here called unstruck sound.

children.text: sa tu bhairavasadbhāvo mātṛsadbhāva eṣa saḥ
children.translated_text: That is the real nature of <s>Bhairava</s>; this is the real nature of the <s>Mātṛ</s>.

children.text: parā saikākṣarā devī yatra līnaṃ carācaram ||
children.translated_text: She is the supreme one-syllabled goddess, in whom the moving and unmoving world is dissolved.
Each of the three short vowels is a solar <s>aṅgula</s>; then the other is different.
The six phonemes called entry proceed in order along the paths of sun and moon.
At the initial junction of the sounds i and u there are the two sandhi letters;

children.text: eo iti praveśe tu aiau iti dvayaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: in entry they know them as e and o, but also as the pair ai and au.
In entry, the six ṭha-class phonemes belong to the dvādaśānta and the forehead,
and at the throat and heart; bindu and visarga stand on the two sides.
The pentad beginning with ka is always taught as being within the first phoneme.
Thus, within the phonemes together with their stations, there is that continuous series together with the phonemes.
In the heart this sa, whose form is prāṇa, has the nature of life.
Bindu is illumination, and the h-phoneme stands as having the nature of filling.
This supreme rise has been stated; the subtle rise of the phonemes is now explained.
In entry, when there is orientation toward the sixteen, the suns are those excluding the six ṭha phonemes.
The remaining phonemes are just the lunar and solar measures; this is the subtle rise.
Time is said to be the half-mātrā of the thirty-three phonemes beginning with ka.

children.text: mātrā hrasvāḥ pañca dīrghāṣṭakaṃ dvistriḥ plutaṃ tu ﾱ
children.translated_text: The short vowels are one mātrā; the eight long vowels are double, and the pluta is triple; the text is corrupt here.
Our guru taught this as eighty-one half-mātrās.
By its power the Blessed One declared the mantra of eighty-one units.
The goddess <s>Śakti</s>, consisting of eighty-one padas, is proclaimed as having <s>Śiva</s> as her self.
So too in the venerable <s>Mātaṅga</s>, since <s>Śiva</s> is of the nature of the aggregate of dharmas,
therefore, in each corresponding way, the Lord, master of the wheel of reflective-awareness power,
is contemplated through gross recitations and reflections consisting of eighty-one padas.
For exactly as far as a single reflective awareness is completed,
so far is that called a pada by us, not constrained by the rule of nominal and verbal endings.
Expanded by the sequence of the exalted vimarśa of eighty-one padas,
the gross means is also the supreme means; this dissolution is made of mātrās.

children.text: ardhamātrā nava nava syuścaturṣu caturṣu yat ||
children.translated_text: Since there are nine half-mātrās in each set of four
aṅgulas, there is the emergence of thirty-six and of the eighty-one padas.
When an aṅgula is divided into nine parts, there are ninth-portions.
There are four mātrās, less by a half-mātrā; the other three are double, quadruple, and sixfold.
Thus the short measure goes through two sets of four aperture-parts of an aṅgula.
The long and pluta are respectively two and three times that; after that, even a consonant has a half.
The letter kṣa has the nature of one and a half mātrās, as a mātrikā together with its interval.
When its repose is reckoned as a half-mātrā,
then, in half an aṅgula divided into seven parts, there was again formerly a half-mātrā.
But the letter kṣa, whose nature is the grasping of all conjunctions, is all-pervading,
sharing in the rise at the beginning, end, and junctions of all phonemes.
In this way, in the thirty-sixfold movement, the rise of the phonemes occurs in relation to the result;
for fierce and gentle effects, in reverse order, from ha down to the final a.
The sound a is in the heart and ha is in the dvādaśānta; they know this as
the non-dual reality whose essence is aham, a repose whose nature is illumination.
Because <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> are undivided, this series consists of eighty-one mātrās.
It circulates through seventy-two aṅgulas by doubling.
The subtle rise has been taught in three ways, and the supreme rise in two ways.
Now the gross rise of the phonemes is stated as taught by the guru.
With each half-prahara in the day, the rise of the eight classes occurs.

children.text: rātrau ca hrāsavṛddhyatra kecidāhurna ke 'pi tu ||
children.translated_text: At night, some say that there is decrease and increase here, while others do not.

children.text: eṣa vargodayo rātrau divā cāpy ardhayāmagaḥ
children.translated_text: This rise of the classes, at night and also by day, proceeds by half-yāmas.
That amounts to one thousand three hundred and fifty breaths.
Thus the transition in each class, by day and by night, is one and a half.
When they are taken together, the rise consists of twenty-seven hundreds of movements.

children.text: nava vargāṃstu ye prāhusteṣāṃ prāṇaśatī ravīn
children.translated_text: For those who state that there are nine classes, a hundred and twelve breaths
and one third are said to be the transition in each class.
When these are taken together over day and night, the total is twenty-four hundreds.
This is the gross rise of the classes; now the rise of individual phonemes is explained.
For each phoneme there are two hundred and sixteen breaths.
Externally there are thirty-six caṣakas in the day, and likewise at night.
There, one hundred and eight is raudra, and the next is śākta;
when the condition of the yamala is joined, there is non-separation of <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.
When day and night are not divided, the breath-movements are expressed by the numbers two, three, four, and five,
and there is a nāḍī with a fifth part; this is remembered as the external rise of the phonemes.
Thus this fiftyfold account of the phonemes has been fully discussed.
But for those who call it one less, we shall explain their view.
There are four movements, less by one fifth, and a half-movement for each single
phoneme as an addition; when day and night are undivided, that is doubled.

children.text: sthūlo varṇodayaḥ so 'yaṃ purā sūkṣmo nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: This is the gross rise of the phonemes; previously the subtle rise was described.
Thus the principle of time has been taught, established by scripture, tradition, and direct experience.
Now this most secret emergence of the cakras is explained.
Thus what is born without effort has been explained; what is born from effort is now stated.
Everything, consisting of bīja and piṇḍa, establishes the vibrating nature of consciousness
within the supreme consciousness; this has been described as the means.
Just as the carrying motion of the streams of water-pot mechanisms at the rim of a waterwheel,
through the effort of a single sustained attention, would display a varied mechanical emergence,
so too, by the power of a single sustained attention, when the rise of mantra has arisen constantly,
the deity of that mantra, through effort, becomes gracious in identity with it.
In the daily rise of a one-unit piṇḍa it is twenty-one thousand six hundred; in a twofold piṇḍaka it is half of that.
In the threefold case the rise is considered to be seven thousand two hundred.

children.text: catuṣke tu sahasrāṇi pañca caiva catuḥśatī ||
children.translated_text: In the fourfold case it is five thousand four hundred,
and in the five-phoneme case it is four thousand three hundred and twenty.
In the sixfold set, the <s>udaya</s> (rise) would be three thousand and six hundred.
In the sevenfold set it is remembered as three thousand plus eighty-six;
but when configured as eight syllables, it is twenty-seven hundreds.
In nine-syllable forms the rise would be twenty-four hundreds;
in the ten-syllable form, it is twenty-one hundreds with sixty added.
In the <s>Śiva</s>-syllabled form it is eighteen hundred and sixty-four;
in the twelve-syllable form, the rise is eighteen hundreds.
In the thirteen-syllable form, indeed, it is sixteen hundreds with sixty-two added;
in the bhuvana-syllabled form it is fifteen hundreds with forty-three added.
In the fifteen-syllable form it is fourteen hundred and forty;
in the sixteen-syllable form it is said to be thirteen hundred and a half-hundred.
In the seventeen-syllable form it is twelve hundreds with seventy-one added;
in the eighteen-syllable form it should be known by the wise as twelve hundreds.
In the cakra numbered twenty-four, it would be nine hundreds;
in that numbered twenty-seven, the rise has the nature of eight hundreds.
In the great cakra of thirty-two, it is six hundreds plus seventy-five;
in the twice-twenty-four cakra, one should observe a rise of four hundreds and a half-hundred,
for the knower of <s>piṇḍayoga</s> should mark the rise among the piṇḍa-mantras.
In the fifty-fourfold cakra it is four hundreds;
in the eight-times-eight cakra it should be three hundred, with thirty-seven and a half added.
There would be two hundred and sixty-six, together with a half and a third of a half.
In the cakra of eighty-one padas, the rise moves through <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);

children.text: cakre tu ṣaṇṇavatyākhye sapādā dviśatī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: in the cakra called ninety-six, it would be two hundred with a quarter added.
In the cakra of one hundred and eight, the rise is two hundreds.
When this cakra, in this sequence, is doubled six times,
and when, beyond that, it is doubled again, there is one unit, one and a half, and half of an eighth part.
Beyond that, by those skilled in subtle calculation, through divisions beginning with halves of halves,
a subtle movement is discerned by establishing the divisions in sixteenth parts.
Thus, for the yogin whose movement of <s>prāṇa</s> has been blocked by effort,
there gradually arises an actual swallowing of the movement of <s>prāṇa</s>.
When the state of contracting time has been attained through the sequence of swallowing <s>prāṇa</s>,
consciousness alone becomes full, because distinctions among cognitions have been cast off.
For, when there is no new arising of the movement of <s>prāṇa</s>,
no difference of cognition produced by difference of time is conceived.
Cognition is not made different by differences among knowable objects, as in the case of an activity on a mountain peak.

children.text: kālastu bhedakastasya sa tu sūkṣmaḥ kṣaṇo mataḥ
children.translated_text: Rather, time is what differentiates it, and that is held to be a subtle instant.
And the limit of subtlety is this: as long as cognition remains, that is an instant.

children.text: anyathā na sa nirvaktuṃ nipuṇairapi pāryate
children.translated_text: Otherwise it cannot be defined even by the very skilled.
For as long as cognition lasts, its absence does not appear.
And that absence is not present so long as, in that pathway of the senses,
whether with regard to an object or to a region of the self, there is no separation from contact.
If that separation does arise as constituted by <s>spanda</s> (vibration), it certainly belongs to that <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: bhavedeva tataḥ prāṇaspandābhāve na sā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the absence of the vibration of <s>prāṇa</s>, that separation would not occur.

children.text: tadabhāvānna vijñānābhāvaḥ saivaṃ tu saiva dhīḥ
children.translated_text: From its absence, the absence of cognition does not follow; in this way that same awareness is just that same awareness.
Nor is it really extended, since temporal difference has been cast off.

children.text: vastuto hyata eveyaṃ kālaṃ saṃvinna saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: For precisely for this reason, in reality, this consciousness does not touch time.
Therefore there is one consciousness, though it apprehends manifold forms in various ways;
even while non-conceptual, it is <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual determination) within the field of entities.
So long as another <s>spanda</s> has not arisen, so long does that one remain.
A single <s>vikalpa</s> would be just that much, constructing a manifold object.

children.text: ye tvitthaṃ na vidusteṣāṃ vikalpo nopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: But for those who do not know this in this way, <s>vikalpa</s> cannot be established.

children.text: sa hyeko na bhavetkaścit trijagatyapi jātucit
children.translated_text: For no single one would ever exist anywhere in the three worlds.
Cognition tinged by a word is indeed called <s>vikalpa</s>.

children.text: sā ca syātkramikaivetthaṃ kiṃ kathaṃ ko vikalpayet
children.translated_text: And that tinging would be sequential in this way; who, then, would conceptualize what, and how?

children.text: ghaṭa ityapi neyānsyādvikalpaḥ kā kathā sthitau ||
children.translated_text: Even the cognition 'pot' would not be such a <s>vikalpa</s>; what need is there to speak of a stable state?
And there is no <s>vikalpa</s> at all that rests in a mere instant alone.
Nor is there an aggregate of cognitions, because they do not exist simultaneously.
Therefore, for them, this practical usage born of <s>vikalpa</s> is simply incoherent.
Therefore, so long as another <s>spanda</s> does not arise, that one single
cognition may touch even the categories of properties whose nature is <s>vikalpa</s>.
Therefore, consisting of reflective awareness of the noble <s>śakti</s> (power) of the eighty-one-pada form,
<s>vikalpa</s>, which bestows the state of <s>Śiva</s>, has already been explained before.
Just as the thought 'I move my ears' becomes effective through effort,
so too, through effort connected with movement in a cakra and the like, awareness itself belongs to that cakra.
Therefore there is a rule of equivalence with <s>prāṇa</s> for japa, homa, worship, and the rest.
In the <s>Siddhāmata</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalinīśakti</s> is equal to <s>prāṇa</s> and is <s>Unmanā</s>.
And this was said by the supreme Lord in the <s>Yoginīkaula</s>:
'In the cakra of the word, mantra, and syllable, the division that reaches the principle of <s>śakti</s>,
having made it among the words, the knower of mantra becomes a recipient of the fruit in japa and the like.
He should omit the rise counted as two, three, seven, and eight, and the hundredfold rise.'

children.text: iti śaktisthitā mantrā vidyā vā cakranāyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus mantras that abide in <s>śakti</s>, or vidyās that are lords of cakras,
should always be known and applied, dear one, in the form of pada and piṇḍa.
In the great principle of constant rise, in <s>Sadāśiva</s> established in rise,

children.text: ayuktāḥ śaktimārge tu na japtāścodayena ye
children.translated_text: those that are not joined to the path of <s>śakti</s> and are not recited with rise,

children.text: te na sidhyanti yatnena japtāḥ koṭiśatairapi ||
children.translated_text: do not attain success through effort, even if recited hundreds of crores of times.
In all garland-mantras, mental japa is prescribed,
or else low-voiced japa; one should not imagine their rise of <s>śakti</s>.
In all word-mantras, as long as it reaches the power of that word,
It can be continually recited, to that extent, by practitioners who are properly disciplined.

children.text: tāvatī teṣu vai saṃkhyā padeṣu padasaṃjñitā
children.translated_text: That same number, among the units called <s>pada</s> (word or step), is designated as the number of <s>padas</s>.
Having produced that many risings, beginning with the statement of the three <s>padas</s>, in sequence,

children.text: dvādaśākhye dvādaśite cakre sārdhaṃ śataṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: in the twelve-spoked wheel, divided by twelve, there would be one hundred and fifty.
That rise, however, would be one hundred and forty-four.
In the sixteen-spoked wheel, divided by twelve, there are one hundred and ninety-two.
Together with half the course, it is said to be one hundred and twelve.
In the sixteen-spoked wheel, divided by sixteen, the rise would reach eighty-four.
That rise is two hundred and fifty-six.
The wise say that here three eighth-parts of the course are additional.
In the eight-by-eight wheel, divided by twelve, there are a half-quarter, twenty, and eight.

children.text: udayaḥ saptaśatikā sāṣṭā ṣaṣṭiryato hi saḥ
children.translated_text: The rise is seven hundred and sixty-eight, for that is its measure.
This <s>cakrodaya</s> (rise of the wheel) has been taught as beneficial to practitioners.
Restraining the mental activities and coming to rest in the wheel,
for as long as one rests after emerging, that indeed is this rise of the course.
But in the full total rise here, entry, oneness in rest, and emergence

children.text: traya ityata evoktaḥ siddhau madhyodayo varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the three; therefore the middle rise is said to be best for accomplishment.
The groups of <s>mantra</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, and <s>cakra</s>, freed from the initial and final rises
and joined with the middle rise, surely become sharers in accomplishment.
The one who knows the rise of the <s>mantra-cakra</s> and understands the purpose of the rise of the <s>vidyā-cakra</s>
quickly attains accomplishment; so it is taught in the glorious <s>Dviṃśatikā</s> of the <s>Trika</s>.
With two, three, or four measures, either the <s>vidyā</s> or the <s>cakra</s>
one should always recite separately, joined with the rise of the <s>tattvas</s>.
One should recite each mantra by mass, syllable, and word, reaching the <s>Śakti</s> tattva.

children.text: bahvakṣarastu yo mantro vidyā vā cakrameva vā ||
children.translated_text: But a mantra that has many syllables, or a <s>vidyā</s>, or a <s>cakra</s>,
is not to be placed there simply in <s>Śakti</s>; rather, the division ends with <s>oṃ namaḥ</s>.
Therefore, in this rise of the <s>tattvas</s>, the day and night are divided thirty by thirty.
And that division is again divided thirty by thirty.
But when, after resting in the prior rise, it flares forth through the second,
and enters by the conjunction increased by a half, then what is called the half-rise occurs.

children.text: yadā pūrṇodayātmā tu samaḥ kālastrike sphuret ||
children.translated_text: But when time, whose nature is full rise, shines equally in the <s>Trika</s>,
in entry, rest, and expansion, then there is a rise in its own three portions.
Thus this power of time is established in <s>prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: sa spade khe sa taccityāṃ tenāsyāṃ viśvaniṣṭhitiḥ
children.translated_text: It is in contact, in space, and in that consciousness; therefore the stability of the universe is in this.
Therefore, because the dissolution and arising of the universe have consciousness as their foundation,
at the end of <s>Śakti</s> on the path, its vibrations are in truth beyond number.
It is said in the glorious <s>Mālinītantra</s>: wherever in the body
a transformation should arise, that <s>tattva</s> is the supreme <s>tattva</s>.
Time is established in <s>prāṇa</s>, and the body is pervaded by it.
Therefore the form of this time, established in the body, is described.
The final grossness of the vibrations of consciousness and the movements of <s>prāṇa</s> is the hollow channel.
Having assumed the form of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (subtle channels), it extends this body.
For this reason it is said in the glorious <s>Svacchanda</s>: just as a leaf is pervaded by its own fibers,
so the body is pervaded by <s>nāḍīs</s>, in the mode of channels at every opening.
Extending upward from the big toe to the <s>Brahmakuṇḍalikā</s>,
all time here is contained within just eighty-four finger-breadths.
They know a somewhat subtle condition of time extending as far as the <s>dvādaśānta</s>.
At ninety-six below, and by the sequence of six and two, it becomes one hundred and eight.
Here, within the rise and dissolution of <s>prāṇa</s> moving in the middle,
are all the creations and dissolutions, varied according to the sequence within the winds.
Thus this <s>cakrodaya</s>, to be cultivated through subtle reflection, has been stated by me from the perspective of the scripture of experience.
Now, through contraction and expansion of the spatial <s>adhvan</s> (path), this method seen in the scripture of <s>Śiva</s> is set forth.
This temporal <s>adhvan</s>, consisting of the Lord's power of action, has been examined.
Now the spatial <s>adhvan</s>, born from and consisting of the variety of forms, is described.
This entire <s>adhvan</s> is established in consciousness alone.
Whatever does not rest there becomes like a flower in the sky.

children.text: saṃviddvāreṇa tatsṛṣṭe śūnye dhiyi marutsu ca
children.translated_text: Through the doorway of consciousness, in the void, in the intellect, and in the winds created from it,
in the wheel of <s>nāḍīs</s> and its sub-wheels, and in the external body, there is the establishment of the <s>adhvan</s>.
There this <s>adhvan</s> should be described in this way, because
the yogin, simply following the sequence of its procedure, quickly becomes <s>Bhairava</s>.
When, merely through the wish to see, he pervades all objects and remains established,
then what need is there of saying much? So it is stated in the <s>Spanda</s> scripture.
Having known the entire <s>adhvan</s>, he should dissolve it into its lords.
He should melt those lords, in sequence as before, into the wheel of body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and mind.
He should dissolve all that into his own consciousness; that consciousness is by nature full.
When worshiped, it is the fire that consumes the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And in the glorious <s>Mahīkṣottara</s>, the guru taught these lords of the <s>adhvan</s>:
<s>Brahmā</s> governs from <s>Ananta</s> up to <s>Pradhāna</s>; <s>Viṣṇu</s> governs from <s>Puruṣa</s> up to <s>Kalā</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> is in the knot and in <s>Māyā</s>; <s>Īśa</s> is in the sphere called <s>Sadākhya</s>.
Beyond that is <s>Śiva</s>, unsupported; the pervaded is below, and the supreme is its pervader.
Thinking, "Thus it has attained <s>Śiva</s>-hood," it was described in this way.
Knowledge is not dependent on procedure; so it is said in the <s>Svacchanda</s> scripture.
In the <s>Triśiraḥ</s> scripture, awakening is imagined as root, middle, and summit.
The construction of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> is memory, a conceptualization of difference.
The unobstructed division, the state of "I am," is the root that leads to awakening.
This entire condition of the <s>tattvas</s> is without division in one's own self alone.
The middle of consciousness becomes something characterized by support and supported,
characterized by the abiding of its own nature through division according to the distinctions of the <s>tattvas</s>.
But the summit of consciousness is awakened consciousness, waveless, a vast bliss,
in which the states of elements, beings, cities, and the like have been brought into unity with consciousness.
<s>Bhairava</s>, the supreme Lord, is uninterrupted consciousness.
And in the <s>Śrīdevyāyāmala</s> it is said:
"Meditating on the sixfold <s>adhvan</s>, beautiful with the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>, one at once becomes filled with <s>Śiva</s>."
Although this Lord is not separate from consciousness,
and, being complete, has in reality no arrangement of above, below, middle, beginning, or end,
nevertheless, for those who understand and for the one who teaches,
according to each one's own form there are conceptions such as middle, beginning, and the rest.
Therefore, because of the determining conception of the knower, they know the earthly
<s>tattva</s> as standing in every interval and covered by all the coverings.
Here, in that earthly <s>tattva</s>, the arrangement of worlds is described.
<s>Ananta</s>, leader of the <s>Kaṭāha</s> Rudras and of those devoted to desire,
is mounted on a boat within the water, reeling from drinking liquor.

children.text: sa devaṃ bhairavaṃ dhyāyan nāgaiśca parivāritaḥ
children.translated_text: He meditates on the god <s>Bhairava</s> and is surrounded by <s>nāgas</s>.
Above is the world of <s>Kālāgni</s>, rising for a crore of yojanas.
From fear of reducing the worlds to ashes, he does not look upward.

children.text: sa ca vyāptāpi viśvasya yasmātpluṣyannimāṃ bhuvam ||
children.translated_text: And though he pervades the universe, since, while burning, he would scorch this earth,
he was formerly manifested below the hells; therefore he is regarded as beneath them.
The flame of the Lord extends for ten crores; above it, half that distance is void.
Above that, in sequence, are the lords of the hells, whose experience is nothing but suffering.

children.text: adho madhye tadūrdhve ca sthitā bhedāntarairvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They stand below, in the middle, and above, enclosed by further distinctions.
Among them in order are those called <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>, and <s>Raurava</s>.
They are eleven, eleven, and ten respectively; that is the internal reckoning called <s>śarāgni</s>.
For each of these, the height and the interval are one less than a crore.
Here the intervening extent is a lakh according to the number indicated by <s>kha-veda-āsya</s>.
Above is <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>; its lordship occupies a place one lakh less than a crore.
Those who, through conduct opposed to scripture, perform black deeds
are tormented there by terrible world-beings until the end of their experience.

children.text: ye sakṛdapi parameśaṃ śivamekāgreṇa cetasā śaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Those who even once go for refuge to the supreme Lord <s>Śiva</s> with one-pointed mind

children.text: yānti na te narakayujaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ teṣāṃ sukhālpatādāyi
children.translated_text: do not become connected with hell; for them the black deed gives only a small diminution of happiness.
Then, in sequence, comes the eightfold <s>pātāla</s>, each with a height of nine thousand and separated by one interval.
Each is one of the eight <s>pātālas</s>; in the eighth, <s>Hāṭaka</s> is the lord.
For each world <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, appointed to his own station, forcibly
grants many accomplishments; so it is in the venerable <s>Rauravaśāsana</s>.
Those observant initiates who stand in improper rites and perform forbidden conduct,

children.text: dīkṣitā api ye luptasamayā naca kurvate
children.translated_text: and those initiated persons who have abandoned the observances and do not perform
expiations, as well as those established there who denounce the left-hand practice,
and those in high positions who live from shares of the property and revenues of gods and sacred fires,
and those devoted to the service of other lower mantras, beginning with <s>Gāruḍa</s>,
are varied servants before the lord <s>Hāṭaka</s>.

children.text: te tu tatrāpi deveśaṃ bhaktyā cetparyupāsate ||
children.translated_text: But if even there they worship the Lord of gods with devotion,
they dissolve into the <s>tattva</s> of his lordship, and then, in sequence, into supreme <s>Śiva</s>.
But those who behave otherwise, whose selves are devoted to those enjoyments,
are reduced to pitiful cries by the heat of the fire of time.
They dissolve into the <s>guṇa-tattva</s>; then, again at the beginning of creation,
they are cast down by the Mothers, with a mass of dreadful torments going before them,
into the lowest of low bodies, in accordance with their own karma.
Among human births too, some knowers of mantra, in due sequence,
are liberated, while others are bound according to what they have done before.
Thus this account of the <s>gaṇas</s>, named <s>Hulahula</s> and the rest,
was taught by the Blessed One in the venerable <s>Ānandādhikaśāsana</s>.
Above the <s>pātālas</s>, the shell of the earth extends for twenty thousand.
But in the <s>Siddhātantra</s>, on the surface of <s>pātāla</s>, surrounded by <s>yakṣīs</s>,

children.text: bhadrakālyāḥ puraṃ yatra tābhiḥ krīḍanti sādhakāḥ
children.translated_text: there is the city of <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, where practitioners sport with them.
After that are darkness, heated earth, then void, and then serpents.
These are places of torment for those who corrupt the guru, mantra, and the like.

children.text: tato bhūmyūrdhvato meruḥ sahasrāṇi sa ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: Then, above the earth, is <s>Meru</s>, sixteen thousand
sunk down; that is the extent at its root, and its upward extent is twice that.
It is golden, eighty-four thousand high, and the abode of all the immortals.
It is rounded in the middle, above, and below, and square like a bowl.

children.text: bhairavīyaṃ ca talliṅgaṃ dharaṇī cāsya pīṭhikā ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Bhairava</s> liṅga, and the earth is its pedestal.

children.text: sarve devā nilīnā hi tatra tatpūjitaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: All the gods are dissolved there, and it is always worshipped by them.
In the middle is the assembly of <s>Dhātṛ</s> on <s>Meru</s>; in the direction of its lord is a standard.
The peak of the luminaries belongs to <s>Śambhu</s>; that lord is a portion of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.
Descending fourteen thousand from <s>Manovatī</s>,
the circular enclosure lies in the four directions; here on <s>Meru</s> are the guardians of the worlds.
<s>Amarāvatī</s>, belonging to <s>Indra</s>, is in the east; to its south
are the <s>apsarases</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, and <s>sādhyas</s>; to its north are the <s>Vināyakas</s>.

children.text: tejovatī svadiśyagneḥ purī tāṃ paścimena tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tejovatī</s> is the city in <s>Agni</s>'s own direction; to its west
are the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, and those who follow them in order.

children.text: yāmyāṃ saṃyamanī tāṃ tu paścimena kramāt sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the southern quarter is <s>Saṃyamanī</s>; to its west, in sequence, are stationed
<s>Mātṛnandā</s>, those counted as her own, Rudras, and their practitioners likewise.
<s>Kṛṣṇāṅgārā</s> and <s>Nirṛti</s> are there, and to its east are the <s>Piśācakas</s>.
To her north, one after another farther north, are the <s>Rakṣasas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s>;
and <s>Vāruṇī</s>, called <s>Śuddhavatī</s>; to her south is the host of <s>bhūtas</s>.
To the north, farther north of this one, are the <s>Vasus</s> and <s>Vidyādharas</s> in sequence;
and to the south of the <s>Gandhavatī</s> of <s>Vāyu</s> are the <s>Kinnaras</s> again.
The goddess <s>Vīṇāsarasvatī</s>, and <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Tumburu</s> as well,
are the secret ones of <s>Mahodaya</s> and <s>Indu</s>; to her west, again in succession,
are <s>Kubera</s>, the <s>Karmadevas</s>, and likewise their practitioners too.
<s>Yaśasvinī</s> belongs to <s>Maheśa</s>; to her west is <s>Hari</s>.
To the south, farther south, are <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, and <s>Dhanvantari</s> in order.
In this <s>Mairava</s> encircling range, the principal ones are thus eightfold in front.
Others, situated in the intervals, are again remembered as twenty-six.

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtaratāḥ puṇye varṣe ye bhārate narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those men in the holy land of <s>Bhārata</s> who are devoted to <s>iṣṭāpūrta</s> (sacrificial and charitable works),

children.text: te merugāḥ sakṛcchambhuṃ ye vārcanti yathocitam
children.translated_text: or who worship <s>Śambhu</s> properly even once, go to <s>Meru</s>.
And in the northern quarters around the circuit of <s>Meru</s> are the buttressing mountains:
<s>Mandara</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>, <s>Vipula</s>, and then <s>Supārśvaka</s>.
White, yellow, blue, and red, they are the foot-mountains in order.
Supporting the earth by means of these, <s>Meru</s> stands immovable.
They call the forests <s>Caitraratha</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Vaibhrāja</s>, and <s>Pitṛvana</s>.
And the four lakes are <s>Raktoda</s>, <s>Mānasa</s>, <s>Sita</s>, and <s>Bhadra</s>.
The trees are <s>Kadamba</s>, <s>Jambu</s>, <s>Aśvattha</s>, and <s>Nyagrodha</s>, in order.

children.text: eṣu ca caturṣvacaleṣu trayaṃ trayaṃ kramaśa etadāmnātam
children.translated_text: And on these four mountains, three of each of these are taught in sequence.
Below <s>Meru</s>, as far as the salt ocean, <s>Jambudvīpa</s> extends on all sides.
Measuring one lakh, it has become ninefold through boundary mountains.
<s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himavān</s> are the three to the south.
Their measures are one lakh, ninety thousand, and eighty thousand in order.
<s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Triśṛṅga</s> again have the same extents on the left side.
These six boundary mountains of <s>Meru</s> extend from east to west.
To the east is <s>Mālyavān</s>; to the west is the one named <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
Those two extend to the left and north, and are thirty-four thousand each.

children.text: aṣṭāvete tato 'pyanyau dvau dvau pūrvādiṣu kramāt ||
children.translated_text: These are the eight; and beyond them are two more in each of the eastern and other directions, in sequence:
<s>Jāṭhara</s>, <s>Kūṭa</s>, <s>Himavat</s>, <s>Yātrajāru</s>, <s>Rudhi</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgin</s>.
With the arrangement standing thus, the division here is set forth for establishing the <s>varṣas</s> (regions).
All around, below the <s>Cakravāṭa</s>, square and without sun or moon,
is the region called <s>Ilā</s>, nine thousand broad, with a lifespan of three myriads.
West of <s>Meru</s> is that <s>Gandhamādana</s>; west of it
is <s>Ketumāla</s>, adorned with a set of seven family-mountains.
East of <s>Meru</s> is <s>Mālyavān</s>; east of it is <s>Bhadrāśva</s>,
with a lifespan of ten thousand, and with five family-mountains.
From the east, from the west, and from the left and north respectively, these
are described as thirty-two and thirty-four thousand.
North of <s>Meru</s> is <s>Śṛṅgavān</s>; outside it is the <s>Kuruvarṣa</s>,
bow-shaped, nine thousand broad; life there is thirteen thousand.
North of <s>Kuruvarṣa</s>, and then in the northwestern ocean, in order,

children.text: daśa ceti sahasrāṇi dvīpau candro 'tha bhadrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the two islands <s>Candra</s> and <s>Bhadraka</s>, measuring five and ten thousand.
Between <s>Śveta</s> and <s>Śṛṅgin</s>, to the left of <s>Meru</s>, is <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>.
Its extent is nine thousand, and its lifespan is twelve and a half thousand.
There, to the left, between <s>Śveta</s> and <s>Nīla</s>, is <s>Ramyaka</s>.
It is nine thousand broad, and its lifespan is twelve thousand.
To the south of <s>Meru</s> are <s>Hemakūṭa</s> and <s>Niṣadha</s>; between those two
is the land called <s>Hari</s>, nine thousand broad, with life a thousand more than that.
There too, to the south, between the pair <s>Hemakūṭa</s> and <s>Himavat</s>,
is <s>Kainnara</s>, nine thousand broad, with life a thousand more than that.
There too, south of <s>Meru</s>, south of <s>Himavān</s>,
is <s>Bhārata</s>, nine thousand broad, bow-shaped, the land of action and experience.
<s>Ilāvṛta</s>, <s>Ketumāla</s>, <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, <s>Kuru</s>, <s>Hiraṇya</s>, and <s>Ramyaka</s>,
and the <s>Hari</s> and <s>Kinnara</s> regions are lands of enjoyment, not lands of action.
Here, for the most part, there is the condition of being a land of action; yet even here, for beings without action,
animals have karmic impressions, because such firm impressions have been formed.
Even beings without such impressions can arise in <s>Bhārata</s> and elsewhere too,
through firm former impressions and by the Lord's will, as auspicious or inauspicious.
In another place too there is karma; and this is seen in ancient tradition.

children.text: tatra tretā sadā kālo bhārate tu caturyugam ||
children.translated_text: There the time is always the <s>Tretā</s> age; in <s>Bhārata</s>, however, there is the cycle of four yugas.
In <s>Bhārata</s> there are nine divisions, and here by the oceanic water
land is divided as five hundred, and water likewise.
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Kaśeru</s>, <s>Tāmrābha</s>, <s>Nāgīya</s>, and eastward <s>Gabhastimān</s>,
<s>Saumya</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Vārāha</s>, and the one called <s>Kanyā</s>, excluding the ocean.
And in the ninth, <s>Kanyādvīpa</s>, to the south, situated in the middle of the ocean,
there are six subsidiary islands, adorned with a set of seven family-mountains.
<s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Yava</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, and <s>Varāha</s>, and <s>Agastya</s> dwelling on <s>Malaya</s>,

children.text: tatraiva ca trikūṭe laṅkā ṣaḍamī hyupadvīpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and right there on <s>Trikūṭa</s>, <s>Laṅkā</s>: these six indeed are the subsidiary islands.
The peoples dwelling in the islands and subsidiary islands are mostly various kinds of <s>mlecchas</s>.
They are rich in pearls, gold, and jewels: so it is in the holy <s>Ruruśāsana</s>.
Whatever karma is done in <s>Bhārata</s>, or is exhausted, from <s>Avīci</s>

children.text: śivāntaṃ tena muktirvā kanyākhye tu viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: up to <s>Śiva</s>, by that there may be liberation, especially in the land called <s>Kanyā</s>.
The crore of <s>Rudras</s> beginning with <s>Mahākāla</s> is here itself in <s>Bhārata</s>;
and the five hundred beginning with <s>Gaṅgā</s> are here. Therefore birth here is hard to obtain.
In other <s>varṣas</s>, karma is carried through by enjoyment like that of animals,
but for those born in <s>Bhārata</s> there is something to be attained even beyond desire.
Since in <s>Kanyādvīpa</s> there is diversity in the pleasures and pains of the varied practices of the different colors and life-stages,
for that reason this is the highest <s>karmabhūmi</s> (land of action).
Here, they say, for men performing white and black deeds,
the higher and lower states, heaven and hell, come to perfection: so it is in the <s>Raurava-vārttika</s>.

children.text: evaṃ meroradho jambūrabhito yaḥ sa vistarāt
children.translated_text: Thus, below <s>Meru</s>, the <s>Jambū</s> region surrounding it
is seventeenfold in full extent, but in summary it is ninefold by its divisions.
<s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s> had ten sons; three of them
renounced the world, and then there was the king named <s>Agnīdhra</s> in the land called <s>Jambū</s>.
He had nine sons; therefore this land has nine divisions.
<s>Nābhi</s> was his ninth son, and his grandson was <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Ṛṣabha</s>.
His eight sons, together with his daughter, formed the ninth share;
because they enjoyed them, the land measuring a hundred thousand yojanas became divided ninefold.
The salt ocean measures one hundred thousand yojanas; outside it, in front of this land, are mountains:
<s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Dundubhi</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, <s>Kaṅka</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and <s>Indu</s> to the north,
<s>Varāha</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, and <s>Aśoka</s> to the west, together with <s>Saha</s> and <s>Balāhaka</s>,
and to the south <s>Cakra</s> and <s>Maināka</s>; the submarine fire <s>Vāḍava</s> stands between those two.
South of the ocean, after crossing two thousand yojanas, there is a mountain,
<s>Vidyutvān</s>, three thousand yojanas high and long; here live fruit-eaters,
smeared with dirt, with long hair and beards, having the nature of cattle,
naked, living for eighty years, and feeding on grass.
There the doors are always without barriers for the attainment of the subterranean caverns;
this has been sung by the teachers in the venerable <s>Rauravaśāsana</s>.
Thus this salt ocean has been set forth.
Outside it are these six <s>dvīpas</s>, each surrounded by its own ocean.
They are doubled successively and are ruled by six sons of <s>Manu</s>.
The six <s>dvīpas</s> are called <s>Śāka</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śalmali</s>, <s>Gomedha</s>, and <s>Abja</s>.
The six oceans are those of milk, curds, ghee, sugar-cane juice, wine, and sweet water.
The kings are <s>Medhātithi</s>, <s>Vapuṣmān</s>, <s>Jyotiṣmān</s>, <s>Dyutimat</s>, <s>Havī</s>,

children.text: saṃvara iti śākādiṣu jambudvīpe nyarūpi cāgnīdhraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Saṃvara</s> in <s>Śāka</s> and the other islands; and <s>Agnīdhra</s> was described in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.
The five beginning with <s>Śāka</s> are imagined as having seven mountains and the same number of divisions.
The one named <s>Puṣkara</s> is two-petalled; <s>Hari</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Indu</s> are here in the east and the other directions.
Fifty-three lakhs, two crores, and five ayutas:
this is the measure in yojanas from half of <s>Meru</s> to the end of the sweet ocean.
Outside the seventh ocean is the golden land, ten crores and then a lakh;
the mountain beyond the world is said to be a lakh in height and ten thousand in breadth.
Eight <s>Rudras</s>, together with the lords of the worlds, stand in the eight directions of <s>Lokāloka</s>.
Some say only this much; the sun is within <s>Lokāloka</s> and not outside it.
The paths of the ancestors and gods run northward and southward from it, as the two courses belonging to their own and the other class;
they call this the sun's two courses, the northern and the southern progress.
For all beings <s>Meru</s> is the north and <s>Lokāloka</s> the south;
one should understand the sunrise and sunset of the sun in this way.
When it is midnight in <s>Amarāvatī</s> and sunset in the southern city,
midday is remembered in the western city, and sunrise in the northern city.
The sunrise that takes place in <s>Amarāvatī</s> is midnight in the abode of <s>Yama</s>;

children.text: ke 'staṃ saumye ca madhyāhna itthaṃ sūryagatāgate ||
children.translated_text: in the northern city it is sunset, and elsewhere midday: so it is with the sun's going and coming.
Beyond the world-mountain there is darkness numbering thirty-five crores,
nineteen lakhs and forty thousand.
The royal ocean called <s>Garbhoda</s> has the measure of the seven oceans;
it is beyond <s>Lokāloka</s>, and in its womb the whole earth rests.
In the <s>Siddhātantra</s>, on the shore of the womb-ocean, there is said to be
a maṇḍala called <s>Kauśeya</s>; there <s>Garuḍa</s> is surrounded by perfected winged beings.

children.text: krīḍanti parvatāgre te nava cātra kulādrayaḥ
children.translated_text: They sport on the summit of the mountain; and here there are nine clan-mountains.
Then there are thirty hot-water rivers, and after that rivers going to <s>Pātāla</s>.
In the four directions is the <s>Naimira</s> garden, always frequented by yoginīs;

children.text: tato merustato nāgā meghā hemāṇḍakaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then comes <s>Meru</s>, then the serpents, then the clouds, and after that the golden egg.
With the shell of <s>Brahmā</s>'s egg, and with half of <s>Meru</s>,
there are fifty crores in the ten directions; this is called <s>Bhūrloka</s>.
This <s>Bhūrloka</s> is pervaded by six kinds: domestic animals, birds, wild beasts, trees, human beings, and reptiles,
and by piśācas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and yakṣas as well,

children.text: vidyābhṛtāṃ ca kiṃ vā bahunā sarvasya bhūtasargasya
children.translated_text: and also by vidyādharas; in short, for the whole creation of beings,
it is, according to their own conception and as they wish, a place of enjoyment and residence.
Likewise <s>Bhuvarloka</s> extends one lakh from the sun; within it
are ten wind-paths, each separated by ten thousand yojanas.
There the first wind-path is described as being spread out;
fifty yojanas above is the wind named <s>Ṛtarddhi</s>.

children.text: āpyāyakaḥ sa jantūnāṃ tataḥ prācetaso bhavet
children.translated_text: It nourishes living beings; above that is <s>Prācetasa</s>,
fifty yojanas higher, and above that again by one hundred.
Here is the <s>Senānī</s> wind; these are mute clouds that release lightning,
standing only a krośa above the earth and raining water.
One hundred yojanas above them are clouds that rain frogs and other living creatures;
fifty above is <s>Ogha</s>, where clouds rain poisonous water.
There are other clouds born of <s>Skanda</s>, and piśācas in the <s>Ogha</s> wind;
then fifty yojanas higher are clouds called <s>Māraka</s>.
There, in that station, are the <s>Vināyakas</s>, born from <s>Mahādeva</s>,
who take away the karma performed by men whose selves are not perfected.
Fifty above that is the wind called <s>Vajrāṅka</s>; there are hail-clouds here,
and the lower <s>Vidyādharas</s> are established here in <s>Vajrāṅka</s>.
Those who die in rites of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>pauruṣa</s>, and in practices carried out in cremation grounds and the like,
being accomplished through those siddhis, are situated in the wind-region <s>Vajrāṅka</s>.
Fifty above <s>Vajrāṅka</s> is <s>Vaidyuta</s>, with clouds that rain thunderbolts,

children.text: abdā apsarasaścātra ye ca puṇyakṛto narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and here are <s>apsarases</s> and men who have performed meritorious acts.

children.text: bhṛgau vahnau jale ye ca saṃgrāme cānivartinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who die from a precipice, in fire, in water, or without turning back in battle,

children.text: gograhe vadhyamokṣe vā mṛtāste vaidyute sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or in a cattle-raid or while freeing one condemned to death, are situated in <s>Vaidyuta</s>.
From <s>Vaidyuta</s> to <s>Raivata</s> is the same extent; there are clouds that carry nourishment,
and above are disease-raining clouds; the <s>Saṃvartas</s> come immediately after that.
Those perfected by rocanā, collyrium, ashes, and the like are there in <s>Raivata</s> itself.
The place of the wrath-water clouds is <s>Viṣāvarta</s>; that is a wind-region.
Fifty above that same place are fire-born storm-clouds,
special <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and also those who always worship <s>Parameśvara</s>
with <s>Gāndharva</s> music; they are then situated in <s>Viṣāvarta</s>.
A hundred above <s>Viṣāvarta</s> is <s>Durjaya</s>, born from breath.
Here stand the clouds of <s>Brahmā</s>, which generate wind at the dissolution,
and the <s>Puṣkara</s> clouds moving in the wind, and <s>Gandharvas</s> in <s>Parāvaha</s>.
There are clouds called <s>Jīmūta</s>, and also the highest <s>Vidyādharas</s>.

children.text: ye ca rūpavratā lokā āvahe te pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those worlds whose vow is form are established in <s>Āvaha</s>.
In <s>Mahāvaha</s> are clouds made by <s>Īśa</s>, beneficial to creatures.
In <s>Mahāparivaha</s> are clouds arisen from the skull of the great Lord.
This wind-path, ending with <s>Mahāparivaha</s>, lies before <s>Ṛtarddhi</s>.
The daughters of <s>Agni</s> and the Mothers are presided over by <s>Rudra</s>'s <s>śakti</s>.
In the second, beyond that, are perfected beings and <s>Cāraṇas</s>, born from their own karma.
In the fourth are the eight divine weapons, and again in the fifth the elephants of the quarters.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe garutmān anyasmin gaṅgānyatra vṛṣo vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: In the sixth is <s>Garutmān</s>; elsewhere is <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and elsewhere the mighty bull.
In the ninth, <s>Dakṣa</s> is firmly established by the <s>śakti</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>.
In the tenth are the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and <s>Ādityas</s> in the wind-path.
The form of the sun, its orb, extends nine thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
That threefold <s>jñānaśakti</s> shines as the sun belonging to the Lord.
<s>Svarloka</s> is defined as extending from <s>Bhuvarloka</s> up to <s>Dhruva</s>.
A lakh above the sun is the moon; that is <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>kriyāśakti</s>.
A lakh above the moon is the lunar mansion; from there, by two lakhs,
they know the five, each one separately, from <s>Bhauma</s> to the son of the Sun.
A lakh above <s>Saura</s> is the group of the Seven Seers, and above that likewise is <s>Dhruva</s>.
<s>Dhruva</s>, unmoving in the station of <s>Brahmā</s>, is <s>Brahmā</s> himself in another form.
Having become the pivot of all aerial vehicles, <s>Dhruva</s> stands above them all.
All these, fastened here, are nevertheless moved within the circle of wind.
In heaven there are principally seven masses of wind, beginning with <s>Āmegha</s>.
From here, those who perform sacrifices, oblations, and the like but are without knowledge
go to heaven; when that is exhausted, they go to the human world through the residue of merit.

children.text: evaṃ bhūmerdhruvāntaṃ syāllakṣāṇi daśa pañca ca
children.translated_text: Thus from the earth up to <s>Dhruva</s> there are fifteen lakhs.

children.text: dve koṭī pañca cāśītirlakṣāṇi svargato mahān ||
children.translated_text: From heaven to <s>Mahat</s> there are two crores and eighty-five lakhs.
<s>Mārkaṇḍa</s> and other seers, sages, and perfected beings are established there.
Gods whose authority has ceased are established in <s>Mahat</s>.
In the interval of <s>Mahat</s> there are other beings who enjoy offices of authority.
Eight crores above <s>Maharloka</s> is <s>Janaloka</s>; here stand <s>Kapila</s> and others.
The <s>Sādhyas</s> are there too, many of them, sharing in happiness.
From <s>Jana</s> to <s>Tapas</s> there are twelve crores; here are <s>Sanaka</s> and the other great-minded ones.
There the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, self-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, hold authority.
From <s>Tapas</s> to <s>Satya</s>, the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>, there are sixteen crores.
Situated there, that self-born one manifests this universe.
In <s>Satya</s> are the Vedas, and also others formed by ritual and meditation.
They are fixed in bliss; above that, one crore higher, is the seat of <s>Vairiñca</s>.
Two crores from the seat of <s>Brahmā</s> is described as the city of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s> reach that place through meditation, worship, and japa.
Seven crores beyond the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> realm is the world of the supreme Lord,
of <s>Rudra</s>, the maker of creation and dissolution, on the path of the cosmic egg.
Those who lack <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), but are intent on worshiping the <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: te yāntyaṇḍāntare raudraṃ puraṃ nādhaḥ kadācana
children.translated_text: go within the egg to the <s>Raudra</s> city, and never to a lower place.

children.text: tatsthāḥ sarve śivaṃ yānti rudrāḥ śrīkaṇṭhadīkṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All who are stationed there, <s>Rudras</s> initiated by <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, go to <s>Śiva</s>.
When their authority has ended, they go together with the host of <s>Rudra</s>'s daughters.
Above <s>Rudra</s>, city after city rises with successively greater extent.

children.text: brahmāṇḍādhaśca rudrordhvaṃ daṇḍapāṇeḥ puraṃ sa ca
children.translated_text: Below the cosmic egg and above <s>Rudra</s> is the city of <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>; and he,
by the will of <s>Śiva</s>, pierces the egg and makes the path of liberation.
<s>Śarva</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Deva</s>, then <s>Mahān</s>,

children.text: īśāna iti bhūrlokāt sapta lokeśvarāḥ śivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Īśāna</s>: from <s>Bhūrloka</s> upward these are the seven lordly <s>Śivas</s> of the worlds.
The seven worlds are begun from gross particulars; the higher ones, however,
from subtle ones, as the teacher too has explained correctly in the <s>Ruru</s>.
Those which were created in the beginning of creation by <s>Brahmā</s> from his own body are called abundant,

children.text: sthūlāḥ pañca viśeṣāḥ saptāmī tanmayā lokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the five gross particulars; the seven worlds consist of these.
Beyond them, with subtle great elements born of the <s>tanmātras</s> and supported by the <s>liṅga</s>,
the coverings of the worlds are mutually upheld by smell and the other qualities.
From <s>Kālāgni</s> up to <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> there are ninety-eight crores.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ kaṭāho 'ṇḍe sa ghanaḥ koṭiyojanam ||
children.translated_text: Above that, in the egg, is the shell, compact and one crore yojanas thick.
And upward from the surface of the earth there are fifty crores, and likewise below it.
Thus the earth would be one hundred crores in extent; beyond that is the golden rice-grain-like layer.
Up to the hundred <s>Rudras</s>, the mantra <s>huṃ phaṭ</s> should pierce it, though it is hard to subdue.
In each direction there are ten and ten; thus outside there are a hundred <s>Rudras</s>.
And that supports the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> on every side by its own power.
The form of the egg has been taught by the gurus in the glorious <s>Raurava</s> and other scriptures.
Turned toward manifestation and fallen away from the condition of pure power,
a mass of reality that contains an insertion and is not differentiated is called an egg.
For that which is tinged with a trace of darkness, the upper shell is <s>sattva</s>.
Its lower shell is <s>tamas</s>, a purified <s>sattva</s> tinged with <s>rajas</s>.
It is called a mass of reality, sharing in the aggregate of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.
That it is an egg is said with reference to its turning toward manifestation.
Even so, the powers immersed in <s>Śiva</s> could have the condition of an egg.

children.text: tadarthaṃ vākyamaparaṃ tā hi na cyutaśaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason there is another statement, since they have not fallen away from the state of power.
So that egghood should not wrongly extend to body, senses, and the rest, another word is used.
For in body, senses, and the rest there is no insertion of anything.
If one asks how there can be unity when there is a collection of body, senses, and so on,
the word 'undifferentiated' is used to show their common class-character.
Even without the expression 'mass of reality,' each individual principle might have
the nature of an egg among the <s>tattvas</s>; but even so, why is that not the case?
It would wrongly apply to a <s>tattva</s> made of the aggregate of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements.
The answer is: by the word 'reality' a form consisting of body, senses, and worlds is stated.
Therefore the aggregate of that is called an egg.
And that aggregatedness may belong to the Lord, who bears the universe as his body.
For this reason it has been shown that other differentiating marks have been taken up.
In the circle of the <s>adhvan</s>, dependent on <s>Māyā</s>, in states of just that extent,
others say that the differentiating marks are employed so that egghood may not occur.
Thus, the <s>Rudras</s> who support the egg of <s>Viriñci</s>, as described, are indeed a hundred.

children.text: teṣāṃ sve patayo rudrā ekādaśa mahārciṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Their own lords are eleven <s>Rudras</s> of great radiance:
<s>Ananta</s>, then <s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, <s>Bala</s>,
<s>Śīghra</s>, <s>Nidhīśa</s>, <s>Vidyeśa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, together with <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
Just as bees making honey surround a kadamba blossom and its filaments,
so those <s>Śivarudras</s>, with countless retinues, surround the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s>.
Their arrangement is eighty śaras, ten thousands, and a crore.
Presided over by <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, they create and also dissolve.
Thus is the lordship of the gods, according to the <s>Rauravavārttika</s>.
But in the <s>Siddhāntatantra</s>, outside the golden egg, beyond a hundred crores, there are a hundred
eggs, each successively twice as large, connected with silver and the other substances.
In them, in sequence, there would be <s>Brahmās</s> whose lifespans are doubled.
And they diminish in sequence; at their end is the principle composed of water.
From earth, here water and the rest arise in successive order upward.
Up to <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> each is tenfold; from that, intellect is a hundredfold.
Then the manifest is a thousandfold; the <s>pauruṣa</s> principle is ten thousandfold.
<s>Niyati</s> is a hundred thousandfold beyond that, and beyond it its next principle is ten hundred-thousandfold.
Up to <s>Kalā</s> it is a crore-fold; beyond that <s>Māyā</s> is ten crore-fold.
<s>Īśvara</s> is a hundred crores; beyond that, the <s>Sādākhya</s> extends a thousand crores.
And that, as <s>Śakti</s>, extends in number through a multitude.
The goddess <s>Vyāpinī</s>, pervading the whole <s>adhvan</s>, is established as having pervaded it.

children.text: aprameyaṃ tataḥ śuddhaṃ śivatattvaṃ paraṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond that they know the pure, immeasurable, supreme <s>Śivatattva</s>.
From water up to the <s>Śivatattva</s>, it has been seen by no one except <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> is the supreme cause of liberation.
And so <s>Mahādeva</s> says in the glorious <s>Svacchanda</s> scripture:
The bound soul does not attain liberation otherwise, even through hundreds of kinds of knowledge.

children.text: śivajñānaṃ na bhavati dīkṣām aprāpya śāṅkarīm ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> does not arise without receiving <s>Śāṅkarī</s> initiation.

children.text: prāktanī pārameśī sā pauruṣeyī ca sā punaḥ
children.translated_text: That is at first divine, belonging to the Supreme Lord, and again it is human.
Above the hundred <s>Rudras</s> is <s>Bhadrakālī</s>'s blue-shining city called <s>Jaya</s>.

children.text: na yajñadānatapasā prāpyaṃ kālyāḥ puraṃ jayam
children.translated_text: The city <s>Jaya</s> of <s>Kālī</s> is not attainable by sacrifice, gifts, or austerity.
Her devotees go there, those well initiated in her maṇḍala.
The supreme goddess grants liberation through seedless initiation.
As much initiation in the enclosure of the <s>Vidyeśas</s> as she performs for human beings,
so much attainment they reach, having been established here in that world.
Then, a crore beyond that, is <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, equal in radiance to the fire at the end of an age.

children.text: vijayākhyaṃ puraṃ cāsya ye smaranto maheśvaram
children.translated_text: And his city is called <s>Vijaya</s>; those who remember <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: jaleṣu maruṣu cāgnau śiraśchedena vā mṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and die in waters, in deserts, in fire, or by the cutting off of the head,
go to the great-splendored <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, full of the knowledge of <s>Īśāna</s>.
Above <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, at a distance of a crore, extended threefold in diameter,
is the watery <s>Rudrāṇḍa</s>, an egg standing in the shape of <s>Śakra</s>'s bow.
From the world of <s>Vīrabhadra</s> and likewise from the abode of <s>Bhadrakālī</s>,
it is adorned with thirteen other worlds.
Then comes the city of earth with its mountain, because of concentration on the odor-subtle-element.

children.text: mṛtā gacchanti tāṃ bhūmiṃ dharitryāḥ paramāṃ budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise who die there go to that supreme realm of the earth.
After that is the watery city of the ocean, because of concentration on the taste-subtle-element.
Then comes the city of <s>Śrī</s>, at the descents for the play of <s>Rudra</s>, and then
by death especially at <s>Prayāga</s> and on <s>Śrīgiri</s>, that attainment is reached.
Then there is the city called <s>Sārasvata</s>, the station of those who know <s>śabdabrahman</s> (the word as Brahman).
Those worlds are fitting for <s>Rudra</s> because of their primacy, and others are likewise established apart from the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: pureṣu bahudhā gaṅgā devādau śrīḥ sarasvatī
children.translated_text: In the cities, in many forms, are <s>Gaṅgā</s>; among the gods are <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
The eight lords of the gods in the waters extend from <s>Lakula</s> and the others down to <s>Amareśa</s>.
After that comes the fiery <s>tattva</s> (principle); here is the station of <s>Śiva</s> as fire.

children.text: te cainaṃ vahnimāyānti vāhnīṃ ye dhāraṇāṃ śritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those who have resorted to fiery <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) approach this fire.
In the fiery realm there is an octad of leaders, beginning with <s>Bhairava</s> and ending with <s>Hari</s> and <s>Indu</s>.

children.text: prāṇasya bhuvanaṃ vāyordaśadhā daśadhā tu tat ||
children.translated_text: The world of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), belonging to wind, is tenfold; and that, in turn, is tenfold.

children.text: dhyātvā tyaktvātha vā prāṇān kṛtvā tatraiva dhāraṇām
children.translated_text: Having meditated and then abandoned the breaths, or having fixed concentration right there,
the great souls enter that realm, becoming wind, their form being space.
The octad from <s>Bhīma</s> through <s>Gaya</s> belongs to the wind <s>tattva</s>.
In the ether <s>tattva</s> is the world of space; it is reached through concentration on space.
In the ether <s>tattva</s> there is an octad of gods, beginning with <s>Sthāṇu</s> and ending with <s>Vastrāpada</s>.
Those who, though uninitiated among the elements, identify themselves with the <s>Śiva</s> <s>tattva</s>,
and who, even without knowledge, possess mature concentration, are outside the cosmic egg.
Or else the initiated who go to the cities of earth, water, fire, wind, and ether
are there only for the sake of connection with purification, not for seeking the supreme station.
And those who die in such descents and in sacred shrines
attain that station and gradually pass into identity with <s>Śiva</s>.
This has been stated again and again in the venerable <s>Devyākhyayāmala</s>.
And in the description of <s>Kaśmīra</s> in the venerable <s>Kāmikā</s>, the Lord said:
In the great holy abode of <s>Sureśvarī</s>, those who die in that city,
whether brahmins and the rest down to mixed castes, animals, or beings down to immovable plants,
are all of <s>Rudra</s> lineage: so the blessed <s>Śiva</s> has said.
Above the covering of space and below ego, dear one,
in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s> are the cities of the <s>tanmātras</s> and the others up to mind.
The great maṇḍala of the smell-<s>tanmātra</s>, endowed with five colors,
stands within, covered over by many crores of yojanas.
So too the maṇḍalas of taste and the other subtle elements are arranged according to their own colors.

children.text: śarvo bhavaḥ paśupatirīśo bhīma iti kramāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s> are, in order,
the lords of the <s>tanmātras</s>; by their will, sound and the others act upon ether and the rest.
After that come the maṇḍalas of sun, moon, and the Vedas, ruled by the great all-pervading one.
<s>Ugra</s> and the others are the lords in these; from them come the sun and moon together with the sacrificer.
Thus these eight are the bodies of <s>Śambhu</s>, proclaimed as the higher forms.

children.text: aparā brahmaṇo 'ṇḍe tā vyāpya sarvaṃ vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: The lower forms stand within <s>Brahmā</s>'s egg, pervading everything.

children.text: kalpe kalpe prasūyante dharādyāstābhya eva tu ||
children.translated_text: In each kalpa, earth and the rest are produced from these very forms.
Then comes the maṇḍala of the instruments, furnished with the action-senses beginning with speech.
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Mitra</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, are the leaders in them.
From that is heard the maṇḍala of manifestation, the five cognitive senses.
The directions, lightning, the sun, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the earth are the deities of hearing and the other senses.
Above the maṇḍala of manifestation stands the maṇḍala of the five objects.
From that comes the mind-maṇḍala, since it is presided over by <s>Soma</s>.
Among the external gods, the presiding deity is characterized by equality, lordship, and pleasure.
Therefore the divine god of mind is declared to be <s>Soma</s>, the all-pervading one.
Beyond even that is the city of ego, the womb of all the senses and the birthplace of the cognitive senses,
joined with the octad beginning with <s>Sthūla</s> and ending with <s>Chagala</s>.
After that, the intellect <s>tattva</s> is lord of the city of the eight divine wombs.
That is said to extend from the <s>Paiśāca</s> up to the <s>Brāhma</s>.
These, according to the ancient account, are the very places and cities of the divine wombs.
Descending into them, and meditating on birth from themselves, they come into being.
By the command of <s>Parameśa</s>, and impelled by <s>Māyā</s>,
and also regulated by <s>Niyati</s>, they proceed from <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is from the unmanifest.
At the beginning of creation they become manifest in many ways through names and forms.
Yet those great souls, by their own portions alone, do not abandon their own abode.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śivatanāvidam adhikārapadasthitena guruṇā naḥ
children.translated_text: And our guru, established in the office of authority and knowing the bodies of <s>Śiva</s>, said this:
These indeed are the wombs for the manifestation of the powers of the eight gods.
Their bodies and experiences, again, are said to be lower and abundant in nature:
worlds more than forty in number, places of equal enjoyment.
Only because of the difference in means of accomplishment are these spoken of as five octads.
These are reached through devotion, yoga, abandonment of the breath, and the like.
In them <s>Umāpati</s> alone is lord, autonomous in his powers of perception and free from instruments.
By gradation beyond that, the octad of divine wombs is also to be recognized.
The senses of the worlds are instruments that delimit their objects.
From smell up to the great principle, lordship arises with one degree of superiority after another.
In this range from the <s>Paiśāca</s> to <s>Viriñca</s>, it has the nature of the powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness).
