Knowing this, one should purify the intellect together with the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (eightfold subtle body) and the senses.
They know the <s>Krodheśa</s> octad, beginning with <s>Saṃvarta</s>, as extending up to <s>Anīla</s>.
The fiery octad begins with <s>Balādhyakṣa</s> and proceeds through the <s>Krodhana</s> octad.
Then in the intellect the <s>Yogāṣṭaka</s> beginning with <s>Akṛta</s> is taught.
In the <s>Svacchanda</s> teaching that is at the root; in the venerable <s>Pūrva</s> teaching,
what is in the station of the <s>Yogāṣṭaka</s> and in <s>Soma</s> is precisely <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.

children.text: tato māyāpuraṃ bhūyaḥ śrīkaṇṭhasya ca kathyate ||
children.translated_text: After that, again, the city of <s>Māyā</s> and that of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> are described.
Thus a second world is taught for each of those two.
There the city of <s>Māyā</s> belongs to the Goddess, by whom the universe is governed.
In each kalpa she, <s>Maheśvarī</s>, is described under different names.
Afterwards comes the city of <s>Umāpati</s>, surrounded by the Mothers.
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> himself, in his higher form, is called <s>Umāpati</s>.
<s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Aiśī</s>, <s>Skandajā</s>, <s>Hārī</s>, <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, together with <s>Viccikā</s>,

children.text: pītā śuklā pītanīle nīlā śuklāruṇā kramāt
children.translated_text: are yellow, white, yellow-blue, blue, white, and red, respectively.
They go to the regions of <s>Agni</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the waters, the east, and <s>Nairṛta</s>.

children.text: aṃśena mānuṣe loke dhātrā tā hyavatāritāḥ
children.translated_text: In a portion they were brought down by the Creator into the human world.
Those <s>Svacchandās</s> are supreme; others are established in the higher sky.
They freely worship the sevenfold <s>Umā</s>, because
above the city of <s>Umāpati</s> stands the supreme group of eight forms,
beginning with <s>Śarva</s>, whose creation extends from earth up to the sacrificer.
The <s>Īśāna</s> form belonging to them is established on <s>Meru</s>.
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is on the crystal mountain; that form pervades the world with eight bodies.

children.text: ye yogaṃ saguṇaṃ śambhoḥ saṃyatāḥ paryupāsate ||
children.translated_text: Those restrained ones who meditate upon the qualified yoga of <s>Śambhu</s>,
or merely see that maṇḍala, are freed from duality and have the three defilements removed.
Because of the higher and lower supports of the <s>guṇas</s>, and because of the condition of purity and impurity,
and because yoga has gradations, there is variety in the results according to difference.
Therefore this difference is said to arise from the difference in obtaining enjoyment and its fruit.
Above the group of eight forms, twelve <s>Suśivas</s> are taught.
They extend from <s>Vāma</s> up to <s>Ekaśiva</s>, are saffron-hued, and possess great radiance.
Above that stands the lord of the maṇḍala called <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.

children.text: yattatsāyujyam āpannaḥ sa tena saha modate ||
children.translated_text: One who has attained union with him rejoices together with him.
Above even that, up to the measure of a thumb, there is the group of eight <s>Mahādevas</s>.
This is called the <s>buddhitattva</s> (principle of intellect), beginning from the eight divine wombs.
At the end of the eight <s>Mahādevas</s>, that is here called the eightfold yoga.
There, what was called the <s>Śraikaṇṭha</s> liberation is likewise that same <s>Umāpati</s>.
The forms, the <s>Suśivas</s>, the hero, and the eight <s>Mahādevas</s> are its body.
Above intellect and below <s>prakṛti</s> lies the principle called the <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: tattvaṃ tatra tu saṃkṣubdhā guṇāḥ prasuvate dhiyam
children.translated_text: There, when disturbed, the <s>guṇas</s> give birth to intellect.
A cause that has not come into differentiation is not able to produce an effect.
Therefore <s>prakṛti</s>, whose nature is the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s>, is the cause.
But if so, without disturbance, how could it bring forth those unequal <s>guṇas</s>
there? And if there is a first disturbance, there would be infinite regress.

children.text: sāṃkhyasya doṣa evāyaṃ yadi vā tena te guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is indeed the defect of the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> system; or else, for it, those <s>guṇas</s>

children.text: avyaktamiṣṭāḥ sāmyaṃ tu saṅgamātraṃ na cetarat
children.translated_text: are accepted as the unmanifest, while equilibrium is only their mere conjunction and nothing else.
For us, however, the unmanifest is connected with the disturbance that is the will of the independent Lord.
It is the cause of the <s>buddhitattva</s>; the <s>guṇas</s> are what has been disturbed.

children.text: nanu tattveśvarecchāto yaḥ kṣobhaḥ prakṛteḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: Objection: the disturbance of <s>prakṛti</s> that occurs first through the will of the lord of the principle
would itself be the <s>buddhitattva</s>; what need is there for other imagined <s>guṇas</s>?
No. That does not obstruct the reflective awareness of the form of causality, since
from it there is another disturbance as the effect, like a swollen seed and the sprout and so on.
In sequence, the rows of gurus are established in <s>tamas</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>sattva</s>:
three rows of thirty-two, thirty-one, and twenty-one.
Through the power of their own knowledge and yoga, the highest teachers sport there.
They have three eyes, are freed from bonds, and there act as bestowers of grace.
From intellect down to the limit of the <s>guṇas</s> there are two hundreds plus seven,
mainly of <s>Rudras</s> and worlds; others are in between them.
In the mass of the <s>guṇas</s>, the eightfold yoga has been taught; again, in the body of <s>Śiva</s>,
having passed beyond the wombs, in the secondary mass, there are givers of yoga.
In due order they are <s>Akṛta</s>, <s>Kṛta</s>, the all-pervading one, <s>Viriñca</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Guha</s>, and then the Goddess.
The instruments are the qualities beginning with minuteness; the effects are the manifold of cognitions.
From the unmanifest are produced the <s>guṇas</s>, beginning with <s>sattva</s>, which belong to these.
Dharma, knowledge, detachment, and lordship, and their various fruits,
these givers of yoga grant from the <s>guṇas</s> to the <s>puruṣas</s>.
Beyond them is the world of the god whose seat is the <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s>,
of the lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s>, husband of the one mother of the whole universe.
By him, in the worlds of <s>Umā</s>, <s>Guha</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Ṛbhukṣa</s>, <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Akṛta</s>, and the rest,
beings are presided over by the power that has the form of a graha, beginning with sovereignty.
He, wishing here to withdraw, enters the lotus of the four-faced one,
burns the four worlds, and then creates the <s>Jana</s> worlds again.
By his will, <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, whose body is the <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s>, emits.
The substitute ritual of <s>Rudrāṇī</s> is the altar; there it is worshipped by means of the substitute.
Then <s>Paśupati</s>, with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and <s>Viriñci</s>, and from the apprehension of that, by the gods,
the sacrifices are likewise diversified by gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages.
The supreme equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> is the unmanifest, above the <s>guṇas</s>.
There are <s>Krodheśa</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Jyotis</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and <s>Sūraka</s>,
and <s>Pañcāntaka</s>, <s>Ekavīra</s>, and <s>Śikhoda</s>; these eight are there.
The dense abode of <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, the root, the primal ground, and the unmanifest,
and the cause of the <s>guṇas</s>: these are synonyms for what arises from <s>māyā</s>.
As many knowers of the field as there are, whose consciousness is smeared with innate and adventitious impurity,
all of them are placed here, as are the <s>Rudras</s> who enjoy the experiences arising from that.
Some are without operative instruments, with instruments that are dull, developed, or dissolved.
Because there is no established basis for action, their capacities for action are dull.
Those that partake of fixed objects are distinct; in scripture they are described as developed.
Those broken at the great dissolution, not produced at creation, are dissolved.
Again, those dependent on will are called without instruments; the effect is the same in this respect.
In the <s>puruṣatattva</s> there are the nine satisfactions, and before it the eight perfections.
and just that many, namely the eight worlds beginning with <s>Aṇimā</s>.
Here, satisfaction is the contentment that comes from taking the non-tattva to be a tattva;

children.text: heye 'pyādeyadhīḥ siddhiḥ tathā coktaṃ hi kāpilaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and siddhi is the thought that what is to be rejected is to be accepted. Thus indeed the <s>Kāpilas</s> have said:
The four inner ones are called nature, means, time, and fortune;
and five arise from turning away from objects, through the obstruction, loss, attachment, protection, and acquisition of them.
Inference, authoritative word, study, the three removals of suffering, the obtaining of a friend,
and giving: these are the eight siddhis. Before siddhi there is a threefold goad.
Above the powers beginning with <s>Aṇimā</s> there are three rows belonging to teacher and disciple.
Even there, threeness is taught because of the conjunction with the shadow of the three guṇas.
Above the eightfold knowledge of the nāḍīs there is the set of rows beginning with <s>Iḍā</s>.

children.text: puṃsi nādamayī śaktiḥ prasarākhyā ca yatsthitā ||
children.translated_text: In the puruṣa there abides the power made of sound and called expansion.

children.text: na hyakartā pumānkartuḥ kāraṇatvaṃ ca saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: For the puruṣa is not a non-agent, and the causal status of an agent is established;
or, even if the puruṣa is a non-agent, he stands as an auxiliary cause.
Otherwise the nature of the remaining effect would have to be accepted, since the doctrine that the effect pre-exists would be lost.

children.text: tasmāttathāvidhe kārye yā śaktiḥ puruṣasya sā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the power of the puruṣa in an effect of that sort
takes on just so many forms and attains fullness.
Above the eight nāḍīs has been described the eightfold body-complex; it is now explained.
Effect, cause, pain, pleasure, knowledge, the object to be accomplished, the instruments,
and the means: in the puruṣa-tattva these form the pair of octads that constitutes the body-complex.
From the eightfold body-complex comes the world of the ten qualities of the body:
non-injury, truthfulness, non-stealing, purity with respect to <s>Brahman</s>, freedom from stain, absence of anger, service to the teacher,
cleanliness, contentment, and straightness: these ten are taught.

children.text: puṃstattva eva gandhāntaṃ sthitaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, within the puruṣa-tattva there is the set of sixteen extending as far as smell.
Beginning there is the city called the body-bond; after that come the qualities of intellect.
There too are the eight forms of egoity, and also the threefold bonds beginning with desire.
The bonds are divided into the adventitious, the Gāṇeśa, and the Vaidyeśvara.
These three kinds abide in the puruṣa as obstructions to the path of liberation.
Whatever is other than the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, beautiful in the freedom of supreme nondual consciousness,
and of the form just stated, that is called a bond.
Thus, when the complete Supreme Lord has assumed the state of puruṣa,
there is ignorance of his own nature; therefore puruṣas are indeed manifold.
All the bonds, whether stated or unstated, whose mark is taught as dependence on another,

children.text: te puṃsi sarve tāṃstatra śodhayanmucyate bhavāt ||
children.translated_text: are present in the puruṣa; by purifying them there, one is released from becoming.

children.text: puṃsa ūrdhvaṃ tu niyatistatrasthāḥ śaṃkarā daśa
children.translated_text: Above the puruṣa is <s>Niyati</s>; there are ten <s>Śaṅkaras</s> stationed there.

children.text: hemābhāḥ susitāḥ kālatattve tu daśa te śivāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are golden in radiance. In the <s>Kāla</s>-tattva those ten are white <s>Śivas</s>.
Each has an entourage of a crore and sixteen thousand.
In <s>Rāga</s> is the world of <s>Vīreśa</s>, the city of teachers and disciples.
In <s>Aśuddhavidyā</s> there is a city shining with the group of nine powers.
Those, ending with <s>Manonmanī</s>, are proclaimed as beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>.
In <s>Kalā</s> is the excellent city of the triad of <s>Mahādevas</s>.
Then comes <s>Māyā</s>, threefold, chiefly occupied by endless crores

children.text: ākrāntā sā bhagabilaiḥ proktaṃ śaivyāṃ tanau punaḥ
children.translated_text: of womb-cavities. In the Śaiva body it is again taught
that, extending down to the measure of the thumb, there is an eightfold group of <s>Mahādevas</s> at night,
as rulers over the eight cakras; and likewise in the <s>Śrīmālinīmata</s>.
Those beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>, said in the venerable <s>Pūrvaśāsana</s> to be in the puruṣa and the other levels,
are said in the Śaiva body to be precisely in the <s>Māyā</s>-tattva, endlessly.
Those who keep the skull-vow, those who offer oblations in their own limbs, harsh ascetics,
those who grant fearlessness to all, those who keep the vow of bearing the sword, and knowers of the respective tattvas,
successively attain those very tattvas, where the Lord is called <s>Ananta</s>.

children.text: uktaṃ ca tasya parataḥ sthānamanantādhipasya devasya
children.translated_text: And it has been said: Beyond it is the station of the god who is lord over <s>Ananta</s>,
the maker of maintenance, dissolution, and creation, the gatekeeper of the cave and womb-door.
Dharma, the qualities beginning with <s>Aṇimā</s>, forms of knowledge, austerities, pleasures, and yogas
he grants from the cave of <s>Māyā</s> to puruṣas, drawing them out again and again.
All those, strengthened by his power and by their own strength, are lamps for the darkness-quality of the cave's domain,
shining from <s>Ananta</s> at their head down to those headed by <s>Śatabhava</s>.
Having presided over the unmanifest, he produces the world by the command of <s>Śambhu</s>,
because he is a <s>Śiva</s> who is the cause of authority over the pure and impure streams.

children.text: śivaguṇayoge tasmin mahati pade ye pratiṣṭhitāḥ prathamam
children.translated_text: Those who, through conjunction with the qualities of <s>Śiva</s>, are first established in that great station
are the creators, maintainers, and dissolvers of the world beginning with <s>Ananta</s>.
This has been called the cave of <s>Māyā</s>; beyond it is the cave that is the womb of the world.
When its husband-powers are agitated and followed in their arising,
then, in the womb-openings, rich with various desires, there is what is called the vulva or generative aperture.
When the Lord desires this goddess, who follows his will,
then from each such aperture her progeny, beginning with the unmanifest, are born.
Because they are extremely subtle, their full extent is not described in the ritual injunctions.
Just as many small rooms are fastened in a single hall,
so the womb-cavities are in one hall that is the head of <s>Māyā</s>.
Covered by subtle walls formed from the veils of <s>Māyā</s>, mutually unseen,
there dwell happy <s>Rudras</s>, countless in each cavity.
Some have attained union in that station, others proximity, and others residence in the same world.
Thus, in each world, this arrangement of the inhabitants has been indicated by the teachers.
Even if the voices of all perfected beings were poured forth for a long time, they would be exhausted;
yet, because of the endlessness of the wombs, the numbers of the streams could not be stated.
Therefore, from hell onward up to what has been taught as the single gatekeeper,
By that stream, other streams too, having the same arrangement, should be understood.
In the unmanifest <s>kalā</s>, through the cave, together with <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>kalā</s>, its own transformation

children.text: otaḥ proto vyāptaḥ kalitaḥ pūrṇaḥ parikṣiptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is woven in, woven through, pervaded, arranged, filled, and enclosed.
In its middle are three enclosures; in the lower interior are six <s>Rudras</s>,

children.text: eka ūrdhve ca pañceti dvādaśaite nirūpitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one above, and five: these twelve have been described.
<s>Gahana</s> and <s>Asādhya</s>, <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>, <s>Daśeśvara</s> and <s>Trikalagopa</s>: these are the six.
In the middle are <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Kṣema</s>, <s>Dvijeśa</s>, <s>Vidyeśa</s>, <s>Viśvaśiva</s>.

children.text: iti pañca teṣu pañcasu ṣaṭsu ca puṭageṣu tatparāvṛttyā
children.translated_text: Thus there are five among those five, and six in the six enclosures; through their reversal

children.text: parivartate sthitiḥ kila devo 'nantastu sarvathā madhye ||
children.translated_text: the arrangement is said to turn about, while the god <s>Ananta</s> is in every way in the middle.
By the pair made of six upper and lower skull-like enclosures, and through their reversal,
from the middle it is pervaded by eight stationed in the directions; this is the knot taught in the scripture of <s>Mataṅga</s>.
But in the glorious <s>Sāraśāsana</s> this is specified as consisting of six enclosures.
This <s>tattva</s> called the knot is a product of <s>Māyā</s>; after that comes <s>Māyā</s>.
The <s>Māyātattva</s> is indeed all-pervading, profound, formless, the place where everything dissolves.

children.text: tatra na bhuvanavibhāgo yukto granthāvasau tasmāt ||
children.translated_text: There no division of worlds is appropriate, since it is at the termination of the knot.
Its lord, the ruler of the <s>Māyātattva</s>, is <s>Ananta</s>; having considered all the arisen atomic souls,

children.text: yugapatkṣobhayati niśāṃ sā sūte saṃpuṭairanantaiḥ svaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he agitates <s>Niśā</s> all at once, and she gives birth through her own countless casings.
Therefore the entire net of coverings, spoken of from <s>Kalā</s> down to earth,
is innumerable and various, yet it is one <s>Māyā</s>, not to be divided.
And it is said in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>: the pair consisting of earth and the unmanifest
is uncountable, called the power <s>Niśā</s>, yet it has a single nature.

children.text: pāśāḥ puroktāḥ praṇavāḥ pañca mānāṣṭakaṃ muneḥ
children.translated_text: The bonds mentioned before, the five <s>praṇavas</s>, the sage's set of eight measures,

children.text: kulaṃ yoniśca vāgīśī yasyāṃ jāto na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kula</s>, the womb, and <s>Vāgīśī</s>: in her, one who is born is not born again.
At the time of initiation, in the purification of what stands in the lower path, whatever belongs to the lower path
is all completely settled near <s>Ananta</s>.

children.text: sādhyo dātā damano dhyāno bhasmeti bindavaḥ pañca
children.translated_text: <s>Sādhya</s>, <s>Dātā</s>, <s>Damana</s>, <s>Dhyāna</s>, and <s>Bhasma</s> are the five bindus,
and, with its array, there is the group marked by <s>Pañcārtha</s>, <s>Guhya</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Aṅkuśa</s>, and <s>Hṛdaya</s>.
Together with <s>Ākarṣa</s> and <s>Ādarśa</s>, this is the eightfold set of the means of knowledge.
All of them, with their powers undiminished, are officers of the <s>Māyātattva</s>.
Having bodies made of <s>Māyā</s>, they enjoy their own enjoyment.
At the end of dissolution they are withdrawn by <s>Ananta</s>, and at the opening of the day,
by the grace of another <s>Ananta</s>, even the wise gods regard him as supreme,
thinking him asleep and awake, but made dull by the conceit that they are independent.
Situated within <s>Māyā</s>, they know only their own self as the cause.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ sthitā māyā devī jantuvimohinī ||
children.translated_text: Beyond this stands <s>Māyā</s>, the goddess who bewilders living beings.
She is the power of the God of gods, making what is extremely hard to accomplish come about.
With their understanding made to wander by her, who is hostile even while free of hatred,
disputants here argue, 'This is the <s>tattva</s>; this is not.'
Those lowest of men who have no devotion to the guru, the deity, the fire, and the scriptures,
she certainly abandons from the right path and leads onto the wrong path.
Those who think over false reasoning and rely on dry logic,
<s>Māyā</s> indeed deludes, through a desire for liberation where there is no liberation.
When cut by the sword of <s>Śiva</s>-initiation and likewise by the sword of <s>Śiva</s>-knowledge,
it does not sprout again; there is no other cause for cutting it.
Above <s>Mahāmāyā</s> are the pure <s>Mahāvidyā</s>, then <s>Mātṛkā</s>,
and <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>; located there is the excellent ninefold city beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>.

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalavikaraṇībalavikārike tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Kalavikaraṇī</s>, and <s>Balavikārikā</s>,

children.text: mathanī damanī manonmanī ca tridṛśaḥ pītāḥ samastāstāḥ
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Mathanī</s>, <s>Damanī</s>, and <s>Manonmanī</s>: all of them are three-eyed and yellow.
Seventy million chief mantras are established here in the <s>Vidyātattva</s>.
Here their lotus-shaped cities each have portions in the hundreds of millions and hundreds of thousands.
The queenly vidyās, beginning with <s>Triguṇī</s>, are seven; and there are seven lords of arbudas.
Above the <s>Vidyātattva</s> is the <s>Īśa</s> <s>tattva</s>; there, proceeding upward in sequence,
is a city furnished with eight cities, from <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> up to <s>Ananta</s>.
<s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>, <s>Śrīgala</s>, <s>Mūrti</s>, <s>Ekanetra</s> and <s>Ekarudra</s>,
<s>Śivottama</s>, <s>Sūkṣmarudra</s>, and <s>Ananta</s>: these are the eight <s>Vidyeśvaras</s>.
Their stations are arranged successively higher and higher; the all-pervading lord of the seven

children.text: ananta eva dhyeyaśca pūjyaś cāpy uttarottaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: is <s>Ananta</s> alone, to be meditated upon and worshipped at each higher stage.
The three and a half crores of chief <s>Mantreśvaras</s> that are established there
have these as their leaders; therefore the <s>Vidyeśas</s> are universal emperors.
And this has been stated by the teachers in this way in scriptures beginning with the <s>Śivatantra</s>:
The god, joined with eight powers, sits on the upper seat of the cave furnished with a hundred sacred openings.

children.text: gahanādyaṃ nirayāntaṃ sṛjati ca rudrāṃśca viniyuṅkte
children.translated_text: He creates from <s>Gahana</s> down to the hells, and he appoints the <s>Rudras</s>.
He raises human souls by means of <s>Manonmanī</s>; among those very beings he becomes the mediator.
With their consciousness lifted up by him, they become intent on beholding the supreme <s>tattva</s>.
He in turn is appointed by <s>Śiva</s> over the atomic souls who move on the lower path.
When the commission assigned by the Lord is completed, <s>Anantanātha</s>, together with many crores of mantras,
is extinguished; then <s>Sūkṣmarudra</s> enters that abode.
Having favored an unprecedented atomic soul, the Lord installs it in the place of <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>.
Thus, in order, until the one guru reaches those abodes,
he brings about release for innumerable living beings.
Those eight too, united with sets of eight powers and seated on stainless lotus seats,
behold the god who is in the heart, the supreme cause.

children.text: taṃ bhagavantamanantaṃ dhyāyantaḥ svahṛdi kāraṇaṃ śāntam ||
children.translated_text: Meditating in their own hearts on that blessed <s>Ananta</s>, the peaceful cause,
even seven pure crores of mantras contemplate him.
From <s>Māyā</s> down to <s>Avīci</s> is <s>bhava</s> (becoming); from <s>Ananta</s> onward it is also called <s>abhava</s> (non-becoming).
This too, extending to the domain of <s>Śiva</s>'s pure qualities, is something to be abandoned.
For even here there is seen a Śaiva appointment of those who are to be favored by grace.

children.text: iṣṭā ca tannivṛttirhyabhavastvadhare na bhūyate yasmāt
children.translated_text: And its cessation is desired; but lower down there is no <s>abhava</s>, because

children.text: patyur apasarpati yataḥ kāraṇatā kāryatā ca siddhebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: causality and effecthood, in relation to the perfected ones, withdraw from the Lord.
In the realization of <s>Śiva</s> with the <s>kañcukas</s> (limiting sheaths), the two called <s>bhava</s> and <s>abhava</s> are therefore very intermediate.
But the fourfold city of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Jñāna</s>, <s>Virāga</s>, and <s>Aiśvarya</s>
is known, in this <s>Īśvara</s> principle, as the enclosure named <s>Rūpa</s>.
It is adorned with the three worlds called <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Raudrī</s>.
In the <s>Īśa</s> principle, the best of gurus have declared the subtle enclosure.
From the <s>Īśa</s> level comes the <s>Sādāśiva</s>, adorned with the pair of knowledge and action.
They call this the pure enclosure; beyond the pure enclosure has been stated
the enclosure of <s>Vidyā</s>, shining with the two powers of being and non-being.
Then the power-enclosure named <s>Pramāṇa</s> is set forth in the scripture.
From the <s>Śakti</s>-enclosure, adorned by <s>Tejasvin</s> and <s>Dhruveśa</s>,
comes the <s>Tejasvin</s>-enclosure; with the <s>Veda</s>-city, next comes the measure-enclosure.
From the measure-enclosure, the very pure enclosure is adorned with a triad of cities.
Above the very pure enclosure there is one Śaiva city.
Above the <s>Śiva</s>-enclosure they call it by the name liberation-enclosure.
In this liberation-enclosure eleven <s>Rudras</s> are set forth.
But from the liberation-enclosure there is a single-city enclosure called <s>Dhruva</s>.
Above the <s>Dhruva</s>-enclosure is the will-enclosure; there those <s>Śivas</s>
stand within the house of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will, and its city is said to be one.
From the will-enclosure comes the one called <s>Prabuddha</s>, marked by the eight directional <s>Rudras</s>.
Above the <s>Prabuddha</s>-enclosure is the great <s>Samaya</s>-enclosure.
The enclosure including <s>Ananta</s> is embraced by five worlds.

children.text: sāmayāt sauśivaṃ tatra sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>Samaya</s> level comes the <s>Sauśiva</s>; there is the great world called <s>Sāda</s>.
In it is the god <s>Sadāśiva</s>; on his left and right
are knowledge and action, while supreme will is the <s>Śakti</s> who goes into his lap.
Through that will he performs the five acts beginning with creation.
The five <s>Brahmans</s>, the group of six limbs, and the eight <s>Śivas</s> beginning with <s>Sakala</s>,
together with the ten and eighteen <s>Rudras</s>: by these <s>Suśiva</s> is surrounded.
<s>Sadya</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and <s>Īśa</s> are the five <s>Brahmans</s>; <s>Hṛdaya</s>,
<s>Mūrdhan</s>, <s>Śikhā</s>, <s>Varman</s>, <s>Dṛk</s>, and <s>Astra</s> are called the six limbs.
Together with <s>Sakala</s>, <s>Akala</s>, and <s>Śūnya</s>, in the sky adorned and rich in <s>kalās</s>, <s>Kṣapaṇa</s> is the last.
<s>Kaṇṭhya</s> and <s>Auṣṭhya</s>, it is said, are the eighth; this is taught as the <s>Sakala</s>-octad.
<s>Oṃkāra-Śiva</s>, <s>Dīpta</s>, <s>Hetvīśa</s>, <s>Daśeśaka</s>, <s>Suśiva</s>, and <s>Kāla</s>,
<s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Sutejas</s>, and <s>Śarva</s>: these are the ten <s>Śivas</s> here, beginning from the east.
<s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Niḥśvāsa</s>, <s>Svāyambhuva</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Raurava</s>,
<s>Mukuṭa</s>, <s>Visara</s>, <s>Indu</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Prodgīta</s>, <s>Lalita</s>, <s>Siddha</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Santāna</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Parakiraṇa</s>, and <s>Pārameśa</s> are remembered as the <s>Rudras</s>.
The knowledges of all these are known by names identical with their own.
Then, surrounded by crores of mantras and sages, joined with <s>Vāma</s> and the other <s>Rudras</s> and their powers,
served by the powers beginning with <s>Tārā</s>, the seat of <s>Suśiva</s> is an exceedingly white lotus with countless petals.

children.text: yaḥ śaktirudravargaḥ parivāre viṣṭare ca suśivasya ||
children.translated_text: Whatever group of <s>Śaktis</s> and <s>Rudras</s> is in the retinue and expanse of <s>Suśiva</s>,
for each one of them, in its own retinue, there are countless parārdha-crores.
Free from the impurity of <s>Māyā</s>, established only in the mere office of authority,
the <s>Rudras</s> in the <s>Suśiva</s>-enclosure are omniscient and complete with all powers.
When the bondage of office dissolves, they again become tranquil and <s>Śiva</s>-formed.

children.text: ūrdhve bindvāvṛtirdīptā tatra tatra padmaṃ śaśiprabham
children.translated_text: Above is the radiant <s>Bindu</s>-enclosure; there, in each place, is a lotus with moonlike radiance.
There is <s>Śiva</s> beyond <s>Śānti</s>, adorned by the embrace of his <s>Śakti</s>.
He is surrounded by the retinue of the classes of <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>.
He is surrounded by countless <s>Rudras</s>, their powers, and crores of cities.
And in the venerable <s>Mataṅgaśāstra</s>, the highest principle called <s>Laya</s>
is a technical designation; here it is called <s>Bindu</s> by name.
That white reality, made of four forms, is both <s>Sakala</s> and <s>Niṣkala</s>.
In that, enjoyment is taught; and this too is described here.
Because <s>Nivṛtti</s> and the other <s>kalās</s> are extremely subtle, embodiment beginning with earth
is not perceived, since it is dissolved in the Mother's flashing great knowledge.
Just as particles of earth in gold do not appear separately
because fiery brilliance is predominant, so the bodies of the <s>Rudras</s> above and below do not appear separately.
Above <s>Bindu</s> is <s>Ardhendu</s>; its <s>kalā</s> is <s>Jyotsnā</s>, and, along with <s>Tadvatī</s>,

children.text: kāntiḥ prabhā ca vimalā pañcaitā rodhikāstataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s>: after that these five are the obstructing ones.
<s>Rundhanī</s>, <s>Rodhanī</s>, <s>Roddhrī</s>, <s>Jñānabodhā</s>, and <s>Tamopahā</s>:
the best of gurus declare these five <s>kalās</s> in <s>Nirodhinī</s>.
<s>Bindu</s> is remembered as the half-mātrā, sky-formed and fourfold in <s>kalās</s>.
Half of that is the half-moon; by an eighth part of that is <s>Nirodhikā</s>.
Because it blocks the causes beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, one should then abandon that <s>Rodhikā</s>.
Having pierced this <s>Nirodhikā</s>, one reaches the supreme world called <s>Sādākhya</s>,
where the great body of the five mantras abides in supreme form.
Thus, above the <s>Bindu</s>-enclosure ending with <s>Ardhendu</s> and <s>Nirodhinī</s>, is the great...
<s>Nāda</s>, resembling a lotus filament, is surrounded by great puruṣas.

children.text: catvāri bhuvanānyatra dikṣu madhye ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: Here there are four worlds in the directions, and a fifth in the middle.
<s>Indhikā</s>, <s>Dīpikā</s>, <s>Rodhikā</s>, <s>Mocikā</s>, and <s>Ūrdhvagā</s> are there.
In the middle here is a lotus; there the upward-moving one is surrounded by its powers.
Above <s>Nāda</s> is <s>Sauṣumna</s>; there is the Lord who bears those powers.
Its lord is surrounded on the left and right by <s>Piṅgalā</s> and <s>Iḍā</s>.
The goddess who rests in the Lord's lap is <s>Suṣumnā</s>, radiant like the moon.
By her the entire path is threaded, both the upper and the lower.
<s>Nāda</s>, having <s>Suṣumnā</s> as its support, pierces this whole universe.
It goes forth below by the lower power and from the crown by the upper power.
Merged in the channel at the <s>Brahmabila</s>, it is the imperishable, unmanifest sound.
It sounds in all beings, indeed presided over by <s>Śivaśakti</s>.
Above <s>Suṣumnā</s> is an enclosure called the <s>Brahmabila</s>, marked by the three-eyed one.

children.text: tatra brahmā sitaḥ śūlī pañcāsyaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Brahmā</s> is white, trident-bearing, five-faced, and moon-crested.
In his lap is the supreme goddess <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, who goes on the path of liberation.

children.text: roddhrī dātrī ca mokṣasya tāṃ bhittvā cordhvakuṇḍalī ||
children.translated_text: She obstructs and grants liberation; having pierced her, the upward <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>,
the power resembling a sleeping serpent, is called the support of the universe.

children.text: tasyāṃ sūkṣmā susūkṣmā ca tathānye amṛtāmite ||
children.translated_text: In her are <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Susūkṣmā</s>, and likewise the others, <s>Amṛtā</s> and <s>Amitā</s>.
In the middle is <s>Vyāpinī</s>; in her is <s>Vyāpīśa</s>, bearer of <s>Vyāpinī</s>.
This is the <s>śakti-tattva</s>; of it, this expansion extends down to earth.
Then there is the <s>śiva-tattva</s>; there, arranged in the four directions,
are <s>Vyāpī</s>, <s>Vyomātmaka</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and <s>Anātha</s>, sharing in its power.
But in the middle is <s>Anāśrita</s>; there the god of gods, <s>Anāśrita</s>,
holds that power in his lap and shines like a hundred crores of suns.
Above the <s>śiva-tattva</s> is the supreme power, called <s>Samanā</s>.
She is established as the agent among all causes.
She bears many cosmic eggs, presided over by <s>Śiva</s>.
Mounted upon her, the Lord <s>Śiva</s> performs the fivefold act.
<s>Samanā</s> is the instrument of that great Lord, the causal agent.
In activity, <s>Anāśrita</s> is called the occasion, the instrumental cause.
Through her the all-pervading Lord presides over the pentad of causes:
<s>Anāśrita</s>, <s>Anātha</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and the one whose body is space, always.

children.text: sa vyāpinaṃ prerayati svaśaktyā karaṇena tu
children.translated_text: He also impels <s>Vyāpin</s> by his own power as instrument.
Below that stands <s>Māyā</s>, in the form of action, as the coiled power.
<s>Nāda</s>, <s>Bindu</s>, and the rest are the effect; thus begins the arising of the world,
which, from earth and the other levels up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, is taught in the scripture.
All that is declared to be prākṛta, joined with destruction and production.
Now the measure of all the worlds, as it was told to me by my own teachers,
will be stated concisely, so that it may quickly pass into the intellect.
Within the egg are <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>Hāṭaka</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: rudrāḥ śataṃ savīraṃ bahirnivṛttistu sāṣṭaśatabhuvanā syāt
children.translated_text: Outside are the hundred <s>Rudras</s> together with <s>Vīra</s>; thus <s>Nivṛtti</s> has one hundred and eight worlds.
In the sevenfold group of water, fire, wind, ether, egoity, intellect, and root-principle, respectively,

children.text: aṣṭau ṣaṭpañcāśadbhuvanā tena pratiṣṭheti kalā kathitā
children.translated_text: there are eight each, making fifty-six worlds; by these the kalā called <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> is taught.
Here some say that only eight are to be purified, namely the lords of their own octads.

children.text: anye tu samastānāṃ śodhyatvaṃ varṇayanti bhuvanānām
children.translated_text: Others describe all the worlds as objects of purification.
The venerable teachers headed by <s>Bhūtirājamiśra</s>, however, said: outside are the hundred <s>Rudras</s>,
and inside are eight together with <s>Śarva</s>; such is this <s>Nivṛtti</s>.

children.text: rudrāḥ kālī vīro dharābdhilakṣmyaḥ sarasvatī guhyam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, <s>Dharā</s>, <s>Abdhi</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and <s>Guhya</s>:
this octad is in water. In fire are <s>Vahni</s> and the two <s>Atiguhya</s> worlds; in wind,

children.text: svapuraṃ gayādi khe ca vyoma pavitrāṣṭakaṃ ca bhuvanayugam ||
children.translated_text: are <s>Vāyu</s>'s own city and the worlds beginning with <s>Gayā</s>; in ether are <s>Vyoma</s>, the <s>Pavitra</s> octad, and a pair of worlds.
In <s>Abhimāna</s> are the octad beginning with <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>Chagala</s>; then within are ether and egoity.
There is the octad of cities belonging to the tanmātras, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Indu</s>, <s>Śruti</s>, and the deities of intellect and action.
There are ten in the aggregate of the tanmātras; again, where the class of sense-faculties descends, there is a world,
and one belonging to mind; thus in <s>Abhimāna</s> there are exactly twenty-two worlds.
In intellect are eight worlds of the divine ones; then the three called <s>Kṛt</s>, <s>Tejas</s>, and <s>Yoga</s>, and <s>Umā</s>.
Then there are her lord, the eight <s>Mūrtis</s>, the twelve <s>Suśivas</s>, and the <s>Vīrabhadras</s>.
After that comes the octad of <s>Mahādevas</s>; thus in intellect the number is seventeen.
In the <s>guṇa-tattva</s> there are three pentads; the ancient authorities know fifty-six cities.

children.text: yadyapi guṇasāmyātmani mūle krodheśvarāṣṭakaṃ tathāpi dhiyi
children.translated_text: Although in <s>Mūla</s>, whose nature is the equilibrium of the guṇas, there is the octad of <s>Krodheśvaras</s>, still in intellect

children.text: tacchodhitamiti gaṇanāṃ na punaḥ prāptaṃ pratiṣṭhāyām ||
children.translated_text: it has already been purified; therefore it is not counted again in <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>.
Thus, from the water-tattva through <s>Mūla</s>, twenty-four tattvas belong to <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>.
The group of <s>Tuṣṭis</s> beginning with <s>Ambā</s>, the siddhis beginning with <s>Tārā</s>, and the group beginning with <s>Aṇimā</s>,
the teachers, the teachers and disciples, the class of seers, and <s>Iḍā</s> and the rest, joined with the octad of forms,
the city of transformations beginning with smell, the eight qualities of intellect, ego-action, and the qualities of the objects,
the twenty-seven beginning with <s>Kāma</s>, the adventitious group, and likewise the forms of <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and <s>Vidyeśa</s>:
thus among the bonds there are three cities; here in the puruṣa there is a group of sixteen worlds.
In <s>Niyati</s> is the decade of <s>Śaṅkaras</s>; in <s>Kāla</s>, the decade of <s>Śivas</s>: thus there are two cities.
In <s>Rāga</s> is the world <s>Suhṛṣṭa</s> and the city of teacher and disciple; in the pair <s>Vidyā</s> and <s>Kalā</s>,

children.text: bhuvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ niśi puṭapuratrayaṃ vākpuraṃ pramāṇapuram
children.translated_text: there is world after world; in <s>Niśi</s> are the three <s>Puṭa</s> cities, the city of speech, and the city of valid knowledge.
Thus the <s>Vidyā</s>, having twenty-seven cities, is joined with the set of seven <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Puruṣa</s>.
The names are <s>Vāmeśa</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Śuddha</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, then <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Tejasvin</s>, and <s>Miti</s>;
<s>Suviśuddhi</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Mokṣa</s>, <s>Dhruveśa</s>, <s>Saṃbuddha</s>, <s>Samaya</s>, and <s>Sauśiva</s> are the designations.
The peaceful <s>Vidyā</s>, with seventeen cities, is joined with the triad of cities belonging to the <s>Vidyeśas</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
<s>Bindu</s>, <s>Ardhendu</s>, and <s>Nirodhya</s>, the supreme <s>Sauśiva</s>, and, in the <s>Sauṣumna</s> series, the cities beginning with <s>Indhikā</s>;
<s>Paranāda</s>, <s>Brahmabila</s>, and <s>Ūrdhvakuṇḍalī</s> as <s>Śakti</s>, together with <s>Sūkṣma</s> and the others;
then the five cities of <s>Vyāpin</s>, <s>Vyoman</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Anātha</s>, and <s>Anāśrita</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca paramamanāśritamatha samanābhuvanaṣoḍaśī yadi vā
children.translated_text: And the sixth is the supreme <s>Anāśrita</s>; or else, if <s>Samanā</s> is a group of sixteen worlds,
there are the covering of <s>Bindu</s>, the supreme <s>Sauśiva</s>, and the five worlds beginning with <s>Indhikā</s>;
<s>Sauṣumna</s>, <s>Brahmabila</s>, <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>, the pentad beginning with <s>Vyāpin</s>, and <s>Samanā</s>.
Thus this sixteenfold set of worlds, a pair of <s>tattvas</s>, is <s>Śāntyatītā</s>.
And in the revered <s>Mataṅga</s> scripture this is the order consisting of the mass of cities.
<s>Kālāgni</s>, the hells, and the chief hundred together with four are taught.
<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, the seven lower regions, the seven worlds, and <s>Maheśvara</s>:

children.text: ityaṇḍamadhyaṃ tadbāhye śataṃ rudrā iti sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is what lies within the cosmic egg; outside it stand a hundred <s>Rudras</s>.
The earth has two hundred and fifty-seven stations.
From the middle of the five octads there are thirty-two in the four gross elements.
And in the subtle elements there are five; after that the <s>Viśvedevas</s> form an octad.

children.text: pañcamaṃ sendriye garve buddhau devāṣṭakaṃ guṇe ||
children.translated_text: In the fifth, together with the senses, is <s>Garva</s>; in intellect there is the octad of gods, and in the <s>guṇa</s>
there is the <s>Yogāṣṭaka</s>, called <s>Krodha</s>; at the root, in <s>Kāla</s>, it is gradually assigned.
<s>Patadru</s> and the others, beginning with those of thumb-size, belong to the <s>Rāga</s>-<s>tattva</s>.
The twelve beginning with <s>Ekaśiva</s> are in <s>Vidyā</s>; in <s>Kalana</s> there are ten.
The three hundred beginning with <s>Vāmā</s> are this set, arranged in three divisions and accompanied by its four.
Some <s>Śaivas</s> here are called <s>Anantas</s>, others <s>Śrīkaṇṭhas</s>; this is the summary.

children.text: yatra yadā parabhogān bubhukṣate tatra yojanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Wherever he desires to enjoy higher experiences, the joining should be performed there.
Then there is purification when that is abandoned; the remainder should be treated as included within.
This differentiated scheme has therefore been shown in order to make the <s>āgama</s> known.
Other numerous alternatives too are to be inferred by teachers through their own intelligence.
But in the venerable <s>Pūrvaśāsana</s>, one hundred and eighteen are taught.
Here that which is principal and additional, and which is to be purified, is stated briefly.
<s>Kālāgni</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, the lord of hell, <s>Hāṭaka</s>, and then the lord of the earthly surface;
<s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of the sage-world, and five <s>Rudras</s> standing in the intermediate spaces;
below is <s>Ananta</s>; in the east are <s>Kapālin</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Anta</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, and the lord called <s>Bala</s>;
<s>Laghu</s>, <s>Nidhipati</s>, <s>Vidyādhipa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s> at the upper end, and <s>Vīrabhadrapati</s>.
With the eleven outer ones and likewise with five inner ones, the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> is counted.
Thus these sixteen cities are to be reckoned here for the <s>Nivṛtti-kalā</s>.
<s>Lakulīśa</s>, <s>Bhārabhūti</s>, <s>Diṇḍin</s>, <s>Āṣāḍhin</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, and <s>Nimeṣa</s>,
<s>Prabhāsa</s> and <s>Sureśa</s>: in water, each has its own retinue.
<s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Kedāra</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Madhyā</s>, and the one called <s>Āmrajalpa</s>,
<s>Śrīśaila</s> and <s>Hariścandra</s>: this secret octad is in the fiery principle.
<s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Kanakhala</s>, <s>Nākhala</s>, <s>Kuru</s>, and the one called <s>Gaya</s>:

children.text: atiguhyāṣṭakametanmaruti ca satanmātrake ca sākṣe ca
children.translated_text: this is the very secret octad in wind, and also in the subtle-elemental and sensory levels.
<s>Sthāṇu</s> and the one called <s>Suvarṇa</s>, then <s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Gokarṇa</s>, and <s>Mahālaya</s>,
<s>Avimukta</s>, <s>Rudrakoṭi</s>, and <s>Vastrāpada</s>: this pure set is in space.
<s>Sthūla</s>, <s>Sthūleśa</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, <s>Śruti</s>, and <s>Kālañjara</s>, bearing the circle,
and the two <s>Mākoṭāṇḍas</s> and <s>Chagalāṇḍa</s>: this is indeed an octad in <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
Others say that the subtle elements and the senses also are within <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
In intellect the octad of wombs is stated; in <s>prakṛti</s> is the <s>Yogāṣṭaka</s>, beginning, it is said, with <s>Akṛta</s>.

children.text: iti saptāṣṭakabhuvanā pratiṣṭhitiḥ salilato hi mūlāntā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the establishment consists of seven octads of worlds, from water down to the root.
In the person are <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhaveśa</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Gaurīśa</s>;
<s>Aja</s>, <s>Sānanta</s>, and <s>Ekaśiva</s>; in <s>Vidyā</s> there is the pair <s>Krodha</s> and <s>Caṇḍa</s>.
<s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Jyotiratha</s>, and, in <s>Kalā</s> and <s>Niyati</s>, the five ending with <s>Sūra</s>;
the triad called <s>Vīra</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is in <s>Kāla</s>.
<s>Mahātejas</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Bhavodbhava</s>, <s>Ekapiṅgala</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s>,
with <s>Bhuvaneśa</s> at their head and <s>Aṅguṣṭha</s>: these eight are situated in <s>Niśā</s>.
This <s>Vidyā</s>, extending from <s>Puruṣa</s> to the end of <s>Niśā</s>, has twenty-eight worlds.
<s>Hālāhala</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Kruddhāmbikā</s>, and <s>Aghorikā</s>, together with <s>Vāmā</s>, are taught.
In <s>Vidyā</s> are the <s>Vidyeśas</s>, eight in number; in <s>Īśa</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s> there are five.

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī śaktiḥ sakalā ca śontayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Sakalā</s> are in <s>Śānta</s>.
There are eighteen worlds; but <s>Śāntyatītā</s> is without worlds.
Thus the division of the path of place has been taught as instructed by the venerable <s>Śambhu</s>.
Now the division of the <s>tattvas</s>, reached in due order, is stated in detail.

children.text: yānyuktāni purāṇyamūni vividhair bhedair yadeṣvanvitaṃ rūpaṃ bhāti paraṃ prakāśaniviḍaṃ devaḥ sa ekaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: The cities that have been described, and the form that appears in them through various distinctions, dense with supreme light: that god is the one <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tatsvātantryarasātpunaḥ śivapadādbhede vibhāte paraṃ yadrūpaṃ bahudhānugāmi tadidaṃ tattvaṃ vibhoḥ śāsane ||
children.translated_text: Again, by the savor of his own freedom, when difference shines forth from the state of <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme form that follows in many ways is called <s>tattva</s> in the Lord's teaching.
For example, from the abode of <s>Kāla</s> up to the city of <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
because firmness, hardness, heaviness, and the like appear, there is the nature of earth.
The same should be said in the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with water, up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
in its own effect, or else in a stream of dharmas, or in a quality similar to itself,
it abides under the conception of generality, because it extends itself and because it has the character of a pervader.
Thus the respective tattvas, in sequence, beginning with earth and pradhāna and including puruṣa and <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: dehānāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca na prasaṅgastato bhavet
children.translated_text: would not thereby incur an unwanted extension with regard to bodies and worlds.
This has been stated by the Supreme Lord in texts such as the venerable <s>Mataṅgaśāstra</s>.
In that regard the accepted view concerning these is shown in the <s>Siddhayogīśvarīmata</s>:
The relation of effect and cause that is imagined by the will of <s>Śiva</s>
is such that, in reality, the maker of all beings is the sovereign, supreme <s>Śiva</s>.
Agency is never at all possible for what is not independent,
and independence belongs to the Supreme Lord, whose body is consciousness alone.

children.text: svatantraṃ ca jaḍaṃ ceti tadanyonyaṃ virudhyate ||
children.translated_text: To be independent and to be inert: these two are mutually opposed.
For inertness is dependence on a knower even with respect to the establishment of its own self.

children.text: na kartṛtvādṛte cānyat kāraṇatvaṃ hi labhyate ||
children.translated_text: And no causality at all is obtained apart from agency.
For the formula, 'when that exists, this exists,' has dependence as its single life-breath.
Among things that are independent and established in themselves, how could that be so?
If one says, 'this one is earlier and that one is later,' then earlier and later
are not additional to their nature; if so, only sameness remains.
If, in the case of seed and sprout, cause and effect possess the same reality,

children.text: ghaṭaḥ paṭaśceti bhavet kāryakāraṇatā na kim ||
children.translated_text: why then should there not also be a cause-and-effect relation between a pot and a cloth?
If the seed transforms into sprout, leaf, and so on,
that nature does not fit something whose own form is not of that nature.

children.text: sa tatsvabhāva iti cet tarhi bījāṅkurā nije
children.translated_text: If one says, 'it is of that nature,' then seed and sprout, in their own case,
do not come to rest within just that much, since utterly other things would also be possible.
Consequently it would follow that this thing is somehow of that whole variegated form.
If this is accepted, no: mutually contradictory forms cannot arise in an inert thing.

children.text: krameṇa citrākāro 'stu jaḍaḥ kiṃ nu virudhyate
children.translated_text: Let an inert thing have a variegated form in sequence; what contradiction is there?

children.text: kramo 'kramo vā bhāvasya na svarūpādhiko bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Sequence or non-sequence does not exceed the nature of a thing.
Both of these are merely apprehensions in that way; and is apprehension itself like that?
Even the apprehender is of the nature of cognition, and that nature of his too,
if it were to apprehend in sequence because it has the form of sequential apprehension,
then what would that sequence of his be, since no other thing is apprehended?
If it is said to be his nature, it cannot be additional to his own form.
If even sequence, though not additional to one's own form,
shines by its own nature through freedom, what else are we saying?
In this way the venerable <s>Śiva</s> alone is defined as the agent.
And this agency of his is manifestation merely in such a manner.
There is also manifestation in such a way that it conveys the relation of effect and cause.
For just as connection with a pot is manifested even for a cloth,

children.text: tathā ghaṭānantaratā kiṃ tu sā niyamojjhitā ||
children.translated_text: so too is being immediately after a pot; but that latter relation is devoid of regularity.
Therefore, whatever necessarily appears immediately after something,
when there is a further continuity of form, we call that thing its cause.
And regularity has as its essence only manifestation in such a form.
The manifestation 'a sprout comes from a seed' is certainly not present at all times,
because a sprout of that kind may arise immediately after a yogin's will.
For regularity appears in relation to a desired form of that sort.
In dream, pots, cloths, and the like appear to possess the nature of cause and effect,
with no invalidation, so long as that sphere lasts.
Therefore, to whatever extent regularity appears from such a nature, free from invalidation,
to that extent, by that nature, there is a firm cause-and-result character.
And when there is such a regularity, producing causeness and effectness,
in reality causality belongs only to what is made of consciousness, for that is all-pervading.
For this very reason, in the production of a pot, the complete assemblage is called the cause.

children.text: sāmagrī ca samagrāṇāṃ yadyekaṃ neṣyate vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if the assemblage is not accepted as a single body of the things assembled,
then difference in the causes would not produce difference in the result, and that is unreasonable.
If one says, 'Whatever follows that thing by positive and negative concomitance

children.text: tattasya hetu cetso 'yaṃ kuṇṭhatarko na naḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: is its cause,' that blunt reasoning is not pleasing to us.
And just as the complete causes are the stick, string, wheel, hands, and so forth,
so too distant and future things are causes in this way, we hold.
If there were there, or were going to be there, some <s>Meru</s>,
the pot surely would not arise, being prevented by that obstruction.

children.text: yathā ca cakraṃ niyate deśe kāle ca hetutām ||
children.translated_text: And just as the wheel enters into causality at a fixed place and time,
so too <s>Karki</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, and the rest stand within the limit of their own condition.
Thus, in the fixed combining and separating of those causes,
<s>Śiva</s> alone, being independent, would attain agency.
The consciousness of the potter in joining the wheel, stick, and the like

children.text: śiva eva hi sā yasmāt saṃvidaḥ kā viśiṣṭatā
children.translated_text: is indeed <s>Śiva</s>; for what distinction could there be within consciousness?
But if the potter's consciousness, because it manifests limitation,
is imagined as different and to be inserted among the stick, wheel, and so forth,
therefore, in the production of each single thing, <s>Śiva</s>, whose body is the one universe,
is the agent; even the person's conceit of agency is the act of the all-pervading Lord.
For this very reason, because the relation of effect and cause is established
as having its ultimate reality in manifestation in that way, there is variety in the world and in scripture.
In the <s>Rauravasaṃgraha</s> it is said, 'From <s>Māyā</s> come the unmanifest and <s>Kalā</s>.'
But in the venerable <s>Pūrva</s>, the unmanifest is said to come from the <s>Kalā</s>-tattva.
From that very one called Night, become <s>Kalī</s>, comes the unmarked principle.
When this principle stated by us is accepted, such exegesis is quite fruitless.
And in ordinary life, from cow-dung, from an insect, from intention, from dream, from memory,
from a yogin's will, and from the power of substances, mantras, and so on, a scorpion may arise.

children.text: anya eva sa cet kāmaṃ kutaścitsvaviśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: If that is indeed different, let it be so, because of some particular feature of its own, from whatever source.
But it is the same everywhere, for there is a unity in the reflective apprehension of that object.
For that very reason, even with respect to intrinsic form and also with respect to sequence, there is a different kind of established arrangement.
Such variety is fitting in the scriptures, since the nature of such entities is to appear in varied ways.
In the <s>Jñānottara</s>, the sequence is <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, <s>kāla</s>, and <s>māyā</s>.
In the <s>Vairiñca</s> there is no <s>niyati</s>; above <s>kalā</s>, <s>niyati</s> is taught.
Above the triad of <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and <s>vidyā</s> is the enclosure of <s>kalā</s> and <s>niyati</s>.
Then <s>kāla</s> and <s>māyā</s>: this is the sequence stated in the <s>Kiraṇaśāstra</s>.
<s>Pumān</s> is joined with <s>niyati</s>, and <s>kāla</s> is accompanied by <s>rāga</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, and <s>kalā</s>.
This sequence is indicated in the <s>Mātaṅga Pārameśvara</s>.
When the <s>tattvas</s>, standing in a relation of effect and cause, have been arranged in this way,
we shall state the construction of the causes as taught in the venerable <s>Śrīpūrvaśāstra</s>.
<s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is autonomous vision, is abundantly filled with the five powers.
The difference manifested by his freedom is divided fivefold.
Because consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, and action are completely manifest,
there is the pentad of <s>tattvas</s> named <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s>.
Even in each single one of these <s>tattvas</s>, which is abundantly filled with all the powers,
each particular distinction is defined according to the predominance of this or that power.
For, by the fullness of his own autonomy, the all-pervading Lord,
shines in innumerable and many forms, because limitation is absent.
The <s>Śāmbhavas</s>, those born of <s>Śakti</s>, the <s>Mantramaheśas</s>, the <s>Mantranāyakas</s>,

children.text: mantrā iti viśuddhāḥ syuramī pañca gaṇāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: and the <s>Mantras</s>: these pure ones are the five classes in order.
Whatever corresponding form shines within each respective class,
that is said to be the <s>tattva</s> among these, as <s>Kālāgni</s> and the others are with respect to earth and the other elements.
Therefore, those who speak as follows, deluded by a resemblance to narrative accounts,
and whose cherished view has been taken merely from books, without service to a guru, say:
"<s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of <s>Nivṛtti</s>, is not counted as a separate <s>tattva</s>.

children.text: sadāśivādyāstu pṛthag gaṇyanta iti ko nayaḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Sadāśiva</s> and the others are counted separately. What principle is this?
In the sixfold group called the causes, consisting of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Suśiva</s>, and <s>Anāśrita</s>,
whence comes this half-and-half old-woman logic?"

children.text: iti tanmūlato dhvastaṃ gaṇitaṃ nahi kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Thus that enumeration is destroyed at its root; it is not a valid account of the causes.
Just as a king, though lord of the earth, is not another <s>tattva</s>,
so how could the lord of each respective <s>kalā</s> be a separate additional <s>tattva</s>?
Thus this pentad is defined as the pure course of manifestation.
There, directly, <s>Śiva</s>'s will itself differentiates what has been manifested through agency.
<s>Aghoreśa</s>, in order to apportion the groups of consciousness eager for enjoyment and stirred by the force of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will,
creates here the white and the other form.
Among the atomic selves, the longing that is free from karma is called <s>lolikā</s>.
The ignorance that thinks, "I am incomplete," is <s>mala</s>, impurity, though it is devoid of any real limiting boundary.
It is merely a capacity for gathering future limitations.
Therefore this <s>mala</s> has no status as a separate <s>tattva</s>, any more than <s>rāga</s> does.
When that same longing is limited only by a portion of unlimited action,
it is <s>rāga</s> in the person; the variety produced by differences of karma is a property of the intellect.
And this thinking oneself incomplete is a manifestation in just such a form.
Just as a pot, in pot-form, is the will of autonomous <s>Śiva</s>,
so <s>mala</s> is a real entity precisely as the will to conceal one's own self.
Just as earth and the other elements, though not separate from him, have a nature as things to be manifested,
so too does this <s>mala</s>; therefore in the scriptures it is presented as distinct.
But there is no distinct autonomous entity at all, like a cart and the like.
If that impurity existed as a second thing, would it not attach to <s>Śiva</s> and to liberated atomic selves?

children.text: malasya roddhrī kāpyasti śaktiḥ sa cāpyamuktagā ||
children.translated_text: If there is some power that restrains <s>mala</s>, and that too belongs to the unliberated,
this is an argument abandoned by logic, fashioned solely out of faith.
That restraining power of an inert thing does not act by itself.

children.text: svayaṃ pravṛttau viśvaṃ syāttathā ceśanikā pramā
children.translated_text: If it did act by itself, the universe would result; and in that case what proof would there be for a Lord?
If <s>Īśa</s> connects that restraining power with <s>mala</s>, then,
when asked, "With respect to which atomic self?" there is no verbal answer.
And <s>mala</s> is a covering, but a covering is not a distinguishing property of the thing covered.
It obstructs apprehension, like a cloth-covering over a jar.
If the true nature belonging to the atomic selves whose form is covered by <s>mala</s>

children.text: śiva eva ca tatpaśyettasyaivāsau malo bhavet
children.translated_text: were seen by <s>Śiva</s> alone, then that <s>mala</s> would belong to him alone.
For the group of atomic selves, whose essence is merely the all-pervading Lord's knowledge and action,
the absence of that is imagined as <s>mala</s> only for the destruction of their own nature.
The difference between property and property-bearer, and their unity through inherence,
has not been stated by you, as it would be by a disciple of <s>Kaṇabhuj</s>.

children.text: nāmūrtena na mūrtena prāvarītuṃ ca śakyate ||
children.translated_text: Neither by something noncorporeal nor by something corporeal can knowledge be covered.
For even when things are of that sort, the knowledge connected with the rays of sight still moves forth.

children.text: sa eva ca malo mūrtaḥ kiṃ jñānena na vedyate ||
children.translated_text: And if that very <s>mala</s> is corporeal, why is it not known by knowledge,

children.text: sarvageṇa tataḥ sarvaḥ sarvajñatvaṃ na kiṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: since knowledge is all-pervading? Then why should everyone not partake of omniscience?
As for the covering of light by darkness, that occurs through things that resist it,
for resistance belongs to corporeal things; such a thing is not noncorporeal among the atomic selves.
Nor is non-autonomous <s>mala</s> capable of covering the conscious self.
And the example of being covered by wine should not be stated here.

children.text: uktaṃ bhavadbhirevetthaṃ jaḍaḥ kartā nahi svayam ||
children.translated_text: You yourselves have said it in this way: an inert thing is not an agent by itself.
These powers of the autonomous <s>Īśvara</s>, indeed, are the impellers.
Therefore, driven by the force of the Lord's power that knows the ripening of karma,
wine produces intoxication, whose fruits are pain, pleasure, and delusion.
And if <s>mala</s>, not impelled by <s>Īśa</s>, were to cover the person, then, because...
In a pure person, likewise, the Lord's being an impeller is not appropriate;

children.text: tulye nirmalabhāve ca prerayeyurna te katham ||
children.translated_text: and if the state of purity is equal, how would those others not impel him?

children.text: tamīśaṃ prati yuktaṃ yad bhūyasāṃ syātsadharmatā
children.translated_text: Whatever common nature among many would be proper with respect to that Lord,
by that, only the innate freedom of one's own nature is displayed as expanded by <s>mala</s>.
This has been determined at length by me elsewhere; so enough of repeating it.
<s>Mala</s> is desire, ignorance, nescience, the manifestation of restlessness,
the fault of becoming, inundation, weariness, desiccation, bewilderment,
the distress of I-ness and mine-ness, the power of <s>Māyā</s>, and covering;
the seed of fault, the state of the bound soul, and the cause of the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
By such meaningful names it is spoken of here and there.

children.text: asmin sati bhavati bhavo duṣṭo bhedātmaneti bhavadoṣaḥ
children.translated_text: When this exists, becoming is faulty because its nature is difference; hence it is called the fault of becoming.
And because, in it, as on a couch or raft, a stream of suffering carries the atomic souls, it is called inundation.
The remaining words are easy in form; in each case one should infer the suitable meaning.
Karma, the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, is called the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
For the fourteenfold variety of beings is born from karma.
Therefore, in the teachings of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Pāñcarātra</s>, and the like,
the abandonment of 'I' and 'mine' is taught for freedom from karma.
For one who is without karma, even though the root <s>mala</s> called ignorance remains,
does not rise upward nor descend downward, because the cause of variety is absent.
Only through limitation, without touching non-difference from <s>Śiva</s>,
he is called a <s>vijñānakevalin</s>, established in pure consciousness alone.
Then, through the will belonging to <s>Śambhu</s>, touching non-difference from <s>Śiva</s>,
he gradually assumes the form of a <s>Mantreśa</s> and of its ruler, and reaches identity with <s>Śiva</s>.
Objection: If <s>mala</s> is the cause of this karma, then how
does it not produce a continuum of karma even for the <s>vijñānākala</s>?

children.text: maivaṃ sa hi malo jñānākale didhvaṃsiṣuḥ katham ||
children.translated_text: Not so; for in the <s>jñānākala</s> that <s>mala</s> is about to be destroyed. How, then,
could it be a cause? And its being destroyed would arise from freedom alone.
In the three conditions called about-to-be-destroyed, being-destroyed, and destroyed,
with further intermediate states included within them, each standing in its own sequence,
there is the construction of the states called <s>vijñānākala</s>, <s>Mantreśa</s>, their lord, and so on.

children.text: tataśca supte turye ca vakṣyate bahubhedatā
children.translated_text: Therefore, in sleep and in the fourth state too, a great variety of distinctions will be explained.
Therefore, when its own power has become impaired because it is turned toward destruction,
how can <s>mala</s> be said to acquire causal status with respect to karma?

children.text: kiṃ ca karmāpi na malādyataḥ karma kriyātmakam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, karma also does not arise from <s>mala</s>, because karma consists of action;
and action comes from freedom in the form of agency, not from <s>mala</s>.
But the karmic character of this karma, familiar as its giving varied fruits,

children.text: prasiddhā sā na saṃkocaṃ vinātmani malaśca saḥ
children.translated_text: does not exist without contraction in the self; and that contraction is <s>mala</s>.
For a varied fruit, being distinct, is conceived as something to be enjoyed;
therefore, in the enjoying self, there is this arrangement whose form is difference.
Thus, relying on its role as assistant in producing its own effect,
<s>mala</s> is the cause of karma by manifesting karma's capacity.
Objection: But if this is so, since karma exists and <s>mala</s> also remains, how
can he have the state of a <s>vijñānākala</s>? For contraction of that sort still exists.
Not so. Although his contraction has not been destroyed, through firm cultivation
he gives up the karmic impression, thinking, 'I am not the agent.'
The firm disposition in the self, 'This karma will bear fruit,'

children.text: sa saṃskāraḥ phalāyeha na tu smaraṇakāraṇam
children.translated_text: is here the impression that leads to fruit, not the cause of memory.
Even when contraction has not been destroyed, because of cultivating 'I am not the agent,'

children.text: na phalaṃ kṣīvamūḍhādeḥ prāyaścitte 'tha vā kṛte
children.translated_text: there is no fruit, as in the case of one drunk or confused, or when expiation has been performed.
The action of one who has the clear intention, 'The austerity I have performed today should belong to him,'
does not bear fruit for the intended person merely because he has been intended.
Rather, what is called intention is a mental conditioning of karma;
when it is made tinged by fruit, it becomes fit for the attainment of fruit.
But one who, even there, firmly abandons the fruit-impression
enjoys the special fruit produced by that renunciation of fruit.
By this procedure, one who casts off the entire continuum of karma
through a state unjoined with I-ness, though he is still contracted, is an <s>akala</s>.
Objection: But in this way some evil deed of one's own, through intention,

children.text: parasmai syānna vijñātaṃ bhavatā tāttvikaṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: would belong to another. You have not understood the true teaching.
If that enjoyer had an intention toward it in the same way as toward his own self,
then that evil deed, being present, would necessarily belong also to the other.
When another's intention is cognized, one's own intention becomes firm;
but when there is no intention, it has no connection with fruit for him.
The settled conviction, 'The evil deed is not mine,' makes it fruitless for him.
When the other's intention is cut off and it is not intended by oneself,
there would be no fruit for either, because the cause of its destruction is established.
In regard to a cause of happiness, and to happiness itself, because of his general intention,
it is proper that he should enjoy the fruit of dharma and the like, even from what is undifferentiated.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ me duḥkhaheturvā stādityeṣa punarna tu
children.translated_text: But the thought, 'May suffering, or a cause of suffering, be mine,'
would not be even a general intention; therefore there is no arrival of that adharma.
We return to the matter at hand: for the <s>jñānākala</s> described above,
all karmic conditionings have dissolved through a state unjoined with I-ness.
Therefore he has no karma at all for which
<s>mala</s> could act as a cooperator; by that he attains the state of being destroyed.
But one whose <s>mala</s> has been destroyed, mastered by inner absorption into <s>Śiva</s>,
even though intent on I-consciousness, does not enter a condition dependent on karma.
And this has also been stated by the supreme Lord in the revered <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>:
'They consider <s>mala</s> (impurity) to be ignorance, the cause of the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'
Karma, whose nature is <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, is characterized by pleasure, pain, and the like;
one should identify pleasure, pain, and the like as its own effects, on the basis of its being their cause.

children.text: nahi hetuḥ kadāpyāste vinā kārya nijaṃ kvacit
children.translated_text: For a cause never exists anywhere without its own effect;
that causal status is just a capacity, understood as immediately preceding its fruit.

children.text: pūrvakasya tu hetutvaṃ pāramparyeṇa kiṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: But the causality of what is prior is by succession; what else could it be?
It is recognized through pleasure, pain, and the like, even when the visible cause is the same.
Because varied effects are seen, there must be some other cause, and here that cause is karma.
For brightness, roughness, and so on, arising in one's own limbs, are observed to come from one's own karma.
Since this is seen, karma is inferred as a cause that can be situated in another body.
For here too the fruits of karma are clearly found in one body after another.

children.text: kṛṣikarma madhau bhogaḥ śaradyanyā ca sā tanuḥ
children.translated_text: Agricultural work is done in spring, while enjoyment comes in autumn, and that body is different;
yet because a single agent of continuity is possible, therefore

children.text: tasyaiva tatphalaṃ citraṃ karma yasya purātanam
children.translated_text: that varied fruit belongs to the very one whose ancient karma it was.
If even a drunken king should order a cook in the morning, 'Prepare such a thing
and feed me,' he obtains that fruit without any further recollective connection.
In this way, karma acquired in another birth too

children.text: vinā bhuṅkte phalaṃ hetustatra prācyā hyakampatā
children.translated_text: is enjoyed as fruit today without recollection; there the cause is the old, unshaken conditioning.

children.text: ata eva kṛtaṃ karma karmaṇā tapasāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, karma that has been performed, whether by an act or by austerity,
or by knowledge, may be checked before it has turned toward the ripening of its fruit.
But how can the karma whose effect has already begun in this body
be cut off? Its final stage cannot be restrained.
As for other karma in that same body, whether current or ancient,
that karma can indeed be rendered impotent by knowledge, initiation, and the like.

children.text: tathā saṃskāradārḍhya hi phalāya dṛḍhatā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For in that way the firmness of the <s>saṃskāra</s> (conditioning) exists; firmness, again, is for the sake of fruit.

children.text: yadā yadā vinaśyeta karmadhvastaṃ tadā tadā
children.translated_text: Whenever that firmness is destroyed, then the karma has been destroyed.
Therefore, although a person subject to delusion may have done anything at all,
nevertheless at the time of knowledge all of that is burned up.
And it has been said in the revered <s>Parā</s>: 'One who neither rejects nor accepts, all-seeing and intense,
burns up in a moment everything, done or not done, that is situated in the body.'
'Situated in the body' means that consciousness, through identity with the body,
is said by its own freedom to be located there; the karma located there is burned.
This occurs because the tendency toward bodily identity has been abandoned, and because there is abiding as the Self of the universe.
For the conditioning process that is unmeasured by time, pervasive, and undivided
is only contraction; and by this, that too consists in identity with the body.
This has been called karmic <s>mala</s>; together with it the <s>layākalas</s>
remain within the depths of the cave, like sleeping creeping beings.
Then, when their conditionings have awakened, receiving their appropriate shares,
they wander again and again in this world, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to stationary beings.
But those who, for the removal of karmic conditionings, have begun cultivation
and have gone to the great dissolution without attaining the full completion of that cultivation,
they, because of the excellent ripening of the cultivation held within,
attain the state of mantra, through karma that is various in ever different ways.
Of this karmic <s>mala</s>, which extends along the path as far as <s>māyā</s>,
the principal cause is said to be the atomic <s>mala</s>, whose nature is ignorance.
The agitation of this, called <s>lolikā</s>, clearly serves as a cooperating factor;
and, under the power of the Lord's will, that is an inclination toward the capacity for the desire to persist.

children.text: na jaḍaścidadhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā kvāpi kṣamo yataḥ
children.translated_text: For what is inert is nowhere capable without a foundation in consciousness.
What is called the atomic being is nothing other than <s>Maheśvara</s>, whose nature is light;
appearing as both conscious and unconscious, it is the individual, the knower of the field, the bound soul.
And because it has the nature of consciousness, it is pervasive, without qualities, and inactive;
it is described as seeking the yogic means, eternal, and not bound to a formed body.
Because of its unconscious aspect there are ignorance, difference, and separation from the enjoyed object and from other enjoyers.
That <s>mala</s> of these atomic beings, by the force of the Lord's will,
awakens intensely; and so it is said in the scripture named <s>Śrīpūrva</s>:
'By the force of the Lord's will, the desire for enjoyment arises in him.
For the sake of helping the one who desires enjoyment, the primordial <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>,
having stirred <s>māyā</s>, creates the manifold <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And what is called <s>māyā</s> is the inseparable power of the God,
the freedom to manifest difference; for thus it is produced by him through her.
The first appearance of difference, which had not yet entered into division,
is the supreme night, containing in embryo infinite future manifestations.

children.text: sā jaḍā bhedarūpatvāt kāryaṃ cāsyā jaḍaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is inert because it has the nature of difference, and its effect too is inert.
It is pervasive because it is the cause of the universe, subtle because the effect is conceived as one,
and, because it is inseparable from <s>Śiva</s>'s power, it is eternal, one, and the root cause.
Everything that is an effect is non-conscious and manifold, like a pot;

children.text: pradhānaṃ ca tathā tasmāt kārya nātmā tu cetanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>pradhāna</s> is the same. Therefore an effect is not the conscious Self.

children.text: ata evādhvani proktā pūrvaṃ māyā dvidhā sthitā
children.translated_text: For this very reason, on the path described earlier, <s>māyā</s> is established in two ways.

children.text: yathā ca māyā devasya śaktirabhyeti bhedinam ||
children.translated_text: Just as <s>māyā</s>, the God's power, enters the status of a differentiating <s>tattva</s>,
so too does the further expansion of <s>tattvas</s>, beginning with <s>kalā</s>.
The Lord's power, whose nature is the slight opening of agency when power has been restrained,
and which casts the <s>puruṣa</s> downward, is called <s>kalā</s>.
In this way, <s>vidyā</s> and the rest, down to earth,
are in reality nothing but forms of <s>Śiva</s>'s power, according to the reasoning already stated.
Nevertheless, because <s>kalā</s> and the others appear separately by the Lord's will,
there is certainly a standing as distinct <s>tattvas</s>, in inertness and in being effects.
Māyā is remembered as the material cause, and in some places as that very effect itself.
Likewise, the variegated form that appears is mutually distinct.
What shines forth in conceptual construction, that surely exists externally, like a pot.
Therefore we affirm the existence of sky-flowers and the like; there is no deviation from the rule.
A sky-flower, in relation to time, direction, and measure, is indicated by the word 'nonexistent'.
As with earth and the other elements, so too absolute nonexistence should be analyzed in this way.
Whatever can be conceived in such a manner has an external conscious body.
Like <s>Caitra</s>, all that, up to <s>Suśiva</s>, has a body of that kind.

children.text: yasya deho yathā tasya tajjātīyaṃ puraṃ bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For each being, according to the body he has, there is outside a city belonging to that same class.
Therefore the ordered system of worlds, extending up to <s>Suśiva</s>, is established.
That city is attainable by selves, because it has the character of a place, like any other place.
From this, the selves' status as enjoyers of the paths is established without effort.

children.text: sā māyā kṣobhamāpannā viśvaṃ sūte samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: That Māyā, having entered into agitation, gives birth to the universe on every side.
Although it is indeed like an amalaka fruit struck by a stick, scattering its fruits,
nevertheless, because of the manifestation of a variegated before-and-after sequence,
even in Māyā's effect, the mass of tattvas, there is mutual causality of effect and cause.
Although this is plainly seen in many ways in other śāstras,
nevertheless we shall explain it from the viewpoint of the <s>Mālinī</s> scripture.
What they declare to extend from kalā down to earth is within Māyā.
This is certainly different for each self, because of differences such as pleasure and pain.
If there were only one world, a single aggregate of instruments for experience,
how could there be difference of experience, since pleasures and the like would manifest equally?
Nor is that difference due to difference of karma, because that very explanation is untenable.

children.text: tasmāt kalādiko vargo bhinna eva kadācana
children.translated_text: Therefore the group beginning with kalā is in fact distinct in each case.
It becomes one through the Lord's will, as in the performance of dance, song, and the like.
For all these tattvas beginning with kalā, which are to arise,
there is purity for those who have been purified by śaktipāta.

children.text: kalā hi śuddhā tattādṛk karmatvaṃ saṃprasūyate
children.translated_text: For kalā, when pure, produces karma of just that kind.
By that karma, though limited, this person is quickly released from saṃsāra.
The aggregate of rāga, vidyā, kāla, yati, prakṛti, and the sense-objects

children.text: itthaṃ śuddha iti procya gururmānastutau vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: is thus declared pure by the all-pervading guru in the <s>Mānastuti</s>.
In this way the arising of these, kalā and the others, is analyzed in detail.
From the Māyā-tattva, kalā is born, whose defining mark is a little agency.
For Māyā, producing difference from consciousness-filled <s>Śiva</s> for the bound soul,
brings about something like deep sleep; for that very reason he lacks vision and action.
