Kalā, through embracing the aṇu, produces a little agency.
And kalā itself is produced through their mutual anointing with the aṇu.
When separation of the soul arises from immediate nirvāṇa-initiation, kalā, though present,

children.text: śliṣyantyapi ca no sūte tathāpi svaphalaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: even while joined to it, does not at any time produce its own fruit in that way.
It is like a first swelling, or like a subtle sprout-phase,
which makes a seed germinate through contact with water, fire, earth, husk, and chaff.
This kalā, though born from the conjunction of Māyā and the aṇu, would not make
the unchanging aṇu the material cause, but rather Māyā, which is transformable.
Mala is the covering factor; Māyā is the material cause of entities.
Karma is only an assisting factor with regard to the arising of pleasure and pain.
Therefore, performing the function of strengthening concealed consciousness,
kalā alone, insentient but impelled by the power of <s>Anantanātha</s>, does this.
And the Lord's power alone will not strengthen his consciousness;
for if that were strengthened directly by it, it would not enter into limited agency.

children.text: seyaṃ kalā na karaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ vidyādikaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: This kalā is not the principal instrument, as vidyā and the others are.

children.text: puṃsi kartari sā kartrī prayojakatayā yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the person is the agent, kalā acts by way of instigation.
When, in this way, between the two indistinguishable entities, the person and kalā,
there arises an inner knowledge of the distinction from Māyā-garbha, the Lord's power, and so on,
then, through the exhaustion of all karma, discrimination between Māyā and the person occurs.
There is the state of a <s>vijñānākala</s>; below Māyā, the person does not go downward.
When discrimination between intellect and person, the difference between pradhāna and puruṣa, is known,

children.text: api na kṣīṇakarmā syāt kalāyāṃ taddhi saṃbhavet ||
children.translated_text: he may still not be one whose karma is exhausted; for that occurs at the level of kalā.

children.text: ataḥ sāṃkhyadṛśā siddhaḥ pradhānādho na saṃsaret
children.translated_text: Therefore, according to the Sāṃkhya view, one established below pradhāna does not transmigrate.
But when there is discrimination between kalā and the person, he certainly does not go below Māyā.
Seeing the self as distinct from mala, however, he attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
And everywhere the Lord's śaktipāta is the assisting cause here.
This one has authority in Māyā-garbha; but in the last two cases he is stainless.
This kalā is inferred to be different, precisely because of difference in its effects.
Otherwise the universe would be one; and to say 'it is for the sake of an effect' would deny the other.

children.text: iti mataṅgaśāstrādau yā proktā sā kalā svayam ||
children.translated_text: The kalā spoken of in the <s>Mataṅga</s> scripture and others is itself
agency, figuratively described as projecting it in the form of something limited.
How could agency qualified by some limited form belong to one who is ignorant?
Therefore it produces vidyā, whose nature is a little knowledge.
That vidyā sees the intellect, which moves in the mirror of intellect.
Pleasure and the other cognitions, delusion and the rest, in cause and effect,
and the network of karma situated there, it discriminates by its own nature.
But the intellect is mixed with the guṇas; how, by discrimination, could it reveal
an object as pleasant, painful, or consisting of delusion?
How could an entity, transferring its own reflection into the intellect, become an object of awareness
without that vidyā? And that too is another instrument, while the person is the agent.
Objection: Surely, because the intellect is like a mirror, pure on both sides,
an entity shines from the light of the person. Not so; that is its reflection.
For it is indeed chiefly inert; but its shining is the illumination belonging to the <s>puruṣa</s>.
And since that <s>buddhi</s> stands outside, what conceptual construction has been made of it?
This is the ground of non-difference, while difference is what is examined here.
Therefore the state that has entered <s>buddhi</s> is the sphere of the instrument called <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: bhāvānāṃ pratibimbaṃ ca vedyaṃ dhīkalpanā tataḥ
children.translated_text: And the reflection of entities is the knowable; from that comes the conceptual construction of the intellect.
Since it does something only slightly, surely there is another principle beyond it.
That which colors there itself is declared to be the <s>rāga</s>-tattva.
And that is not mere non-detachment, because even there it has the activity of attachment.
For even in detachment, a subtle <s>rāga</s> is established in one who is satisfied.
Therefore <s>kāla</s>, through instants and the like, determines this agency.
<s>Kāla</s> necessarily determines agency as delimited by an effect.
<s>Niyati</s> establishes ordering within a particular field of effects.
<s>Vidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>niyati</s>, and <s>kāla</s>: this fourfold set,
as the work of <s>kalā</s>, abides in the state of the enjoyer, filled with enjoyership.

children.text: māyā kalā rāgavidye kālo niyatireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kāla</s>, and <s>niyati</s>:
these are said to be the six <s>kañcukas</s> (limiting sheaths); when consciousness is situated in them, it is the <s>paśu</s>.
In bodies, the subtle body, and the rest, and in knowable objects, cognition
is contracted by this sixfold group; that one, the knower who is not knowable, is the <s>aṇu</s>.
This has been stated in the <s>Śivatanuśāstra</s>; the same matter is now given again in another manner:
Impurity is a covering that pervades everything; though other, it is also as if non-other in form.
Since it is burnable by the masses of rays of the fire that is <s>Śiva</s>, it is truly other in form.
Since, before any prior 'this'-objectification, it colors him by its own self, it is therefore non-other.
For the <s>aṇu</s> possessed of innate impurity, there is a threefold <s>kañcuka</s> from <s>Īśa</s> and <s>Guhā</s>.

children.text: tasya dvitīyacitiriva svacchasya niyujyate kalā ślakṣṇā ||
children.translated_text: For that transparent one, fine <s>kalā</s> is applied like a second consciousness.
By this, the <s>paśu</s> that is made distinct becomes capable of enjoyment.
And <s>vidyā</s> for him arose from <s>kalā</s>, like the gleam of a lamp within a shelter.
It distinguishes, by division, the cognition of pleasure and pain for the <s>paśu</s>.
And <s>rāga</s> arises from the <s>kalā</s>-tattva, like dye on a clean cloth.
For he does not wish to abandon the bliss of awareness in the pleasures of transmigration.
Thus, made impure by <s>avidyā</s> and empowered by the force of the three <s>guṇa</s>-<s>kañcukas</s>,
the <s>paśu</s>, helpless and downward-facing, falls into the womb of dense enjoyment.

children.text: etena malaḥ kathitaḥ kambukavadaṇoḥ kalādikaṃ tuṣavat ||
children.translated_text: By this, <s>mala</s> has been described: it is like a shell around the <s>aṇu</s>, while <s>kalā</s> and the rest are like husks.
Thus, in the particular aspect of the principle called <s>kalā</s>,
whose mark is doing something, agency has been discussed as preceded by enjoyership.
The 'somewhat' portion here that arises as a qualifier

children.text: vedyamātraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhinnaṃ pradhānaṃ sūyate kalā ||
children.translated_text: produces only the knowable, clearly differentiated, as <s>pradhāna</s>; that is <s>kalā</s>.

children.text: samameva hi bhogyaṃ ca bhoktāraṃ ca prasūyate
children.translated_text: For it gives birth at the same time to both the enjoyed and the enjoyer.
<s>Kalā</s>, through the intention toward difference, produces them mutually inseparable.
If they were mutually separated, there would be no state of being enjoyer and enjoyed.

children.text: vilīnāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ syānmāyāsyāpi na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: And when it is dissolved, even <s>māyā</s> has no reality here.
Objection: But in the venerable <s>Raurava</s> and similar texts, the pair consisting of <s>rāga</s> and <s>vidyā</s>
is produced by <s>kalā</s> simultaneously; from that comes the unmanifest. Such is the established position.

children.text: uktamatra vibhātyeṣa kramaḥ satyaṃ tathā hyalam
children.translated_text: Reply: This sequence has been stated here as it appears; true, for in this way it is sufficient:
while being colored, he knows everything; and while knowing, he is also colored here.
Nevertheless, the real existence of the thing has been analyzed here by us.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca na kramaḥ ko 'pi syādvā so 'pi viparyayāt ||
children.translated_text: And in that there is no sequence at all; or if there is, it may even be the reverse.
Therefore one should not create disagreement regarding the procedure taught in scripture.
Thus, whatever is merely to be cognized, because of pleasure, pain, and bewilderment,
and whatever will be enjoyed, is first said to have the nature of their equilibrium.

children.text: sukhaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśatvāt prakāśo hlāda ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Pleasure is <s>sattva</s>, because it is luminosity; luminosity is called delight.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ rajaḥ kriyātmatvād kriyā hi tadatatkramaḥ
children.translated_text: Pain is <s>rajas</s>, because it has action as its nature; for action is the sequence of this and that.
Bewilderment is <s>tamas</s>, the covering factor, because it is joined with absence of light.

children.text: ta ete kṣobhamāpannā guṇāḥ kārya pratanvate
children.translated_text: These <s>guṇas</s>, having become agitated, extend the effect.

children.text: akṣubdhasya vijātīyaṃ na syāt kāryamadaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: For from what is unagitated, this effect of a different class would not previously arise.
This very point has been stated; in this scripture they know the <s>guṇas</s> as another tattva.
Here a world is shown separately because of the distinction among the <s>guṇas</s>.
With respect to the <s>puruṣa</s>, made wavering and agitated by the will of <s>Īśvara</s>,
the autonomous Lord strongly agitates <s>prakṛti</s> for the sake of enjoyership.

children.text: tena yaccodyate sāṃkhyaṃ muktāṇuṃ prati kiṃ na sā
children.translated_text: Therefore the objection raised by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, 'Why does she not, with respect to a liberated <s>aṇu</s>,
produce effects, since the <s>puruṣa</s> would be subject to transformation?' is no obstacle here.

children.text: guṇebhyo buddhitattvaṃ tat sarvato nirmalaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: From the <s>guṇas</s> comes the <s>buddhi</s>-tattva, altogether stainless; then
the light of the <s>puruṣa</s>, as the knowable here, attains the condition of a reflection.
And the reflection of the object in it, produced by the senses, is external.
In acts such as supposition and intuition, a similar activity occurs without that channel.
The modification of <s>buddhi</s> is cognition, and that too is certainly a support.
It belongs to the light of self-awareness, though that cognition, being of <s>buddhi</s>, is also thoroughly inert.
From <s>buddhi</s> comes <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, when the nature of the reflected <s>puruṣa</s> is present
in a light stained by the knowable, as the state whose nature is the thinking 'I'.
By that, this fivefold <s>vāyu</s>, whose form is impulsive activity,
is set in motion for life; otherwise there is death again.
For this very reason, because pure selfhood has freedom and 'I' as its nature,
this other one is artificial; so it is expressed by the word <s>kṛti</s> ('making').
Thus this aggregate of instruments belonging to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> has been explained.
Its <s>prakṛti</s>-aggregate is threefold: sāttvic, rajasic, and tamasic.
From <s>ahaṃkāra</s> dominated by sattva, clearly touching the experiencer-aspect,
there arose the mind, the intellect, and the set of six sense-faculties; but their distinction is now stated.
Since mind has all objects as its field, what is meant here
is that <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> is qualified by being the producer of all the <s>tanmātras</s>.
They call intellect, <s>ahaṃkṛt</s>, and mind the instrument for the impulse toward cognition,
one not made by the external deities, nor indeed by those turned inward.
Nor is <s>prāṇa</s> an inner instrument, because it is insentient and has the nature of propulsion;
this is settled because it is the cause of effort, desire, and awakening.
Determination, self-appropriation, and imagination are not a single action;
therefore a threefoldness in the inner organ is clearly reasonable.
Nor is intellect unconscious merely because it is an instrument, as mind is;
therefore the doctrine that intellect is unconscious like <s>pradhāna</s> is rejected.
But the <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> that is specified by being the cause of the sound-<s>tanmātra</s>
is the instrument in the ear, and so on down to the nose, where it is indicated by smell-ness.
From this, materiality too may be accepted, sufficiently, because there is restriction among the objects;
yet in cognitions such as 'I hear,' 'I see,' and 'I smell,'
because the sense of I-ness follows along, their derivation from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is clearly established.
Therefore their being instruments is proper, because they are connected with contact with the agent's aspect.
If an instrument is different from the agent, since it has to be impelled, how could it be an instrument?
If another instrument were required there, an infinite regress would result.

children.text: tasmāt svātantryayogena kartā svaṃ bhedayan vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the possession of freedom, the agent differentiates his own body
and himself turns his own portion, touching the action-aspect, into an instrument.
Through the force of identifying with that own portion that has been made an instrument,
he makes even something completely separate into an instrument, like an axe.
Thus impure <s>vidyā</s> is first the general instrument for his knowing;

children.text: jñaptau kṛtau tu sāmānyaṃ kalā karaṇamucyate ||
children.translated_text: but in knowing and in acting, <s>kalā</s> is called the general instrument.
Objection: In the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s> and other scriptures, agency is stated of <s>kalā</s>.
For when it is present, <s>vidyā</s> and the rest become fit to have instrumentality.
Reply: The very agency that is stated is what makes instrumentality possible;

children.text: tayā vinā tu nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ sthitiryataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for without it the other instruments would have no established existence.
Therefore there it is treated separately from the class of non-general instruments;

children.text: vidyāṃ vinā hi nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ nijā sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for without <s>vidyā</s> the other instruments have no standing of their own.

children.text: kalāṃ vinā na tasyāśca kartṛtve jñātṛtā yataḥ
children.translated_text: And without <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s> too would not have knowership in its agency.

children.text: kalāvidye tataḥ puṃso mukhyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore they know <s>kalā</s> and <s>vidyā</s> as the principal instruments of the person.
For this very reason, even when someone lacks intellect and the organs of action,

children.text: andhe paṅgau rūpagatiprakāśo na na bhāsate ||
children.translated_text: as in a blind or lame person, the manifestation of form and movement does not fail to appear.
Rather, by the power of the general instrument, even with respect to such an object of knowledge,
the blind person attains apprehension of form in general alone.
From that same <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, more specifically touching the <s>tanmātras</s>,
the organs of action arose: speech, hand, anus, generative organ, and foot.
'I speak, I take, I quickly cast off, I excrete, and I go':

children.text: iti yāhaṃkriyā kāryakṣamā karmendriyaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: the I-making that is capable of an effect is precisely the organ of action.
Therefore even a man whose hand is cut off has a hand in the form of an organ of action;
its chief seat is the hand with five fingers as the further support.

children.text: mukhenāpi yadādānaṃ tatra yat karaṇaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: When grasping is done even with the mouth, the instrument established there

children.text: sa pāṇireva karaṇaṃ vinā kiṃ saṃbhavet kriyā ||
children.translated_text: is the hand itself as instrument; without it, how could action occur?
If that were absent, what purpose would even the intellectual and sensory faculties serve?
For seeing depends on an instrument, because it is an action; so it is said.

children.text: parairgamau tu karaṇaṃ neṣyate ceti vismayaḥ
children.translated_text: It is astonishing that others do not accept the instrument in going.
Going, throwing upward, and the like are the primary apprehension of action.
But in the grammarians' view, this action is again a quality.
Since action is pervaded by being preceded by an instrument, it is preceded by an instrument.
The claim that knowledge is not a taking up is plainly the full expansion of blindness.
Therefore they say that the organs of action, like the skin, are chiefly pervasive.
My teachers in the <s>Mataṅga</s> say that they operate in their own places.
Objection: But there are many other actions as well; for them
other instruments too should be stated, and thus there would be no fixed limit among the faculties.
Objection continued: Was this not refuted by <s>Kheṭapāla</s> and others? Not every means for actions

children.text: yatsādhanaṃ tadakṣaṃ syāt kiṃtu kasyāpi karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: would be a faculty, but only the means for some particular action.
This does not cool the burning thirst of the question we have raised.
For peacocks are not satisfied by waters that are mostly unclear and scant.
Reply: Here I give my answer, taught by the venerable <s>Śambhu</s>:
it has been strengthened by clear, generous consciousness and by flawless reasoning.
Here one thing is divided according to distinctions in the connection with action.
In that case the connection is fivefold; therefore there are five organs of action.
For casting off, for taking, and for accomplishing the twofold pair, apart from the pair,
there is also action outside for the sake of repose in one's own form; thus it is fourfold.
The instruments are the anus, hand, foot, and organ of generation; that is fourfold.

children.text: antaṃ prāṇāśrayaṃ yattu karmātra karaṇaṃ hi vāk
children.translated_text: But the action here whose end rests in <s>prāṇa</s> has speech as its instrument.
The varied operations of these in their effects have been stated in brief.

children.text: tadetadvyatiriktaṃ hi na karma kvāpi dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Indeed, no action distinct from this is seen anywhere.
For what purpose, then, should this lack of fixed limit for the faculties be imagined?
These faculties perform this cycle of duties without mutual confusion.

children.text: akṣāṇi sahavṛttyā tu buddhyante saṃkaraṃ jaḍāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But dull people, because they occur together, understand them as confused.
This class of faculties has been stated as arising from the rajasic <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
From the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> dominated by tamas, whose nature is to cover the experiencer-aspect,
there arose the set of five <s>tanmātras</s>, called <s>bhūtādi</s>, the cause of the elements.
the group of mind, intellect, cognitive senses, active senses, and the group of tanmātras.
Here the conjunction of rājasa ahaṃkāra is what connects the two.
Others, however, say that mind is born from rājasa ahaṃkāra, because
it is skilled in the movement of all the senses, light, and swift.

children.text: anye tu sāttvikāt svāntaṃ buddhikarmendriyāṇi tu ||
children.translated_text: But others think that the inner mind comes from the sāttvika ahaṃkāra, while the intellect and the organs of action
come from the rājasa ahaṃkāra, since they touch both the grasping and the grasped aspects.
The <s>Kheṭapālas</s>, however, think that the group of organs of action clearly
is born from rājasa ahaṃkāra, since action belongs to rajas.
But in the <s>Śrīpūrvaśāstra</s>, mind is said to come from the rājasa ahaṃkāra, and again, from the sāttvika,
all the senses. This view seems reasonable to us.
For, in the manifestation of the functions of the senses, whose operation is outward,
the power lies in direct apprehension, while that of mind lies in inward connection.
And it has been said by the teacher: mind, being subsequent determination, should perform
the activity consisting of the operation of the knower, resting on those two.
But the group of tanmātras arises from ahaṃkāra in which darkness predominates.
Here there is no dispute at all, since the process begins with the graspable object.
In earth, within the varied range of fragrances and the like,
the general property that is smell-ness is called the smell-tanmātra.

children.text: vyāpakaṃ tata evoktaṃ sahetutvāttu na dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: It is called pervasive for that very reason; but, because it has a cause, it is not permanent.
Since its disappearance is a concealment in its own cause, it is therefore not permanent.
The same application should be made to the tanmātras beginning with taste and ending with sound.
For the particulars must necessarily have an earlier state that is undifferentiated.
The sound-tanmātra, when stirred, bearing variegated forms of auditory modes,
becomes ether, whose sound has the nature of space, since it permits superimposition of what is denoted.
That very thing, through conjunction with the touch-tanmātra, reaches agitation
and becomes air; therefore here it has the nature of both sound and touch.
Others say that sound is the single quality of ether; that too is acceptable,

children.text: yato vāyurnijaṃ rūpaṃ labhate na vināmbarāt
children.translated_text: because air does not acquire its own form apart from ether.
Since each preceding element remains in each succeeding element,
for that very reason air and ether are remembered as mutually inseparable.
Sound and touch, when stirred together with form,
are said to be the fire-tattva, possessing three properties, in just the previous manner.
With those three together with fluid tastes come waters, and with smells comes earth; such is the sequence.
There the accumulation of qualities in earth and the other elements is established by direct perception.
For earth does not appear apart from the mass of properties such as smell and the rest,
just as, even for those who teach a duality of quality and qualified substance, this one thing,

children.text: citraṃ rūpaṃ paṭe bhāti kramāddharmāstathā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: a variegated form, appears in a cloth, and likewise the properties appear in sequence in earth.

children.text: yathā ca vistṛte vastre yugapadbhāti citratā
children.translated_text: And just as variegation appears all at once in an extended cloth,
so too earth appears to yogins with the totality of its properties.
Therefore earth has a variegated form consisting of smell and the rest down to sound.
Because of differences in means, it appears divided into sequential and non-sequential modes.
For that very reason a difference of cognition produced by sequential manifestation is spoken of.
The use of the sixth case, and likewise the relation of what is differentiated and what differentiates, come from a difference in cognition.

children.text: tena dharmātirikto 'tra dharmī nāma na kaścana
children.translated_text: Therefore here there is no possessor of properties at all apart from the properties.
There, in earth, smells, forms, and tastes may be of many kinds;
touch is produced by cooking and is neither hot nor cold, and sound is variegated.
In water there are whiteness, sweetness, coldness, and variegated sounds.
In fire there are white brightness, heat, and variegated sounds.
In air there is touch, not produced by cooking and neither cold nor hot, and sound is variegated.
In ether there is sound, having the nature of phonemic color, or else reflections of sound.

children.text: yattu na sparśavaddharmaḥ śabda ityādi bhaṇyate ||
children.translated_text: But what is said, namely that sound is not a property possessing touch and the like,
by the followers of <s>Kaṇāda</s>, contradicts one's own experience; by whom could it be accepted?
For what appears without being contradicted is simply, 'There is a sound in the drum.'
Nor, merely because it is a cause, is there cognition that it is the material receiver of that sound.
And in our view the ear, having ahaṃkāra as its cause, here and there
shares in its function and so adequately grasps sound in that place.
But he who says, 'The ear is space, differentiated by contact with the ear-cavity;
a sound born from sound arrives and produces cognition of sound,'
for him, even when there is a faint drum-sound within earshot,
how could there be the distant cognition, 'This hearing is over there'?
For a sound born from sound, arising as a far or near noise,
and located in the space of the ear, cannot have the nature of being far or near.
Nor is it reasonable that the first sound is pervasive to that extent.
If, while being intense for those situated there, it is heard by this person,
how could it be heard while faint, since it does not rest on another property?
And this has been refuted in many ways by others, so once more it is pointless.

children.text: nāyastaṃ patitāghātadāne ko hi na paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For who is not learned when it comes to striking one who has fallen and is already wounded?
But of these elements, earth and the rest, however many tattvas there were before,
that many, standing as superior through an increase of qualities, appear as pervaded.
This pervaded-and-pervading relation of the tattvas that has been shown

children.text: sā guṇādhikyataḥ siddhā na hetutvānna lāghavāt ||
children.translated_text: is established through superiority in qualities, not through being a cause and not through subtlety.

children.text: ahetunāpi rāgo hi vyāpto vidyādinā sphuṭam
children.translated_text: For rāga is plainly pervaded by vidyā and the rest, even though they are not its causes.
Since that without which a thing would not exist is called pervaded by it.

children.text: na lāghavaṃ ca nāmāsti kiṃcidatra svadarśane
children.translated_text: And in our doctrine there is no such thing here as subtlety.
Therefore the pervaded-and-pervading relation should clearly be known from superiority in qualities.

children.text: yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmādūrdhva ucyate
children.translated_text: For whatever is superior in qualities to something is said to be above it.
In the revered <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>, aboveness is clearly identified with being pervasive.
Therefore, beginning with <s>Śiva</s>-hood, taking up within its own self the nature of luminosity, certainly
the earth shines fully with the whole collection of properties belonging to the series of <s>tattvas</s>, which stand as pervading factors.
So too water and the others, whose sphere extends as far as the <s>Śakti</s>-tattva, have a body of that kind.

children.text: kiṃ tūttaraṃ śaktitayaiva tattvaṃ pūrva tu taddharmatayeti bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the distinction is this: the higher <s>tattva</s> is such by being <s>Śakti</s> itself, while the prior one is such by possessing its qualities.
This has been shown at length in the procedure concerning the <s>Anuttara</s>.
Therefore one who is discriminating and desires fuller detail should look there for it.
Thus the nature of the <s>tattva</s> has been properly illuminated.
Now the <s>kalā</s>-adhvan will be stated according to the glorious <s>Śāmbhava</s> command.
Just as, among the worlds previously described, each one follows its own group
and, being distinct from what is beyond it, is spoken of by the name '<s>tattva</s>',
so too, even among those <s>tattvas</s>, what consists in continuity within its own class
and is distinguished from another class is called <s>kalā</s> in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>.
Some again say that the very inward and extremely subtle power

children.text: tattvānāṃ sā kaletyuktā dharaṇyāṃ dhārikā yathā ||
children.translated_text: of the <s>tattvas</s> is called <s>kalā</s>, just as the sustaining power is present in earth.

children.text: atra pakṣadvaye vastu na bhinnaṃ bhāsate yataḥ
children.translated_text: In these two positions the reality does not appear to be different, because
a merely concomitant universal, as accepted by Naiyāyikas and the like, is not admitted here.
Others say that, in initiation and similar rites, for the sake of easy comprehension,
a class based on convention was fashioned by <s>Śiva</s>, and that is <s>kalā</s>.
And a convention made by the God of gods
does not lose ultimate significance; it is not false, nor is it the rise of some alien convention.
<s>Nivṛtti</s> is in the earth-tattva; <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> has the unmanifest as its range;

children.text: vidyā niśānte śāntā ca śaktyante 'ṇḍamidaṃ catuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vidyā</s> ends at <s>Niśā</s>, and <s>śāntā</s> ends at <s>Śakti</s>; this cosmic egg is fourfold.

children.text: śāntātītā śive tattve kalātītaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śāntātītā</s> is in the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva, while the supreme <s>Śiva</s> is beyond <s>kalā</s>.
For here neither classification, nor convention, nor even reckoning is appropriate
in the all-sided abode of the flashing forth of freedom.
Yet, by freedom, his own form, not fallen away from the quality of the knower,
for the establishment of the ultimate reality of instruction and immersion in that,
is clearly contemplated as the Lord brings it into the condition of being knowable.
For this reason, even in the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva, a connection with <s>kalā</s> is stated.
And what is called an egg is the cause for the stable ordering of the divisions of worlds.
They call that a covering, and it exists as far as the end of <s>Śakti</s>.
Although earlier a system of worlds was described even in the <s>tattva</s> called <s>Śiva</s>,
nevertheless, since that is unobstructed, no covering is possible in it.
Objection: Then, leaving aside earth, in <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Māyā</s>,
even though there too is unobstructedness, how can the egg come into being?
On this point our teachers say: since the pentad beginning with earth
appears directly as this world, there is nothing at all beyond it
as an object of knowledge, because of grossness and subtlety, and as a means of knowledge, because of instrumentality.
In the condition of the agent, because of the flashing forth of agency, it is plainly declared
that the thirty <s>tattvas</s> have difference as their nature; their non-difference is regarded as <s>Niśā</s>.
When the divisions such as being an effect and being an instrument dissolve,
they speak of the pentad ending in <s>Śiva</s> as a fully blossomed freedom.
And in the venerable <s>Kālottara</s> and similar scriptures this is repeatedly stated in this way:
'These five <s>tattvas</s> are those by which the entire world is pervaded.'
Therefore, in the body of the five mantras, they are spoken of as <s>Sadyojāta</s> and the rest,
ending with <s>Īśāna</s>; in each case they extend from earth through ether.
Thus the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva would be void, beyond the void, and unsupported.
But that which has the nature of complete non-division, independent and beautiful as consciousness,
they call the thirty-seventh <s>tattva</s>, known by the name <s>Paraśiva</s>.
When, according to the reasoning already stated, even for that a knowable state is imagined here,
then what remains uninterrupted is called the thirty-eighth.

children.text: na cānavasthā hyevaṃ syāddṛśyatāṃ hi mahātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in this way there is no infinite regress; let the great ones see this.
Whatever appears as something knowable, when that has ceased, what shines forth
is determined to be that very <s>tattva</s>; the thirty-sixth shines in the heart.
When, under the force of the question, 'Is that nothing, or is it something?', its body
is taught to be only consciousness, bliss, and freedom,
then the thirty-seventh shines forth, and there no further question remains.

children.text: taccāpi kﾱptavedyatvaṃ yatra bhāti sa cinmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And where even that appears as having been made into an object of knowledge, that one is consciousness itself;
he is the thirty-eighth, and he too is taught for the sake of contemplation.

children.text: yadi nāma tataḥ saptatriṃśa eva punarbhavet ||
children.translated_text: If, from that, he should perhaps again become only the thirty-seventh,
the possession of qualities such as non-division, freedom, and being consciousness itself
is just the same; only being made knowable is something additional.
In the earth, up to the end of the <s>guṇa</s>-tattvas, and up to the end of <s>Māyā</s>, there are successively
smell, taste, and form, according to an inward sequence of increasingly subtle being.
Given this principle, even up to the end of the <s>Śakti</s>-tattva there is something partaking of subtlety:

children.text: sparśaḥ ko 'pi sadā yasmai yoginaḥ spṛhayālavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a certain touch, for which yogins are always longing.
At the limit of that touch there is awareness, whose form is the pure sky of consciousness;
one who is established in it reaches the supreme one, whose nature is self-luminosity.
Therefore there is <s>bindu</s>, therefore <s>nāda</s>; from this comes form, and from this, taste.

children.text: ityuktaṃ kṣobhakatvena spande sparśastu no tathā ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been said because these are exciters in <s>spanda</s>; touch, however, is not so.
And this is the doctrine of <s>Maheśa</s>, which he proclaimed in the venerable <s>Pūrva</s> scripture:
with words such as 'supporting,' 'satisfying,' 'knowing,' 'purifying,' and 'granting space,'
he describes the own nature of <s>nivṛtti</s> and the other <s>kalās</s>.
The rule of the five <s>tattvas</s> has been stated; now the three-<s>tattva</s> scheme is explained.
The <s>ātman</s>-principle extends as far as the <s>vijñānākala</s>; the <s>vidyā</s>-principle as far as the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>.
For the remainder, in the three Śiva-tattvas, in the one-tattva scheme <s>Śiva</s> would be supreme.
These two distinctions are both made only by the difference of tattvas.
Thus this is precisely the tattva-adhvan; and in this way there is no damage to the arrangement of the six adhvans.
Prakṛti, puruṣa, niyati, kāla, māyā, vidyā, īśa, sadāśiva,
and <s>Śiva</s>: even in the procedure of nine tattvas there is the form of the tattva-adhvan.
In the same way, in the procedure called eighteenfold too, the wise man should state the principle.
For wherever there is the desire for enjoyment, because that predominance is useful,
and because the others are included within it, initiation comes to possess endless differentiations.
Therefore there may be a procedure from thirty-six tattvas down to a single tattva.
This, in brief and in detail, has been declared by the God to be the tattva-adhvan itself.
And this one-tattva procedure was taught by <s>Śambhu</s> with reference to a thoroughly awakened guru
and a disciple whose hope for enjoyment has departed; for that reason it was stated.
Again and again expanding difference by his <s>Śakti</s>, whose form is free and self-willed,
the Lord remains, eternally bringing it to rest in his own non-different self.
In this way the division of the threefold adhvan, according to gross, subtle, and supreme status,
has been stated as belonging to the measured portion, consisting of pura, tattva, and kalā.
Now the form situated in the portion of the measuring subject is determined in three ways.
The form of the adhvan that has the nature of a means of knowledge and belongs to the measuring-subject portion
is called pada, because it enters into the state of cognition.

children.text: tadeva ca padaṃ mantraḥ prakṣobhātpracyutaṃ yadā
children.translated_text: And that very pada is mantra when it has slipped from agitation,
because the measuring subject is a hidden speaker, established as silent.

children.text: tathāpi na vimarśātma rūpaṃ tyajati tena saḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, he does not abandon the form whose nature is reflective awareness; therefore it
has the nature of reflective awareness as a means of knowledge, but it does not, like an ordinary knower, partake of agitation.

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ ca padānāṃ ca tenoktaṃ trikaśāsane
children.translated_text: Therefore in the <s>Trika</s> teaching it has been said of mantras and padas
that in the supreme condition their own form is not different, whether motionless or agitated.
When neutrality is abandoned and agitation has descended,

children.text: varṇādhvā mātṛbhāge syāt pūrvaṃ yā kathitā pramā ||
children.translated_text: the varṇa-adhvan is in the measuring-subject portion; the cognition that was previously described
is without division, since it has the nature of fullness.
From that, after making each single phoneme, beginning with earth, in each tattva,

children.text: kṛtvā śaive pare proktāḥ ṣoḍaśārṇā visargataḥ
children.translated_text: the sixteen phonemes ending with visarga are taught in the supreme Śaiva state.
There the vibration of <s>Śakti</s> is just so much, and it was explained before.
Now everything is gathered together and stated for easy understanding.
One pada, one mantra, one phoneme, the sixteen puras, and earth: this is nivṛtti.
The other has the tattvas and phonemes counted by fire and eye, the puras counted by taste and arrow, and an astra, a mantra, and a pada.
The other kalā has the tattvas and phonemes counted by sages, two padas and mantras, and the bhuvanas counted by Vasus and eyes.
The fourth has the tattvas and phonemes counted by fires, one pada and mantra, and the bhuvanas counted as an army.
Śāntyatītā consists of sixteen phonemes, and of one pada, mantra, and tattva.
These three āryā verses have been spoken by <s>Abhinavagupta</s> for the sake of summary for his pupils.
This whole adhvan, then, has the activity of non-difference from <s>Bhairava</s>,
and it appears as attaining freedom because of his autonomy.
Thus, when it is situated in the form of the measuring subject, it has been determined as the mantra-adhvan.
For when the state of what is denoted is swallowed by conscious reflective awareness,
intent on thinking and protecting, dependent on <s>Śiva</s>'s knowledge and action,
through its skill in delighting in the play of the entire host of powers,
consciousness, fallen away from the form made of measure, reaches the state of the mantra-adhvan.
Having come to the form of a means of knowledge, it proceeds to the adhvan whose nature is pada.
For the resting of the measuring subject gathers together those many phonemes,
and that gathering is sequential and has the nature of speech-expression.
Its own form, that of determinate conception, is clearly made of immersion in enjoyment.
Therefore our guru called pada the form of a means of knowledge.
Without abandoning its entrance into the form of a means of knowledge, and going toward objecthood
through conjunction with kalana, the adhvan is called kalātmaka, consisting of kalā.
In pure conjunction with knowability, when it takes on the share of subtlety and grossness,
the guru should follow it in sequence as the tattva-adhvan and the bhuvana-adhvan.
The form of the knowable, the means of knowledge, and the knowers, which is situated above,
this adhvan, standing here merely as cognition and consisting of phonemes, should indeed be seen.
For yogins who taste repose in the mere consciousness that rises up,
the powers are unrestricted because of their capacity for every expression.
Created in an object that rises together with their own self and extends as far as earth,
touching so many objects on the ground of their own consciousness as non-different,
those streams of phonemes bear true consciousness in the form of cognition.
Even children and animal knowers, who have no share in convention,
through the essence of natural impressions, rest upon this very consciousness of their own,
divided in many different ways, and attain manifold forms of knowing subjecthood.
And if conventions become established in this natural, infinite phonemic consciousness,
then they too come to function without convention.

children.text: anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But without this, all conventions, even when made many times,
because they lack repose, would produce an infinite regress that is very hard to cross.
For when a child is instructed by seeking the path of convention there,
even in pointing with a finger, his understanding is not in that way free from determinate conception.
Determinate conception has word as its root, and word lives by convention.
Therefore such an infinite aggregate of phonemes, not belonging to māyā,
always expands, accompanied by conscious reflective awareness.

children.text: yata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire
children.translated_text: And precisely from it the māyīya phonemes spread forth creation;
and those that are described as potency among the māyīya phonemes,
independent of convention, should be accepted as cognition.
For thus, when the words of others are heard, one's own

children.text: pramā yasya jaḍo 'sau no tatrārthe 'bhyeti mātṛtām
children.translated_text: valid cognition is covered; the inert person for whom this is so does not attain subjecthood with respect to that object.
Like a parrot, he merely recites, possessing only what has been handed down by another in sequence.
But through gaining autonomy, when valid cognition arises in one's own speech, there is true knowing.
For the one who has awakened to his own valid cognition, by bringing forth and checking the opposing side,
becomes a knower and master over his own mass of phonemes, beginning with sentences.
To whatever degree that unmade form expands,
to that same degree gradations of <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) are discerned.
When the later and later convention is immersed within the first <s>māyīya</s> phoneme,
and when, in convention, each earlier portion is submerged, there arise divisions of <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive illumination).
Even when the greatness of the first expansion is present, those established in the nature of <s>pratibhā</s>
certainly come, in every way, to possess poetic and oratorical power.
What does one whose awareness rests in the conscious realm,

children.text: viśrāntaścinmaye kiṃ kiṃ na vetti kurute na vā
children.translated_text: freed from the construction of convention, not know, and what does he not do?

children.text: ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, for perfection in speech, the phonemes are to be worshipped.

children.text: sarvajñatvādisiddhau vā kā siddhiryā na tanmayī
children.translated_text: Or, for the accomplishment of omniscience and the like, what accomplishment is there that is not composed of them?
Thus it has been said by <s>Varada</s> in the <s>Śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmata</s>:

children.text: tena guptena guptāste śeṣā varṇāstviti sphuṭam
children.translated_text: 'By that hidden one the remaining phonemes are hidden' - this is plain.
Thus, that sixfold <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic path) which appears through knowerhood, means-of-knowledge, and objecthood,
attains purification when its own body is purified.
When purification has been effected in one body, then right there
the attentive guru should perform purification by including the other modes within it.

children.text: anantarbhāvaśaktau tu sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: But when there is no power of inclusion, he should purify each subtle level successively.
When that is purified, because it has become seed-like, it does not produce any further continuation.
Purification is manifold: single-pointedness toward obtaining each respective enjoyment,
mastery over that, abandonment of that, recognition of its identity with <s>Śiva</s>,
absorption into it, rejection of it - all this may occur sequentially or non-sequentially.

children.text: ata eva ca te mantrāḥ śodhakāścitrarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: For this very reason those mantras, as purifiers, are varied in form.
In <s>Siddhānta</s>, <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and the rest, they spread out a varied purification.
But the non-sequential mantras called those of the <s>Anuttaratrika</s>, indeed,

children.text: te sarve sarvadāḥ kintu kasyacit kvāpi mukhyatā ||
children.translated_text: all bestow everything at all times; yet for someone, somewhere, one may be primary.
Therefore, in their role as purifiers, in the scripture called <s>Śrīpūrva</s>,
the mantras beginning with <s>Parāparā</s> are arranged along the <s>adhvan</s>.

children.text: śodhakatvaṃ ca mālinyā devīnāṃ tritayasya ca
children.translated_text: And the purificatory function belongs to <s>Mālinī</s>, to the triad of goddesses,
to the triad of gods, to the faces, and to the set of eight limbs.
Why say too much? In the sequence of gateways, dwelling, support, and guru,
and in the rite of the world-protectors and weapons, apart from the mantras, everything is purificatory.

children.text: yaccaitadadhvanaḥ proktaṃ śodhyatvaṃ śoddhṛtā ca yā
children.translated_text: And this being-to-be-purified of the <s>adhvan</s>, and the purifierhood that has been taught,
is fitting through autonomy in non-difference from <s>Śiva</s>; so too it has been stated in the teaching.
All this certainly shines in the supreme Lord
in the form of a reflection, and not as something external, because
within the sky of consciousness alone, <s>Śiva</s>, there is this sort of cognition of particular bodies and the like.
For bound beings it is differentiated, like the cognition of a snake, garland, or wave in a rope.
Therefore the doctrine of a prior body, death, and so on belongs to the sphere of dream.
At death, what sort of production of another body and the like could there be?
Even in a dream, by the force of a mere general manifestation of <s>pratibhā</s>,

children.text: viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante 'pi te yathā ||
children.translated_text: particular things appear, even though they are not deliberately imagined.
Just as some <s>śālagrāma</s> stones bear variegated shapes,
so too, as designs within the levels from <s>māyā</s> down to earth, consciousness holds pictures
such as cities, oceans, and mountains, conforming to its will.
For us, these are not in themselves existent or nonexistent, nor are they of the nature of causes or non-causes.
Because firmly rooted <s>niyati</s> (necessity) can be cut off and set in motion,
and because the unrooted is subject to autonomy, this <s>Bhairava</s>, the sky of consciousness, stands free.
In one who shares in non-difference from <s>Bhairava</s>, complete as nothing but a single consciousness,
the unreflective notion, 'I am thus,' is what divides within the circle of phenomena.
Just as in a dream no other agent is established by any means of knowledge,
so everywhere this should be understood from self-established self-awareness.
One who knows thus plays in the city-garden painted by consciousness, thinking,
'I myself stand here as the cities of the <s>tattvas</s> of beings and entities.'
Thus the varied notions, 'I have been born' and 'I have died,'
appear, self-created, on the wall of mind, although there is no birth and no death.
The other world is only consciousness here, and this world is present as this world in the other world.

children.text: vastutaḥ saṃvido deśaḥ kālo vā naiva kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: In reality, for consciousness there is no space or time whatsoever.
If this creation were material and not made of consciousness,
then from within it who could perceive even a single mountain?
In the sequence of support and supported among the class of elements, subtle elements, and so on,
at the end there is the power made of consciousness, the bearer, which is itself the form of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tasmātpratītirevetthaṃ kartrī dhartrī ca sā śivaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore cognition alone, in this way, is the maker and the supporter; she is <s>Śiva</s>.
Hence entities are entities within her; therefore power is the supporting principle.
Something imagined, though without a support, does not fall downward at all.
Thus the universe should be reflected upon as resting in its own supporting power.
Her dense fixed conviction beginning with 'I am' is precisely earth and the rest,
until, at the end, the realization 'I am consciousness' is completed as the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>.
As blue and other colors are appearances in a rainbow-jewel, so are these in <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayo na vyayaḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: But in ultimate reality there is nowhere any arising or disappearance of these.
The claim that creation occurs here in space or in time is incoherent.

children.text: cidātmanā hi devena sṛṣṭir dikkālayor api ||
children.translated_text: For creation of direction and time too is by the god whose nature is consciousness.
In what is regarded as waking, within a range of three and a half hands,
and separately within a watch of time, dreams have varied measures of direction and time.

children.text: ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcidapi manmahe
children.translated_text: Therefore we do not suppose that there is anything at all called a moment;
or even in a single moment of action, there might be many rapid actions.
Thus those who accepted the contraction of entities as ending in a moment
surely rely on this <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) of the doctrine of emptiness.

children.text: tadya eṣa sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkartuṃ tathāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, he who by his freedom is able to make existent things void
and to make nonexistent things manifest is <s>Śiva</s>, the Lord, our master.
Thus the supreme Lord is proclaimed as having the universe as his form;
but no separate thing, such as earth and the rest, is reasonably established.
And this was said earlier, so it is not examined again;
and further refutations of external objects have also been left aside.
Thus this expanse of the <s>adhvan</s> (course), beginning with <s>kalā</s>, has been determined.
Now the practical use of this <s>adhvan</s> under discussion is made clear.
This entire <s>adhvan</s>, in the way it is established in consciousness,
is, through that consciousness, also established in void, intellect, breath, channels, wheels, and bodies,
and externally too in the <s>liṅga</s>, image, fire, altar, and so on, everywhere.
It is established both as a whole and separately, in sequence and without sequence.
This <s>adhvan</s>, arranged from the consciousness-principle out to the external,

children.text: tatra tatrocitaṃ rūpaṃ svaṃ svātantryeṇa bhāsayet ||
children.translated_text: should, in each place, make its own appropriate form shine by its freedom.

children.text: sarvaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ ca tasyāpi na na bhāsate
children.translated_text: And every form everywhere appears for that too;
for we cannot bear limitation anywhere, even in dream.
Thus one should behold the body as filled with the universal <s>adhvan</s>, variegated by the activity of time,
as the abode of <s>spanda</s> (vibration) made of place and time.
When thus beheld, that body, made of the deities within the universe,
should be meditated upon, worshipped, and satisfied; one who is possessed by that is liberated.

children.text: itthaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pustakaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: In this way, a pot, a cloth, a <s>liṅga</s>, an altar, a book, water,
or whatever one sees anywhere, one should enter into identity with that there.
For the offering of objects there, in non-difference, is considered worship,
and the contemplation of their complete form is called meditation.
Bringing the contemplation of completeness to unshaken firmness,
and reflecting by means of inner muttering, one becomes fit for <s>japa</s> (recitation).
Dissolving the particular differences of the entities offered there,
one intent on the act of <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) should offer their real nature as rays.
For one who acts thus, seeing everything with equal vision,
steadfastness is the pure vow, the equality taught in <s>Nandiśikhā</s>.
Thus, according to the sequence of ritual worship, recitation, meditation, fire-offering, and vow,

children.text: paripūrṇāṃ sthitiṃ prāhuḥ samādhiṃ guravaḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: the ancient gurus have called the complete state <s>samādhi</s> (absorption).
Here, in worship, recitation, and the rest, whether situated externally, internally, or in both ways,

children.text: dravyaughe na vidhiḥ ko 'pi na kāpi pratiṣiddhatā ||
children.translated_text: there is no rule at all concerning the mass of substances, and no prohibition of any kind.
There is no use here for imagined purity, twilight rites, and the like.

children.text: uktaṃ śrītrikasūtre ca jāyate yajanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: And it is said in the venerable <s>Trikasūtra</s> with regard to worship:
'One who knows no rule and one who knows rule,' and so on, in great detail.

children.text: yadā yathā yena yatra svā saṃvittiḥ prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: Whenever, however, by whatever, and wherever one's own awareness becomes clear and pleased,

children.text: tadā tathā tena tatra tattadbhogyaṃ vidhiśca saḥ
children.translated_text: then, in that way, by that, and there, that particular enjoyandum is the rule.
Therefore one should employ here everything, ordinary and extraordinary alike.
When there is unsteadiness instead of steadiness, one should forcibly diminish the tremor,
by whatever means, gradually or even all at once.
In whatever way hesitation melts away inside, one should apply oneself diligently in that way.
One should satisfy the goddesses belonging to intellect, action, and the senses precisely with forbidden things.
And one should approve the heroic vow: this is the statement of <s>Bhargaśikhā</s>.

children.text: tathāhi śaṅkā mālinyaṃ glāniḥ saṃkoca ityadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For doubt, impurity, dejection, contraction, and the like
become like thick posts inside the prison-house of saṃsāra.
Those mantras whose nature is phonemes, that substance which is made of the five elements,

children.text: yaccidātma prāṇijātaṃ tatra kaḥ saṃkaraḥ katham
children.translated_text: and the race of living beings whose self is consciousness: what mixture could there be among these, and how?
Since there is no mixture, what is this doubt? Even with respect to that, clearly,
one should not doubt; rather, doubt should dissolve through disdain.
In scriptures such as <s>Śrīsarvācāravīrālī</s>, <s>Niśācāra</s>, and the <s>Krama</s> texts,
this is set forth at length, since it is stated in place after place.
Through doubt dejection arises; through doubt one becomes a vessel for obstacles.
And the venerable <s>Utpaladeva</s>, the teacher of our teacher, said:
'We praise that <s>Māheśvara</s> path, a thunderbolt against all doubts.'
For the attainment of the unsurpassed state, this <s>āṇava</s> means, with the method shown at great length, has now been taught; learned ones, understand it.
Now, for the accomplishment of <s>putrakatva</s> (the status of a ritual son), the rite taught by <s>Śiva</s> is described here.
But when the preceptor wishes to appoint one who is established in the commitments
to <s>putrakatva</s>, to the state of a guru, or to the state of a sādhaka,
then, having performed the preliminary consecration, on the second day he should draw the maṇḍala,
whether in a communal sacrifice or elsewhere, just as prescribed.
With the numbers six, eight, twice that, and twenty-four,
the group of five wheels is taught in the scripture called <s>Śrīpūrva</s>.
According to the revered <s>Traiśirasa</s>, there are thirty-two and twice that number;
in texts such as the <s>Śrīsiddha</s>, connection with countless wheels is described.
Therefore, in whatever way the sacrifice is measured by however many wheels,
one should worship by means of that; here one should draw a set of three tridents.
In the threefold set of tridents, the three goddesses are placed in alternating order.
It will have been worshiped completely, without distinction among the middle, the left, and the other positions.
The procedure of the maṇḍala will now be taught briefly at the front of the maṇḍala.
Having drawn the maṇḍala, one should wipe it with a scented cloth.
Having done this, the guru, bathed as before, should stand before the maṇḍala; here he should worship the deities
who are outside, and at the doorway he should worship the door-deities.
In front of the maṇḍala, then, beginning with the northeast quarter in order
and ending with the southeast, he should worship <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and the others, down to <s>Kṣetrapa</s>.
Those called <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Guru</s>, <s>Parama</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhī</s>, <s>Pūrvasiddha</s>, <s>Vāk</s>, and <s>Kṣetrapati</s>
are declared to be the seven to be worshiped, according to our gurus, in the rite of the guru-line.
Then, having received permission, with flowers, incense, and the other articles offered in worship,
one should fully worship <s>Ādhāraśakti</s> and the rest, beginning from the root of the trident
and ending with <s>Śiva</s> at the end of the white lotus, in order on the three tridents.
On the middle trident, in the middle position, there should be <s>Sadbhāva</s> together with <s>Parā</s>.

children.text: vāme cāparayā sākaṃ navātmā dakṣagaṃ param
children.translated_text: On the left, together with <s>Aparā</s>, is <s>Navātman</s>; the supreme one occupies the right.
On the right trident, standing on the middle peak, is <s>Ratiśekhara</s>.
He should be together with <s>Parāparā</s>; on the right is <s>Bhairava-Satpara</s>.
On the left trident, in the middle, <s>Navātman</s> should be together with <s>Aparā</s>.

children.text: syātpare parayā sākaṃ vāmāre saṃśca bhairavaḥ
children.translated_text: In the supreme position he should be together with <s>Parā</s>, and on the left side is <s>Bhairava</s>.
When <s>Śrīparādevī</s> is thus established as all-pervasive,
the worship becomes fully complete merely through her presiding presence.
Therefore, even in worship on a single trident, one should contemplate it as presided over by her.
Thus it is stated in the <s>Trīśikā</s>: 'The one ignorant of the rule is one who knows the rule.'

children.text: tato madhye tathā dakṣe vāme śṛṅge ca sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the middle, likewise on the right, on the left peak, and everywhere,
one should worship, as having a single self, all the way to the world-protectors and the weapons.
And one should worship all the deities as supreme.
One should worship the glorious, stainless Lord <s>Mātṛsadbhāva</s>.
After that too, by the worship of enjoyment, one should worship the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>, the limbs of the vidyā,
the <s>Yāmala</s>, and the circle-goddesses outside, each in its own place.
With fragrances, flowers, wine, and the like, one should worship the world-protectors together with their weapons,
with supreme devotion and free from miserliness about wealth.
Then, through the contemplation of nonduality, one should make the conjunction
of the five: the pot, the weapon-jar, the maṇḍala, the place, and the self.

children.text: ye tu tāmadvayavyāptiṃ na vindanti śivātmikām ||
children.translated_text: But those who do not attain that nondual pervasion whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>
enter the nondual path through the application of the mantra-channel.
Going out by his own right side, and entering by the left side of what is in the maṇḍala,
then going out by the other side and entering what is in the pot, in the pitcher,
and in the fire, in this sequence, until, in himself, on his own left side,
by the force of connection with the root, the thread of breath is held fast,
in this way the consciousness of pervasion shines forth, its nature a flashing unity.
Then he should perform the special worship, conceived as nondual.
For whatever is sprinkled with the nectar of nondual <s>Śiva</s>, that indeed is supreme.
Through that, with respect to the argha, flowers, fragrances, wine, and then the sacrificial beast,
the vision of identity with nondual <s>Śiva</s> is purification and supreme consecration.
Before the Lord he should offer living beings and the bodily constituents that arise from them,
whether perfected, unperfected, mixed, or whatever else is moving or unmoving.
The heroic sacrificial beast, seen, sprinkled, looked upon by the beholder, touched, taken up, and joined,
and finally extinguished, is eightfold, each later form superior to the former.
The higher form in each case must never be given to those who are unfit.
For an oblation used by <s>Śiva</s> is not fit for everyone to consume.
But one who, even without initiation, is impelled by <s>Śiva</s>'s will and rule
and eats it with devotion becomes complete, a well-disposed samayin.
'Seen' and 'looked upon' mean that it has been offered by sight inflamed with rays.
'Sprinkled' means merely moistened with drops from the argha-vessel.
The 'beholder' is one to whom the whole properly worshiped maṇḍala has been shown.
The 'touched' one, consecrated by the three just mentioned, should also shake,
tremble, flow, become rigid, or dissolve, each state higher than the last.
The 'taken up' one is calmed in the nearness of the worship by the winds of the weapon.
The 'joined' one is united with <s>Śiva</s> by the sequence of abandoning the causes.
The 'extinguished' one is such through practiced offering of the guru's breath and mind.
By the southern fire, it is so through the dissolution of the network of gentle kalās.
Thus, at the beginning, one should resort to the supreme form as a unity.
Therefore, by the fiery procedure, one should enter the garland of flames that it emits.
By the beast's left side, one should melt the net of moonbeams with heat.
Then one should rest in the navel-wheel together with the host of rays of breath.

children.text: paro bhūtvā svaśaktyātra jīvaṃ jīvena veṣṭayet ||
children.translated_text: Having become supreme, one should here envelop the individual soul with the individual soul by means of one's own power.
Heating it with the sun of one's own consciousness, one should liquefy each kalā.
Then, bringing the melted network of kalās into unity within oneself,
complete with all the tattvas and producing replenishment,
one should violently uproot this one, bound by karma, from the fluid essence.
Then, through the procedure of uprooting and unwinding, turning leftward,
serving his own breath, filled with the nectar of <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>,
and taking up, in leftward sequence, the nectar-filaments of the heart-lotus,
by gaining ascent to the heart's pericarp, he should dissolve the vital essence,
the pure lunar essence, slightly reddish-yellow,
and, taking it into a body of breath like the tip of an elephant's trunk,
he should go out at once and enter by the left path of his own self.
With that essence he should satisfy the deity-circle
which stands in the heart-lotus of the lunar wheel called apāna, while replenishing it.
By this procedure he should gather all of them, the <s>rasa</s> and blood and the rest,
the bodily constituents, according to the sequence of their aggregate, or else one by one.
Or else he should draw only the living principle that lies in the midst of the conjunction of fire, moon, and sun,
having the form of light and called the power of breath.
Through visualization he should make that living principle one in essence with the circle of goddesses.
That alone is the chief <s>tarpaṇa</s> (satiating offering); she herself is the identity of the enjoyed and the enjoyer.
The great mass, whose nature is the triangle of time, the blossoming flood enclosed by fire,
is used for setting in motion, drawing forth, and the like, the streams of essence such as blood.
Thus, when the sequence lasts half a <s>ghaṭikā</s> through the yoga of repose,
with a hundred repetitions the extinguishing of the <s>paśu</s> comes about.
Having practiced there for some time, with undivided mind,

children.text: yathā cintāmaṇau proktaṃ tena rūpeṇa yogavit
children.translated_text: in the form taught in the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, the knower of yoga
attains accomplishment without fear. This is plainly to be guarded as one guards one's life.
Even when the <s>paśu</s> is remote, this procedure applies for each <s>yojana</s>.
If he has been brought into the sacrificial ground, killed there, and consecrated there itself,
and if he is also attended by the circle there, he is called a heroic <s>paśu</s>.
But one who has been killed elsewhere, whether wholly or even in part,
and is offered to the deity, is regarded as an external <s>paśu</s>.
Kingship, gain, the stability of that gain, devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, identity with him,
knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, attainment of the world of mantras, membership in his retinue,
and union with him belong to the <s>paśu</s>, by reason of the likeness between the external and the rest and the heroic mode.
Even flowers and the like share in those gains through worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
The Lord of gods, whose nature is the favoring of the universe, by a single means,
namely by sacrifice alone, favors everything whatever, moving and unmoving.
Therefore even one who is not a hero, who is full of doubt and also compassionate,
should never form the idea of violence in the rite concerning a <s>paśu</s>.
This is a great benefit to the <s>paśu</s>, although at that moment it may be unpleasant.
The example here is the application of cutting, medicine, and austerity for a disease.
It is said in the venerable <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> that, when the bonds of the <s>paśu</s> have been cut,
because of separation from the three impurities, the body does not sprout again.
Since the mass of merit and demerit has been severed, the body is said to fall away.
Therefore this is not called killing; this initiation is manifold in form.

children.text: rūḍhapāśasya yaḥ prāṇairviyogo māraṇaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: For killing is the separation from the breaths of one whose bonds have taken root.
But this is only the joining of the <s>paśu</s> to the deity in the satiating offering.
Therefore, relying on the deity's statement, one should offer many <s>paśus</s>.
Once offered, he obtains a body again and is offered again.

children.text: ṣaṭkṛtva itthaṃ yaḥ so 'tra ṣaḍjanmā paśuruttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The one who is thus offered six times is here the excellent <s>paśu</s> of six births.
He is said to be like gold purified by a process of smelting.

children.text: kāṃ siddhiṃ naiva vitaretsvayaṃ kiṃvā na mucyate ||
children.translated_text: What accomplishment would he not bestow, or why would he himself not be liberated?
But it is said in the <s>Ānandaśāstra</s>: one who, though possessing mantra-consecration, abandons it,
reviles the observances and the goddesses, or gives mantras without proper rule,
and, having received initiation, mantras, and the rest, abandons them because deluded by sons and the like,
then, having come to human birth, does the same again.
In this way that two-footed being, whose births extend from one up to seven, is of two kinds;
or, as a four-footed <s>paśu</s>, he is born for the oblation of the goddess.
Offered by the giver, through that offering he goes to <s>Śiva</s> by way of union.
Thus, reflecting on the strange behavior of <s>paśus</s>,
one should not use elsewhere a <s>paśu</s> that is intended to be made an object of enjoyment.
Nor should one reject that <s>paśu</s>, thinking, 'This one is not fit.'

children.text: taṃ paśuṃ kiṃtu kāṅkṣā cedviśeṣe taṃ tu ḍhaukayet
children.translated_text: Rather, if there is a desire for a special result, one should present that very one.
One should offer that many <s>paśus</s>; so too it has been stated by the Great Lord.
When the omentum and fat of the <s>paśu</s> have been melted in the midst of the fire,
one should offer them to the circle of powers; this is regarded as the supreme satiating offering.
One should offer especially the heart, entrails, head, shoulders, and liver,
or, as still more important, the pericarp, the coiling channel, the marrow, and the ribs.
Then the teacher should perform the satiating offering of the mantra-circle in the fire.
And, having offered that to the deity, he should then make his declaration to the Lord:
'By you yourself, as guru, I have been commanded, O Supreme Lord.
Through direct instruction in dream, through recitations, or through the mouth of the guru,
the disciples impelled by <s>Śiva</s>'s power are to be favored by you.
These such persons have now arrived; grant favor to them.
Enter me with the rays of your own self, so that I am <s>Śiva</s>.'
Then he should affirm the utterance of <s>Śiva</s>, 'So be it.'
Next he should contemplate himself as non-different from <s>Śiva</s>, the performer of the five acts.
For the sake of granting favor, he should contemplate his own instruments, the mantras, and the embodied form.
Then, after binding on a white turban, he should worship them in due order on his hands,
for the burning of each other's bonds and for the emission of the pure principles.
In the form of light he should worship the mantras in the hands of <s>Śiva</s>.
Afterwards he should contemplate himself, freed from the covering of the womb, the limbs, retinue, and seat,
as solitary, like the moon in water.
Though divided because of the limiting adjuncts of the functions, he is in reality undivided in six ways.
'This one standing in the <s>maṇḍala</s> is I myself, and I am the witness of all rites.

children.text: śuddhā hi draṣṭṛtā śambhormaṇḍale kalpitā mayā ||
children.translated_text: For the pure seeing of <s>Śambhu</s> has been imagined by me in the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
As the locus of the oblation, I am situated in the fire.
The mantras, whose own nature is kindled, are sufficient for the rite of burning the bonds.
The <s>Bhuvaneśvaras</s>, invoked into the inner common form of light,
when satisfied and made to hear, do not extend authority over the individual soul.
Until the end of the sacrifice I remain established in the jar for the pacification of obstacles.'
by which its general form brings increase to the particular forms.
And in the body of the disciple, for the evident loosening of his bonds,
he acts, as it were, shaking off the bonds by the power of his own will.
Directly established in my own body, I am the agent of acts of grace,
and, because knowledge and action are free, I am skillful in the rite of initiation.
I possess a connection with the circle of the senses, with their groups of distinct functions and forms.
Just as I, though one, am clearly sixfold as fire and the others, so it is.
Having reflected in this way, by whichever <s>adhvan</s> he wishes to perform this initiation,
for the sake of its integration he should worship that in the five, apart from the disciple.
And when the force of integration has reached its limit, according to the distinction between concise and expanded treatment,
he should perform what has been practiced to the utmost and filled by the inclusion of the others.
After that, through contemplation, he should again and again integrate identity with <s>Śiva</s>:

children.text: ahameva paraṃ tattvaṃ naca tadghaṭavat kvacit ||
children.translated_text: 'I alone am the supreme reality, and it is not anywhere like a pot.
It is the great light; therefore this entire world is in me,
and it is not placed there by anyone, like an external reflection.
I am its agent; it is not dependent on another and is founded in me.'
Purified by the awareness of such a great pervasion,
a living being who has attained equality with me is called liberated.
Just as an iron ball comes to the state of fire through the sequence of heating, rubbing, sprinkling, and so on,
so the guru comes to the state of having <s>Śiva</s> as his own self.
Then, seeing before him the disciple who is present, or a body mentally set before him,
or, in a remote initiation, a dead disciple fashioned from darbha grass and the like,
he should worship him with flowers and the like and install that disciple's <s>adhvan</s> in him.
Whichever <s>adhvan</s> the teacher chiefly wishes to use for the initiation,
he should install that in the body, and the rule is that the others are to be included within it.
And when the <s>adhvan</s> to be purified has been placed, there itself
he should place the purifying mantra as desired, according to the fitness of what is to be purified.
Sometimes, without placing what is to be purified, merely by the installation of the purifier,
the thing to be purified is itself purified through the power of the purifier.

children.text: aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca paraṃ ca vidhimicchayā
children.translated_text: Taking up, as he wishes, the lower, the higher-and-lower, and the higher procedures,
the installation of the sixfold <s>adhvan</s> follows the manner of joining them.
Up to the forehead is eighty-four; up to the aperture is ninety-six;
up to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> is one hundred and eight: this is the threefold procedure.
It is now explained in sequence, as seen in the scripture called <s>Śrīpūrva</s>.
There, among the <s>tattvas</s>, the installation extends to the ankle and four finger-breadths.
Earth, and then from water onward up to the root, each occupies two finger-breadths in order.
In this way, above the navel, it is forty-six finger-breadths, or six finger-breadths by another reckoning.

children.text: puṃsaḥ kalāntaṃ ṣaṭtattvīṃ pratyekaṃ tryaṅgule kṣipet
children.translated_text: From <s>puruṣa</s> up to <s>kalā</s>, he should place the group of six <s>tattvas</s>, each in three finger-breadths.
Thus it is eighteen finger-breadths, ending at the hollow of the throat.
The tetrad beginning with <s>māyā</s>, up to <s>sadāśiva</s>, is in four finger-breadths
each, thus having the number eighty-four in the region of the garland.
After that, he should contemplate the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, made of radiance and undisturbed,
as pervading all of them, both outwardly and inwardly.
From water through intellect is two and a half; the root is three finger-breadths; therefore,
because it exceeds by twelve finger-breadths, this is the higher-and-lower procedure.
But if from water through intellect is three finger-breadths, and the unmanifest is in four,
then, because of its excess of twenty-four, the higher procedure too is one hundred and eight.
The threefold measure has been made clear through reduction from the numbers of the Vasus and directions to that of the sun.
So too it has been stated in the <s>Maya-tantra</s>, with regard to the wish for each particular result.
In the installation of nine, five, four, three, or one <s>tattva</s>,
he should devise the installation by his own understanding, to that extent, through contemplation of the inclusion of the other <s>tattvas</s>.
The installation of the five <s>kalās</s> and the four eggs is indicated by this same principle.
And it is said in the <s>Triśiras-tantra</s>: 'As it stands in its own support,
the upward extension is twelve finger-breadths, equal beyond the body.
Seventy-two, ten, and two are within the body up to the end of the head.
Beginning from the feet, O fair-hipped one, up to the station of the unstruck sound,
even in what is beyond the body there is bodyhood, because consciousness rests there
through the force of imagination; therefore the upward extension is twelve finger-breadths.
This one hundred and eight has been stated here in order to determine it in this way.'
Now the installation of the <s>puras</s>: up to the ankle is earth; here there are sixteen <s>puras</s>.
Therefore, beginning with <s>Lakula</s>, each has an extent of one finger-breadth.
Up to <s>Dviraṇḍa</s> it is three finger-breadths; then <s>Chagalāṇḍa</s> is in the waters.
In the group of eight <s>Devayogas</s>, there are two, each by a quarter finger-breadth.
Thus, up to <s>Pradhāna</s>, there are forty-six finger-breadths.
In this way there are fifty-six <s>puras</s>; before earth there are sixteen.
After that, by an extent of half a finger-breadth, six <s>puras</s> occupy three finger-breadths.

children.text: catvāri yugma ekasmin ekaṃ ca puramaṅgule ||
children.translated_text: Four occupy two finger-breadths, and one <s>pura</s> occupies one finger-breadth.
Together with <s>rāga</s>, the numbers of the <s>puras</s> of <s>puruṣa</s> and of the Lord are thus in six finger-breadths.
The <s>pura</s> of <s>Krodheśa</s> is in one, and the egg is in two; and this is knowledge.
So too for <s>Saṃvarta</s> and <s>Jyotis</s>, respectively belonging to <s>kalā</s> and <s>tattva</s>,
and for the <s>puras</s> ending with <s>Śūra</s> and <s>Pañcānta</s>, in <s>niyati</s> there is one and two respectively.
This has been stated in the <s>Śrīpūrva-śāstra</s> by the supreme Lord <s>Śambhu</s>.
According to the sequence beginning with the northern one, in the triad beginning with <s>vidyā</s> there is a division into two and one.
Because the sequence is not essential, <s>niyati</s> comes first, and after that <s>kalā</s>;
or the two <s>tattvas</s> may be designated by one another's names.
<s>Ekavīra</s>, <s>Śikheśa</s>, and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> are the three in the three with respect to time.
The installation of time is said to come before that of <s>niyati</s>.
Or rather, designation by one another's names is indeed seen.
Thus the set of six <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>puruṣa</s> is arranged within eighteen aṅgulas.
Beyond that, up to the limit measured by the thumb, there is the group of eight situated in the <s>māyātattva</s>.
Each one, by half-aṅgula portions, should occupy four aṅgulas.
In this way, in the two eyes, the twenty-eight cities beginning with <s>puruṣa</s> are set forth in the night-region.
Then, in sequence, a triad of cities is placed in two, short of an aṅgula by one third.
In the two there are two each; the five-city group in the <s>Vaidyīya</s> division occupies four aṅgulas.
Then come the eight <s>Aiśa</s> cities in a group of four, proceeding by half-aṅgula intervals.

children.text: tatastrīṇi dvaye dve ca dvayoritthaṃ catuṣṭaye
children.translated_text: After that there are three in two, then two in two, and thus the arrangement is made in the group of four.
The <s>Sādāśiva</s> set is five; thus there is one group of eight in the twelvefold measure.
The classes of cities are sixteen, the rasa-arrow number, two eights, and the eight-moon number.

children.text: vedā rasābdhi yugmākṣi ca ravayastatra cāṅgulāḥ kramaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the aṅgulas, in order, are denoted by Vedas, rasa-ocean, paired eyes, and suns.
In this body, measured as eighty-four, one hundred and eighteen cities

children.text: vinyastāni taditthaṃ śeṣe tu vyāpakaṃ śivaṃ tattvam ||
children.translated_text: are thus arranged; in the remaining part, however, the pervasive <s>śivatattva</s> is placed.
Thus another procedure, called <s>Parāparā</s>, has been taught in the station denoted by rasa and śruti.

children.text: aṣṭaśaraṃ saṃkhyānaṃ khamunikṛtaṃ tatpare vidhau jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: In the further procedure, the enumeration called eight-arrow, made with space and sages, should be known.
Here, for this mass of worlds extending from <s>Lakula</s> up to the <s>Yogāṣṭaka</s>,
