one should assign the portion according to the calculation, in the two procedures respectively and in order.
After this triad of procedures beginning with <s>Aparā</s>, there is the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual installation) of the path of words.

children.text: pūrvaṃ daśapadī coktā svatantrā nyasyate yadā ||
children.translated_text: The tenfold word-series has been stated before; when it is installed independently,
and if initiation is to be performed by that alone, then this is the arrangement of <s>nyāsa</s>.
But in initiation, because the <s>tattvas</s> and the rest have primary importance, the word-series
is included there according to those particular <s>tattvas</s> and other categories.
When, however, it has its own primacy in initiation, the system of words
should be installed in order, without looking toward the faces of the <s>tattvas</s> and the rest.
In four, in eight, again in eight, then in ten and again in ten,
then in ten, then in fifteen, and then in the Veda-arrow-moon number,
one should connect, beginning with the earth-word, the ninefold series belonging to <s>Mātṛkāmālinī</s>.
The tenth word, called <s>Śiva</s>, is the pervader and should be joined as such.

children.text: dharāpadaṃ varjayitvā pañca yāni padāni tu ||
children.translated_text: Leaving aside the earth-word, the five words that remain
make two procedures when installed over twelve and twelve aṅgulas.
For the arrangement of installation in the path of mantras, this same procedure applies.
Only the extent of pervasion differs; this very point has already been stated before.
Now the installation of the path of phonemes is taught here in three procedures.
First there is one in each of four, then two in each of two aṅgulas, in sequence.
There is a set of twenty-three phonemes, and a set of six phonemes, one by one, in the threes.
Then four each in the four, in reverse order.
These are the syllables of <s>Mālinīmātṛkā</s>; the pervading Śaiva one is given by the rasa-moon number.
Leaving out the first phoneme, as in the case of the <s>tattvas</s>, there should be twelve and twelve.
In those twenty-three phonemes, the other two procedures should also be understood.
Therefore, in the <s>Śrīpūrvaśāstra</s>, the threefold procedure was first taught with regard to the <s>tattvas</s>.
It is then extended equally to the two classes of phonemes, whether different or not different from them.

children.text: dvividho 'pi hi varṇānāṃ ṣaḍvidho bheda ucyate
children.translated_text: Although twofold, the distinction among phonemes is said to be sixfold.
It should be understood in truth by the method of the path of <s>tattvas</s>.
What was stated with regard to words and the rest by direct teaching and by extension
is again extended there in that very scripture, our Lord of the Heart.
According to the previous sūtras, one should make the triadic form
of words, mantras, kalās, and the rest, following the path stated for <s>tattvas</s> and phonemes.
That has been stated for words and mantras; now it is explained with respect to the <s>kalās</s>.
In four, in the rasa-Veda number, in twenty-two, and then in twelve,
there are the four <s>kalās</s> beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>; the pervading one is <s>Śāntyatītikā</s>.
But in the second <s>kalā</s>, having placed twelve and twelve aṅgulas
in sequence, there are two procedures, consisting of <s>Parāparā</s> and <s>Parā</s>.
The procedure of the four eggs is here included by the initial word.
Therefore, as with the set of four <s>kalās</s>, the threefold procedure should be stated in that case.
Thus, after first purifying the sixfold <s>adhvan</s> in the body of the disciple to be purified,
one should install it according to whichever one has primacy and in the manner approved for the purifier.
For the mass of mantras used in the installation of the <s>adhvan</s> is the purifier, beginning with the single one.
The mass of sound, namely <s>Mālinī</s>, is twofold as a whole and in its parts.
Or, by being a single heroine, the set of six arises through yāmala-combination.
Because of the distinction between the five-faced form and the śakti likewise, it is again sixfold and twofold.
By being single and paired in this way, it has twelve forms.
As six-limbed, and because it may be whole or other than whole, it is twofold; again, like the faces,
when multiplied by twelve, it has twenty-four divisions.
In the eight beginning with <s>Aghora</s> there are two, and the third arises from the emergence of the yāmala.
The <s>Mātṛsadbhāva</s> mantra, existing alone in the cycle of śruti,
has thirteen divisions through its one-, two-, three-, and fourfold distinctions.
As a single heroine, this stands as a fourteenth form.
The cycle of namelessness, withdrawal, stability, and creation is fourfold.
Together with its own deities, it is enlarged by the <s>Mātṛsadbhāva</s>.
Thus this group of purifying mantras is remembered as numbering seventy.
It is taught in the scriptures of the <s>Ṣaḍardha</s> and in the venerable <s>Sāraśāstra</s>.
Here the wise one should purify with the eight beginning with <s>Aghora</s>,
or else with one-syllabled mantras, or according to the sequence of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>,
or with the <s>Bhairavīyahṛdaya</s>, or with the <s>Khecarīhṛdaya</s>,
or, O great goddess, with <s>Bhairava</s>, and then with the five sets of faces and limbs.

children.text: yena yena hi mantreṇa tantre 'smin udbhavaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For by whichever <s>mantra</s> the emergence has been effected in this <s>tantra</s>,
by that very one the <s>mantrin</s> should initiate: such is the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Thus, according to the division of the purifiers, seventy distinctions have been stated.
When <s>dīkṣā</s> is performed with these <s>mantras</s>, without the <s>nyāsa</s> of what is to be purified,
then it should be known as seventyfold, devoid of the processes beginning with generation.
Now the division of what is to be purified must be stated; that too is explained briefly.
The <s>tattva</s> aspect is fourfold, by divisions into one, three, five, and thirty-six;
the <s>adhvans</s> also are according to divisions of five and one, and likewise there are the four <s>aṇḍas</s>.
Thus what is to be purified is tenfold; through its three procedures it is thirtyfold.
By the distinction between purifier and purified object, however, there are one hundred and twenty-one.
Here too, by the application of <s>nyāsa</s>, when the <s>adhvan</s> to be purified has been made of that form,
there would be a one-hundred-and-twenty-onefold division, without generation and the rest.
When it consists of generation and the rest, it is of just that extent; thus the scripture regards it in a hundredfold way.
That too exceeds by seventy, because of the distinction between material rite and knowledge.
Since it is twofold, it becomes eighty-five hundreds with forty added.
Because of the consideration of <s>bhoga</s> and <s>mokṣa</s>, it is proclaimed as twofold.
Through purification of only the inauspicious, and then through purification also of the auspicious,
<s>bhoga</s> is twofold; purification of the auspicious, divided according to the three times,
becomes sevenfold according to one, two, or the totality; thus enjoyment is eightfold.
And according to the sequence of guru and disciple, it too is twofold; in this way it is divided.
For in direct initiation, since the two have one and the same intention,
the fruit of such <s>dīkṣā</s> is complete; but where there is discrepancy, there is disruption.
In indirect initiation, initiation of the dead, and the like, the guru alone possesses the intention;
by the power of ritual and knowledge he should lead that disciple to the desired abode.
When ritual and knowledge are undivided, and likewise when <s>karma</s> is purified,
the intention, however, is different, since the <s>karma</s> consists of that.
And in the venerable <s>Svacchanda</s> scripture, the result, because of the distinction in latent impressions,
is stated for disciples and for the guru, even when the ritual and the rest are the same.
In <s>bhoga</s> there is variety because of the purifier, the purified object, and such an intention,
since variety is the vital principle of distinction.
For example, one whose <s>adhvan</s> has been purified by certain mouths and joined by those very ones,
when he wishes to enjoy in some <s>tattva</s>, is an enjoyer endowed with that power.
And when auspicious <s>karmas</s> are present here, the diversity of enjoyment
will be of that very kind; but when <s>karma</s> is purified, the diversity is different.
And <s>bhoga</s> is fourfold: immediately through departure, or connected with the very body,
or else at that very time through practice, or at the end of the body.
Together with the preceding eightfold classification, a thirty-twofold division is stated.
<s>Mokṣa</s>, though one, has such a relation to the seed called <s>samaya</s>:
with reference to a child and the like, to one known to be near death, to one lacking <s>śakti</s>,
or to an old person, or to one who is capable, it is twofold according to purification and non-purification.
Through immediate departure it is threefold; and that should be performed by the guru when death is near,
such is the command of <s>Maheśa</s>, spoken in the venerable <s>Gahvara</s>.
Having seen a disciple overcome by old age and severely afflicted by disease,
he should then cause him to depart and establish him in the supreme <s>tattva</s>.
These thirty-five divisions, by reckoning the twofold distinction mentioned
for the guru, or for guru and disciple, are proclaimed as seventy.
With these divisions the guru should multiply those previously stated divisions belonging to <s>dīkṣā</s>,
and state the enumeration for the accomplishment of the knowledge he has well practiced.
That number which was stated as eighty-five hundreds with forty added,
reckoning it by seventy, he should himself calculate the divisions of <s>dīkṣā</s>.
Here the total count is five lakhs and ninety-seven thousand,
and eight hundred: this is the division of <s>dīkṣā</s> in the <s>Mālinītantra</s>.
The group of purifiers is seventyfold; what is to be purified, beginning with the single <s>tattva</s>, is thirtyfold;
including the <s>aṇḍa</s>, it has the form of the six <s>adhvans</s>; and the procedure is fourfold.
It is made of material rite and knowledge, either devoid of generation and the rest or joined with them;
again this is thirty-fivefold from the consideration of <s>bhoga</s> and <s>apavarga</s>.
Because <s>bhoga</s> is thirty-twofold, divided by purification of the auspicious and inauspicious and by time,
and <s>mokṣa</s> is threefold and doubled, the divisions of what is to be done are seventy.
Because of the divisions of purifier and purified object, and because of divisions in procedure,

children.text: dīkṣā bahudhā bhinnā śodhyavihīnā tu saptatidhā ||
children.translated_text: this <s>dīkṣā</s> is divided in many ways; but without what is to be purified it is seventyfold.
Because the <s>mantras</s> are reckoned according to distinctions such as complete, incomplete, with limbs, and without limbs,
and because the purified object, beginning with <s>tattva</s>, is counted with divisions beginning with fifteen,
the enumeration of the divisions cannot be carried out; these are unmixed distinctions,
while other mixed distinctions again produce multiplicity in many ways.
Because there are divisions into two, three, and so on among the purifier, the purified object, and the rest,
when <s>bhoga</s> is the goal, the wise person should attend to whatever many things must be done.
For multiplicity of causes leads to multiplicity of results; what is surprising in that?
But in <s>apavarga</s> there is no division; therefore, in this, for one possessed of firmness of latent impression,
even a small rite should be relied upon, or else knowledge alone.
But the teacher <s>Abhinavagupta</s> says that, when wealth, place, time, and so on are available,
even for <s>apavarga</s> an extensive collection of ritual and knowledge should be performed,
because of the variety of the movement of consciousness and because, even amid instability, conjunction occurs gradually.
In each and every object, firm establishment inevitably becomes Śiva-natured.
This <s>tattva</s> (principle) has that nature; from it I have drawn up the disciple.
In this way, through awareness of the sequence, even a dull person becomes one whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>.
And when he sees the teacher made blessed by the grace of such sequential <s>Śiva</s>-hood,
even a child, through the vision of non-difference from him and through the force of devotion, attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
Although the Lord has taught in scripture that, even for one whose activity is still conceptual, liberation comes by initiation alone at the end of the body,
nevertheless this is joined with firm latent impressions.
Some say that even in liberation there is a distinction, such as dwelling in the same world and the rest, produced by the lesser or greater amount of ritual action.

children.text: iti kecittadayuktaṃ sa vicitro bhoga eva kathitaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: That is not correct, for that would be described as varied enjoyment alone.
During this life, which continues by the remainder of former impressions, no mass of obstacles comes to him from transgression of observances and the like.
That multiplicity of ritual belongs to one who desires liberation.
For in the case of a man consecrated by <s>sabīja-dīkṣā</s> (seeded initiation), when there has been transgression of observances and the like,
liberation comes after he has experienced the enjoyments; this is not so in <s>nirbīja-dīkṣā</s> (seedless initiation).

children.text: iti kecinmanyante yuktaṃ taccāpi yatsmṛtaṃ śāstre ||
children.translated_text: So some think; and that too is reasonable, since it is remembered in scripture:
'From violating the observance, O Goddess, there is the state of being a flesh-eater for a hundred years.'
Therefore, in the opinion about eminent disciples, the sequential ritual beginning with the extraction of the <s>tattvas</s>,
being capable of bestowing firm establishment in the state of <s>Śiva</s>, is appropriate even for liberation, though it is very extensive.

children.text: yastu sadā bhāvanayā svabhyastajñānavānguruḥ sa śiśoḥ
children.translated_text: But a guru who always, by contemplation, possesses well-practiced knowledge
may perform, for the child's release, any means whatsoever as he wishes.
Thus, having placed upon the disciple's body the <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic course) to be purified, as desired,
he should place the purifying mantra above it according to the <s>tattvas</s>.
The order of the letters in the two <s>mātṛkās</s> (letter-matrices), according to the placement of the <s>tattvas</s>,
was stated earlier; he should place it in that way for the purification of each respective <s>tattva</s>.

children.text: varṇādhvā yadyapi proktaḥ śodhyaḥ pāśātmakastu saḥ
children.translated_text: Although the <s>varṇādhvan</s> (course of letters) is said to be what is to be purified, it is of the nature of bondage.
The purifier, however, is another: belonging to <s>māyā</s>, yet <s>Śiva</s>-natured and consisting of supreme speech.
And <s>Sadyojyotis</s> said this in the commentary on the <s>Svāyambhuva</s>:
'Certainly, one sound is of the nature of bondage, and another is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.'
Therefore, for that same letter, the relation of purifier and purified is appropriate.
And in the <s>Śrīpūrva-śāstra</s> too it is said, 'They were embraced by those.'
The faces beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s> and the five limbs beginning with the heart
should be placed six times; from earth upward he should perform the thirty-sixfold <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement).
Because of the reverse order of <s>Parāparā</s>, there are three words in earth.
Then, from water up to ego, there are five words, on the basis of five groups of eight.
In the triad called intellect, root, person, and passion there are three words.
There is one word in the pair, impure knowledge and time, and one in the regulator.
And in the pair, <s>kalā</s> and <s>māyā</s>, one word is stated here in sequence.
In knowledge, the lords of knowledge, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, power, and <s>Śiva</s>, there is a group of five words.
This <s>Parāparā</s> consists of nineteen words.

children.text: sārdhaṃ caikaṃ caikaṃ sārdhaṃ dve dve śaśī dṛgatha yugmam ||
children.translated_text: One and a half, then one, one, one and a half, two, two, the moon, the eye, and then a pair,

children.text: trīṇi dṛgabdhiścandraḥ śrutiḥ śaśī pañca vidhumahaścandrāḥ
children.translated_text: three, the eye, the ocean, the moon, scripture, the moon, five, the moon, the day, and moons:
this is the number of syllables in the nineteen words of the Goddess.
Her own letters are counted with a pair of consonants, the Vasus, and <s>Citragu</s>.
Up to the root there is a half-letter; up to <s>māyā</s> there is a single letter.
Up to power there is one; this is the rule taught for the <s>Aparā-nyāsa</s>.
Up to <s>māyā</s> there is a consonant, and then up to power a vowel is stated.

children.text: niṣkale śivatattve vai paro nyāsaḥ paroditaḥ
children.translated_text: In the partless <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, the higher <s>nyāsa</s>, called supreme, is taught.
The very words of <s>Parāparā</s> are the mantras in the two octads beginning with <s>Aghorī</s>.
According to that, one should cast this pair upon the <s>tattvas</s>.
For all the compact syllables, the count of letters differs according to the divisions.

children.text: avyaktāntaṃ svare nyasyā śeṣaṃ śeṣeṣu yojayet
children.translated_text: Up to the unmanifest he should place them among the vowels, and he should join the remainder to the remaining ones.
He should conceive the seed-syllables in all the <s>tattvas</s> as pervaders.
But others have understood the placement of the compact syllables to be like that of seed-syllables.

children.text: akṛte vātha śodhyasya nyāse vastubalāt sthiteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, if the placement of what is to be purified has not been performed, because its establishment exists by the force of the real principle,
everything to be purified is purified by the mere placement of the purifier.
And in the revered <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> and other scriptures it has been taught by the Supreme Lord:
'Now, by mere <s>nyāsa</s>, purification of the elements comes about.'
For the purpose of bodily purification too, this is in fact equivalent to that.
If something stated in another section is applicable in a different section,
whether as an indicator or directly, why should it not be accepted elsewhere?
The <s>nyāsa</s> of the limb of the <s>Mālinī-mātṛkā</s>, which was previously taught in the rule for worship,
is just the same in the placement of the mantra that is solely purifying.
In each pair there is a three-word unit; then, in the eight, there are words measured by scripture,
according to the reckoning by directions, moon, moon, taste, sun, arrows, autumn, eyes, eyes, moon, and moon.
In the finger-measure of the Goddess, eighteen is another word by its full extension.
This is another measure in the <s>nyāsa</s> of the mantra that is solely purifying.
From the fourth word through the group of six words there are two measures, called <s>Parāparā</s> and <s>Parā</s>.
A group of twelve and another group of twelve are above the <s>tattvas</s>; the rest is as before.
With reference to the <s>nyāsa</s> of the mantra that is solely purifying, <s>Mahādeva</s>,
although he had taught a <s>nyāsa</s> according to the order of the <s>tattvas</s>, again states one even contrary to that.
'In the partless one there is a one-letter word; in earth there are as many as three,'
and so on: by such statements, the sequential <s>nyāsa</s> belonging to the <s>tattvas</s> is taught.
And again, in the <s>Mālinī-tantra</s>, according to the distinction between the groups and the vidyās,
after saying, 'The words are of two kinds,' the Lord explained a <s>nyāsa</s> of another sort.

children.text: ekaikaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra pūrvaṃ padatrayam
children.translated_text: There, first, the three words are to be understood as two aṅgulas each.
Four are eight aṅgulas; after that comes a measure of ten aṅgulas.

children.text: dvyaṅgule dve pade cānye ṣaḍaṅgulamataḥ param
children.translated_text: And two other words are each two aṅgulas; after that comes a measure of six aṅgulas.
Another is twelve aṅgulas, and two others separately are each five aṅgulas.
A pair of words has four joints, and likewise two others have two joints.
Thus the independent <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual installation) of <s>Parāparādevī</s> is taught.
One should apply the two <s>vidyās</s> (sacred formulas) in the disciple's body precisely as pervaders.
In order to show this, he did not set out its <s>nyāsa</s> separately.
Thus, in the <s>nyāsa</s> of the purifying mantra, through union with its rays,
the net of bonds dissolves by the force of the guru's meditation on it.
In the <s>tattva</s> (principle) to be purified, because all wombs are generated simultaneously,
and because there is experience, separation comes about when the karma has been exhausted.
For this <s>aṇu</s> (limited soul), even though it is an enjoyer through so many bodies, it is clearly remarkable
that there is no mental continuity, unlike the connection and separation belonging to the whole universe.
By <s>niyati</s> (limiting necessity), the mind functions only in a single body; beyond that
there is no continuity, since that continuity is imagined through sense-organs joined to one single mind.
And the self's cognition operates in a limited region, there in each particular place.
The cognition of an object of experience does not deserve continuity in other bodies.
But when, for that mind, even while it functions in a body, there is certainly
purity produced by one who knows, through yoga, mantra, ritual action, and the like, then,
just as a stainless mind swiftly sees even what is far away,
so in <s>pratyayadīkṣā</s> (initiation through cognition) there is vision of each corresponding world.
But when he wishes to perform an initiation free from birth and the rest,
then the imagined reasoning, "I shall extract him from this," is appropriate.
When there is a <s>nyāsa</s> of the purifier without the object to be purified, even there, through mantra,
he should perform the sequence beginning with birth, but without conjunction with the <s>tattvas</s>.
And in the solitary <s>nyāsa</s> of the purifier, when birth and the rest are omitted,
he should simply imagine what is called the enclosing vessel of that purifier.
In initiation performed by means of substances, he should offer sesame, ghee, unbroken rice, and rice grains
with each corresponding mantra, for the conjunction and separation connected with birth.

children.text: yadā vijñānadīkṣāṃ tu kuryācchiṣyaṃ tadā bhṛśam
children.translated_text: But when he performs <s>vijñānadīkṣā</s> (initiation through knowledge) for the disciple, then intensely,
by the force of reciting that mantra, he should see him up to the nonconceptual state.
For conceptual construction is made of verbal determination, since it is reflective awareness.
That is the nature of mantra; and reflective awareness is pure, having the nature of freedom from bonds.
It is eternal and is conceived as non-different from beginningless, boon-giving <s>Śiva</s>.
Through union with that, even the officiating teacher's conceptual construction attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
This was spoken by the Supreme Lord in the venerable <s>Sāraśāstra</s>:
"The apprehension of an object, having the form of grasped and grasper,
is itself mantra-power, extended through the lineage of mantras.
Thus mantra-power is declared to have the nature of reflective apprehension."
Reflective apprehension is twofold, since it distinguishes mantras by being pure or impure.
It is said in the venerable <s>Pauṣkara</s>: "Others too, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, are contained within the cosmic egg.
They belong to <s>Pradhāna</s>, are affected by impurity, and consist of sattva, rajas, and tamas.
When a guru has become identified with them through impure reflective apprehension,

children.text: vaiṣṇavādiḥ paśuḥ prokto na yogyaḥ patiśāsane
children.translated_text: he is called a <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), such as a Vaiṣṇava, and is not fit for the Lord's teaching.
But the mantras that stand on the pure path, beginning with <s>Śivabhaṭṭāraka</s>,
according to the view of the venerable <s>Mataṅga</s> and other scriptures, make the guru who is identified with them <s>Śiva</s> himself.
One may object: Let there be reflective awareness through union with an independent verbal determination.
But where would that have been before? If it comes from reflective awareness, whence is that too, on analysis?
The first such determination may bestow nonconceptuality because it comes from a teacher.
And the utterance transmitted from him also has another teacher.
Thus, through the sequence of earlier and earlier teachers, that very verbal determination of the original guru long ago
has been transmitted and still exists today: this should be accepted.
If some independent reflective awareness is imagined through the power of that kind of verbal determination,
that too is certainly of the same nature as it.

children.text: ghaṭakumbha itītthaṃ vā yadi bhedo nirūpyate ||
children.translated_text: And if a distinction is established in this way, as between "ghaṭa" and "kumbha,"
that too introduces another conceptual construction and should be carefully disregarded.
For conceptual construction, the usages "paṇāyate" and "karoti" are plainly appropriate.
How indeed could the utterances "kara" and "pāṇi" be mixed together?
Therefore learning proceeds from one word to another word only through an intervening relation.
But through ordinary usage it is direct, reflecting the cognition called an image.
The arising of that reflective awareness shines forth as composed of a prior self-reflection.
So long as a child's awareness rests in unartificial reflective apprehension,
therefore, seeing the conceptual construction arising from the particular word and meaning of that mantra
as distinct from one arising from another word, the mantra is respected.
And what was previously said of the seed, the piṇḍa, and the rest as having the form of awakening,
belongs to this very awareness; how could it belong to another? Why then imagine another?
For this reason, the characteristic mark there, in each case, has carefully been taught by the guru
in the definition; for he is skilled in mantra and tantra.
Therefore, in understanding the meaning of mantra, the guru should respectfully use
a mantra-commentary, or else reasoning by supposition and exclusion, in every possible way.
But when there is no knower of the meaning of the mantra, in every way
he should make the guru mantra-formed; through practice, he consists of that resolve.
When, from contemplating the meaning of the mantra, the guru comes to have the same utterance as that mantra,
then, if everything is equal, what difference can be stated?

children.text: aṃśenāpyatha vaiṣamye na tato 'rthakriyā hi sā ||
children.translated_text: But if there is inequality even in part, then that does not have the efficacy of the object.
When, according to the maxim, "from cow-dung, from an insect, an insect,"
even from another discourse he sees that very practical efficacy.
Then this one is called a true saṃjalpa; he is <s>Śiva</s> himself.
Whatever he says, that alone becomes a mantra, granting enjoyment and liberation.
This is not the position of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, whose self is offered to mantra:
namely, that one should speak of a different practical efficacy even in two such insects.
But if one whose mind is offered to mantra says something and thereby removes poison,

children.text: tanmantra eva śabdaḥ sa paraṃ tatra ghaṭādivat ||
children.translated_text: that sound itself is mantra; only there it is like the word 'pot' and the like.
A lover, made beautiful by talk of union with his beloved,
though conditioned by that, is satisfied in himself even while doing something else.
So too, one infused by the discourse of that mantra, even while saying something else,
and even without intending it, has that form and certainly brings about the effect.
For even while forming a conception of one object, he also sees another;
this has been stated in the <s>Śrīpūrvaśāsana</s> and elsewhere, as in the case of poison-removing mantras.
Or, even in the destruction of poison, there may be variety because of differences in causes,
arising from endless differences of effects such as the nourishment of the bodily constituents and so on.
Thus, through the practice of mantra-discourse and conceptual formation,
the object to be contemplated becomes manifest, through the gradual diminution of discourse.
This one contemplates the object itself, and no longer

children.text: gṛhṇāti bhāsanopāyaṃ bhāte tatra tu tena kim ||
children.translated_text: grasps this discourse as the means of manifestation; when the thing shines forth, what need is there of it?
In this way, when discourse has diminished, the object, by nature very clearly manifest,
consisting of uncontrived reflexive awareness, would shine forth as non-conceptual.

children.text: nirvikalpā ca sā saṃvidyadyathā paśyati sphuṭam
children.translated_text: And whatever that non-conceptual consciousness sees clearly,
that is precisely so, because the object too, even when externally situated, has that very nature.
Especially for those who possess identity with the <s>Śiva</s>-state beyond māyā,
saṃjalpa is a means in liberation; from it, indeed, come bondage and liberation.
Even in the conceptual cognition of a guru who properly enjoys non-different <s>Śiva</s>-hood,
waiting until the non-conceptual limit is reached is of no use.
For that mantra-deity, which is to be expressed, has the nature of such reflexive awareness
and is close to the great consciousness, as is stated in the <s>Śrīgamaśāsana</s>.
Just as those who stand near kings can fully accomplish for others
a success connected with the king very quickly, so mantras and the like accomplish the supreme success.
Therefore, containing the intention already stated, it is said in the <s>Śrīmālinīmata</s>,
when the sages asked, 'What is the characteristic mark of mantras?'
They regard yoga as the unity of one thing with another thing.
That thing is said to be what is to be known, for the establishment of rejectability and the like.
For establishing that, the knowledge described by <s>Śiva</s> was taught;
it is also fully the characteristic of mantra for the accomplishment of seeded yoga.

children.text: na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge 'sti śāṅkare
children.translated_text: And without dīkṣā there is no eligibility for the yoga of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
That dīkṣā is taught as twofold, according to the distinction between action and knowledge.
Therefore it is to be performed in two forms, and this has been explained:
by it there would not be eligibility for yoga alone.
There is also eligibility for mantra, and liberation, through <s>Śiva</s>-dīkṣā.
By this too it has been said that the yogin, for the attainment of unity with the tattvas,
should devotedly rely on the root mantra itself, all the way to the non-conceptual limit,

children.text: mantrābhyāsena bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vāpi prasādhayan ||
children.translated_text: accomplishing either enjoyment or liberation by the practice of mantra.
For gaining eligibility there, one should receive dīkṣā from a preceptor.
Then whatever he may accomplish through the power of mantra, knowledge, yoga, and the like,
that becomes his, even when, as a disciple, he is joined by the guru to another tattva.
For dīkṣā is useful for his consecration; consecrated, he is refined.

children.text: svabalenaiva bhogaṃ vā mokṣaṃ vā labhate budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise person obtains enjoyment or liberation by his own power alone.
Therefore, first becoming a samayin, strong through knowledge, yoga, and the like,
or becoming a putraka, he would not be so dependent, but rather suited to his own power.
But one who is barren of knowledge, yoga, and the like is like a blind man on a road.

children.text: daiśikāyatta eva syādbhoge muktau ca sarvathā
children.translated_text: He is wholly dependent on the preceptor, both for enjoyment and for liberation.

children.text: dīkṣā ca kevalā jñānaṃ vināpi nijamāntaram ||
children.translated_text: And dīkṣā alone, even without one's own inner knowledge,
has previously been stated, by reasoning and by scripture, to be liberating.
But the disciple who relies only on the yojanikā produced by dīkṣā,
and then resorts to the knowledge and yoga appropriate for making that manifest,
wherever he is joined, he attains identity with that.
Therefore every state depends on guru, dīkṣā, mantra, and scripture.
Of all bad karmas, past, present, and future,
purification should be performed for one desiring enjoyment, but not of wholesome karmas.
But when a disciple seeks worldly enjoyment, such as kingship or heaven,
or, having abandoned that, desires supramundane enjoyment, then even with respect to his wholesome karmas,
when performing material dīkṣā there with ghee, sesame, and the like,
the excellent preceptor should offer oblation, saying, 'I purify his karma.'

children.text: jñānamayyāṃ tu dīkṣāyāṃ tad viśudhyati saṃdhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in knowledge-made dīkṣā it is purified through resolve.
By the power of the guru, firmly established in his own consciousness, its destruction occurs.
When his inauspicious karmas have been purified, then the auspicious karma,
because it depends on its own gradations, gives birth within the adhvan.
After the completion of the enjoyment of the fruit obtained through the sequence of auspicious maturation,
when future karma has been destroyed, he remains in that to which he has been joined.
And when future karmas, differentiated by the present body and by later bodies,
have had their inauspicious portion purified, there is no diminution of enjoyment itself
for him as he continually enjoys pleasures up to the dissolution into māyā.
There is nothing at all, even within the body and the rest of the adhvan, that yields the fruit of pain.
Then, at the dissolution into māyā, he has enjoyed all pleasurable enjoyments.
By the force of the joining rite, it undergoes dissolution either in the partless or in the with-parts state.

children.text: iti prameyaṃ kathitaṃ dīkṣā kāle guroryathā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the object to be known has been stated, namely how <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is performed by the guru at the proper time.
Now I shall explain the procedure that bestows identity with <s>Bhairava</s>.
Thus, in the five loci: the maṇḍala, the jar, the fire, the disciple, and his own self,
the teacher should take up their pervasion through unity and place the <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic course) that extends to the disciple.
The triad of impurity consisting of <s>karman</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and atomic limitation he should cast upon the arm, the throat,
and the topknot respectively, by tying knots in a thread.
The appearance of something as not being of that nature is impurity; that is called the knot.
The external construction of a knot is for the sake of firming this recognition.
The arms are the seat of action; <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose nature is <s>māyā</s>, rests in the throat.
The topknot, flowing downward, represents atomic limitation; therefore this visualization is made in this way.
To express the manifold divisions of the triad called the bound soul, power, and <s>Śiva</s>,
he should arrange the thread for tying as three times threefold.
This triad of fire, water, and food is itself threefold in each case.
At the end of the <s>Śruti</s> some, for this reason, accepted it as white, black, and red.
Then, in the fire, where all the mantras have been satisfied and which is simply the sky of consciousness,
he should perform, in order, the purification of the <s>tattvas</s> in their general form.
There, through the appropriate mantra, he should first invoke earth.
After worshipping it with flowers and the like, he should then satisfy it with ghee, sesame, and so on.
Afterwards he should invoke the deity presiding over the <s>māyā-tattva</s>,
the <s>Māyā-śakti</s> that pervades that <s>tattva</s>, with her own mantra, worship her, and fully satisfy her.
In invocation he should use the syllable of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, and in worship the syllable of the <s>Mālinī</s>.
So the guru taught, because there is a twofold strengthening of the essential form.
The liberating syllable, then the word of address, and after that the word 'you',
joined with the first person singular and followed by the action-word, should also be an illuminator.
Then the name in the dative, 'to you', and after that the appropriate illuminator should be added.
With such inferred mantra-connection he should set each particular act in motion.
For every act is stated after the invocation.
Invocation is address, because a being is established in its own nature;
it is the state of being made to enter into identity with one's own self as made of 'I'.

children.text: śāktī bhūmiśca saivoktā yasyāṃ mukhyāsti pūjyatā
children.translated_text: That same state is called the śāktī ground, in which worship chiefly exists.
For, because it is not manifest and because of non-difference, it is not separate from the self of the bound person and <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore, for consciousness to abide in the <s>tattvas</s> that appear as inert, the guru
first makes the case-ending of invocation and then, through the fourth case-ending,
by joining it with an ending in obeisance, should imagine full being.
Then fullness of its own nature arises because of the predominance of that form.
For the predominance of the object of meditation occurs by the meditator's becoming bowed down before it.
'Having invoked, worshipped, and fully satisfied it': this is explained in the revered <s>Svacchanda</s>.
Our teachers have said that this should be understood by this very method.
But what is worshipped as supreme is of the nature of autonomous consciousness.
Since it is unlimited illumination, it is nowhere something to be illuminated.
Indeed, whatever worshippability, meditatability, and so on shine forth in relation to it,
that very thing is its autonomy, its capacity to accomplish what is difficult to reconcile.
How could there be an act of addressing in that thing whose nature is address itself?
If illumination were made an object of illumination, illumination would not be illumination.
Without the power of object and action, through the vocative case-ending alone,
one should perform this inference there, in order to show it through its autonomy.
One says, 'I invoke the deity'; then an illuminator such as 'to the deity',
which gives fullness by the reasoning stated earlier, becomes 'namaḥ', 'svāhā', and the like.
Praise is fullness; the nourishment produced by the conjunction of fire and moon is supreme.
And the nourishing, the washing forth, and formulas such as 'vauṣaṭ' should be made illuminators.
There, even in an external rite, an action established through identity is enjoined.

children.text: yadi karmapadaṃ tanno gurur abhyūhayet kvacit
children.translated_text: If the action-word is not present, the guru should infer it in some cases.
A mantra is employed to make an unmanifested object appear.

children.text: mantraḥ kiṃ tena tatra syātsphuṭaṃ yatrāvabhāsi tat
children.translated_text: What need is there of it where that object is already clearly manifest?
Therefore, in rites such as sprinkling, anointing, and recitation, certainly
one should infer the relevant action; otherwise it would instead become an obstruction.
When there is the appearance of such identity externally, the inference of the action-word is to be made.
But in satisfaction, oblation, the fire that consumes the oblation, burning the bonds, cutting, and similar acts,
where, in the rule already stated, the goal is accomplished afterwards by the succeeding
actional parts, there is no such inference, as in the rules for initiation and the like.
Then, after striking the disciple with the missile-mantra at the place of each <s>tattva</s>,
he should touch the heart with the hand of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tataḥ svanāḍīmārgeṇa hṛdayaṃ prāpya vai śiśoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, through the path of his own channel, having reached the heart of the child,

children.text: śiṣyātmanā sahaikatvaṃ gatvādāya ca taṃ hṛdā
children.translated_text: he becomes one with the disciple's self and, taking him with his own heart,
enclosed in the form called <s>haṃsa</s>, there with the gesture of withdrawal
he should make him manifest as also situated in his own heart.
Because the disciple's body is not separated from its rays, its lights,
because it has moved from its own place of bondage and has obtained a free place,
and because it is independent of its own <s>karman</s>, it is fit to arise everywhere.
Therefore, having first brought the individual soul into his own heart,
he should then bring forth for it, in <s>māyā</s>, bodies made of that earth-<s>tattva</s>.
There, for it, the rite of impregnation is proper, together with rites such as <s>puṃsavana</s>.
He should perform one consecratory rite extending up to emergence from the womb.
Birth and the state of being an enjoyer of experience, joined together, are then one consecratory rite.
After that he should bring about its absorption into identity with those experiences.
Then he should perform the cutting of the bonds belonging to each of those <s>tattvas</s>.
In this tetrad of <s>saṃskāras</s> (consecratory rites), one should apply <s>Aparā</s>, <s>Parāparā</s>,
or <s>Parā</s>, the fifteenfold set of mantras, in order.
The group of eight beginning with the <s>Pivanī</s>, the group of six beginning with the weapon-mantra, and also <s>Parā</s>
are thus the fifteen, in sequence, in the consecration into absorption.
Having first uttered the <s>Aparā</s>-mantra, then saying, 'for the one whose self is so-and-so,'
and 'I perform the rite of impregnation,' and again that same mantra,
the guru, pronouncing it with <s>svāhā</s> at the end, should give three oblations.
Next, with the supreme <s>Parāparā</s>-mantra, then saying, 'for the one whose self is so-and-so,'
and 'I make the one born into an enjoyer and experiencer of enjoyment,' then <s>Parāparā</s>
with <s>svāhā</s> uttered at the end, he should offer three oblations.
Having uttered the <s>Pivanī</s>-mantra and then, 'for the one whose self is so-and-so,'

children.text: bhoge layaṃ karomīti punarmantraṃ tameva ca
children.translated_text: and 'I bring about absorption into enjoyment,' and again that same mantra
ending in <s>svāhā</s>, he should give three oblations with ghee, sesame, and the like.
This same procedure applies in the rites beginning with <s>Vamanī</s>, down to the fifteenth.
First, the mantra whose nature is <s>Parā</s>, then 'for the one whose self is so-and-so,'
and 'I perform the cutting from the bond'; then the <s>Parā</s>-mantra again,
and, having uttered together <s>huṃ svāhā phaṭ</s>, he should give the three oblations too.
Among the mantras that I have taught in this tetrad of <s>saṃskāras</s>,
in them one should state the word 'earth-<s>tattva</s>' before the action-word.
Then, having addressed the lord of the earth-<s>tattva</s>, worshipped him, and fully satisfied him,
the guru, intent with the resolve of <s>Śiva</s>, should command thus:
'O lord of the <s>tattva</s>, by command of <s>Śiva</s> you must not make
an obstruction for this <s>putraka</s>; let him go to the stainless state.'
Then, if the <s>mantrin</s> should wish to purify separately
the fivefold path beginning with the worlds, which lies within the earth-<s>tattva</s>,
then, from the <s>Aparā</s>-mantra, as before, he should give three oblations each,
with the adaptation, 'I purify the city,' his mind being clear.
In this way, regarding the <s>kalā</s>, mantra, word, and phoneme paths also, the discerning one
should give three oblations each, either separately or collectively.
Then, having given the full oblation with <s>Parā</s> ending in <s>vauṣaṭ</s>,
he should lift the disciple out by means of the <s>Aparā</s>-mantra and lead him to his own heart.
But when, through one purified principle, by meditating on the inclusion of the others within it,
he does not purify each <s>tattva</s> separately after the address to the lord of the <s>tattva</s>,
then, having offered the full oblation, he should raise up the atom-soul and unite it with himself.
For the union consisting in its being established there and being established in the self,
some think that oblations should be given with that same <s>Aparā</s> furnished with the action-word.
But other gurus say that this kind of thing is made of contemplation.
Here no external oblation is to be given separately by the preceptor again;

children.text: dadyādvā yadi no doṣaḥ syādupāyaḥ sa bhāvane ||
children.translated_text: or he may give it, if there is no fault, since the means lies in contemplation.
Thus the guru should join him to the earlier state of being established there and in the self.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyahṛdaṃ neyaḥ sa ātmā tāvato 'dhvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that self of so much of the path should be led into the disciple's heart.
It is purified, and for the accomplishment of firmness in that, there should again be a full oblation with <s>Parā</s>.
First, for the purification of the reversed order, the <s>Mahāpāśupata</s>:
'I offer with the weapon-mantra ending in <s>vauṣaṭ</s>,' and he should cast it in.
Then again, having made the full oblation, he should worship <s>Māyā</s> and then dismiss her.
He should visualize the earth-<s>tattva</s>, purified, as mixed with water of pure form;
then the water, mixed in this way, becomes fit for purification.
Likewise, through the mixing of each preceding city-<s>tattva</s> with the next and the next,
the whole series of <s>tattvas</s> becomes <s>Śiva</s>-like and purified; otherwise each remains separate.
And separateness is the impurity called <s>Māyā</s>; when that exists,
even if <s>karman</s> is exhausted, there would be no liberation, as in the case of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and others.
After that, for the water-<s>tattva</s>, into fire, into space, into the light whose self is consciousness,
all the acts beginning with invocation continue up to its mixing into that light.
Thus, when the <s>kalā</s>-<s>tattva</s> has been purified in order, he should cut the bond lodged in the arm;
for that <s>kalā</s> has the nature of unfolding a little agency.
It has the nature of the expansion of the impurity called <s>karman</s>; and that knot, placed at the tip of the ladle,
he should burn in the fire of the mantra's radiance, together with the full oblation.
For the mantra, while being of universal form, nevertheless, because of its dependence on a support,
has a manifest form; therefore in the fire it brings about the scorching of the bond.
That bond, scorched and with its nature dissolved, in relation to him, like <s>Śambhu</s>,
attains the state of being only the residue of the great radiance of the supreme Lord.
When the bond of <s>karman</s> is to be offered here, with the full oblation,

children.text: aśubhaṃ vā bhavadbhūtaṃ bhāvi vātha samastakam ||
children.translated_text: whatever is auspicious or inauspicious, or inauspicious, present, past, future, or all together,
he should cast in the full oblation, saying, 'I burn it; <s>phaṭ</s> three times; <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.'
Thus, in the purification extending up to <s>Māyā</s>, he should also offer the throat-bond.
The bond of that full one, called <s>Māyā</s>, whose nature is the manifestation of division among bonds,
the guru should cast in the full oblation, saying, 'I burn it; <s>phaṭ</s> three times; <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.'

children.text: nirbījā yadi kāryā tu tadātraivāparāṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: But if he is to be made seedless, then right here he should cast in the <s>Aparā</s>
full oblation furnished with the words for burning the seed called the <s>samaya</s>-bond.

children.text: gurau deve tathā śāstre bhaktiḥ kāryāsya nahyasau
children.translated_text: Devotion toward the guru, the deity, and also the scripture must be practiced by him; for that is not

children.text: samayaḥ śaktipātasya svabhāvo hyeṣa no pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: a mere <s>samaya</s>; it is the very nature of the descent of power, not something separate.
When purification has reached the end of <s>Māyā</s>, the <s>Vāgīśī</s> who was formerly
<s>Māyā</s>, consisting of power, herself attains the state of <s>Vidyāśakti</s>.
Having invoked that pure <s>Vidyā</s>, he should assign <s>Vidyāśakti</s>.
Thus, when the station of <s>Sadāśiva</s> too has been well purified in order,
having cut the topknot together with its knot, he should burn the <s>āṇava</s> impurity,
because in <s>Sadāśiva</s> there are indeed two bonds, called authority and enjoyment.
By this statement the <s>āṇava</s> bond is meant here; the <s>māyīya</s> bond extends as far as <s>Niśā</s>.
The disciple should bathe as is appropriate, and the teacher himself should perform <s>ācamana</s>.
When the bond called <s>āṇava</s> has been thoroughly burned in the stainless downward-moving flame,
then, contemplating all the objects of knowledge stated earlier,
and having joined the disciple's body and the rest with his own body, breath, and so on,
he should call to mind the universe within his own body, breath, and the rest.
By the procedure already taught, firm in understanding and with no other thought,
he should meditate on the pair of spatial and temporal paths as situated in the breath, and on the breath as gone into <s>Śakti</s>;

children.text: tāṃ ca saṃvidgatāṃ śuddhāṃ saṃvidaṃ śivarūpiṇīm
children.translated_text: on that <s>Śakti</s> as entered into consciousness, pure, and on consciousness as having the form of <s>Śiva</s>;
and on it as not different from the disciple's consciousness and not different from mantra, fire, and the rest.
Meditating in this way, by the previous application, he should cast the full oblation toward <s>Śiva</s>, who is both with parts and without parts,
or toward him as twofold, with the instrument made tranquil.
In the <s>Traiśirasa Tantra</s> this is taught as consisting in complete filling:
rising from the root, it is flooded all around by the moon of <s>Śiva</s>;
it arises from the root-current in the inner cavity, from birth up to the end;
it is the nectar of knowledge, stirred by the intense rays of the sun of <s>Śiva</s>.
With that he should fully satisfy the disciple, with the instrument made tranquil.
Radiant with rays of light situated in the lotus in the abode of emptiness,
taking hold of the teaching of motionless awareness in relation to support and supported,
and striking together the single bursting forth of the manifestation that is founded in birth,
beginning from the root-place and making it extend up to <s>Someśa</s>,
as long as it abides like space, so long it is called the tranquil state.
And in the revered <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> it is said: having filled the ladle with ghee,
having made the disciple likewise situated in himself, and remembering the root-mantra,
making <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, himself, the disciple, the ghee, and the fire one,
he should proceed slowly to the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, with no other thought.
There, undertaking retention of the breath and meditating on <s>Śiva</s> as with parts and without parts,
he should remain undisturbed for as long as the ghee has not been exhausted.

children.text: evaṃ yuktaḥ pare tattve guruṇā śivamūrtinā
children.translated_text: Joined in this way to the supreme <s>tattva</s> by the guru whose form is <s>Śiva</s>,
he does not again become a bound creature, for the bonds of <s>Māyā</s> have been burned.

children.text: dehapāte punaḥ prepsed yadi tattveṣu kutracit
children.translated_text: If, when the body falls, he should again desire enjoyments in any of the <s>tattvas</s>,
through distinctions of collectivity and individuality, and at the end the supreme state,
then, on the level of each such <s>tattva</s>, in its proper number, with no other thought,
he should perform a further joining by means of another full oblation.
The initiation that is declared to grant liberation, or to grant both enjoyment and liberation,
is twofold, according as it has the nature of <s>sabīja</s> or <s>nirbīja</s>.
For a child, for one whose death is known to be near, or for one incapacitated by old age and the like,
a seedless initiation should be performed when the force of the descent of power has arisen.
In the <s>nirbīja</s> initiation he should also purify the <s>sāmaya</s> bonds.
One who has received <s>nirbīja dīkṣā</s>, and who possesses devotion to the deity, fire, and guru,

children.text: iyataiva śivaṃ yāyāt sadyo bhogān vibhujya vā
children.translated_text: by just this much reaches <s>Śiva</s>, either immediately or after enjoying experiences.
And in the revered <s>Dīkṣottara</s> it is said: in the course of thirty-six finger-breadths,
he should abandon the <s>tattvas</s> and worlds in sequence, from the feet to the head.
For a mere instant that partless, bodiless one is to be contemplated: 'That supreme one am I.'
Meditating, 'By <s>Śakti</s> I cast him there,' he should initiate him.
But in <s>sabīja</s> initiation he should not purify the observances.
This is the distinction in it: as long as the child lives, the guru,
for the maintenance of the remaining course of life, should create the pure <s>tattvas</s> by the full oblation.
Flashing all at once from the undivided ocean of <s>Śiva</s>-consciousness,
he should meditate on the full oblation, casting forth the network of <s>tattvas</s> as flowing out in the form of light.
Or he should make the creation of pure <s>tattvas</s> through consecration with the jar,
likewise solely through the power of meditation, or else through full consecratory ablutions.
Earth, imagined as his stable form in the form of <s>Śiva</s>,
makes that very visualization firm; thus it is purified.
Water nourishes it; fire brings it to luminosity;
wind brings the touch of bliss, and space brings expansiveness.
In this way the group of subtle elements too is understood to be made of <s>Śiva</s>.
There is the great pervasion of supreme bliss and the falling away of every impurity.
Going toward <s>Śiva</s>, grasping, and praising <s>Śiva</s> as what is to be taken up,
as well as smelling, tasting, seeing, and touching, filled with the delight of <s>Śiva</s>, are sufficient;
and hearing that too: in this way the purity of the senses is described.
Conception, determination, self-measurement, illumination, attachment, and steadiness,
when these belong to the mind and the rest as having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, constitute their purity.
Restriction, coloring, the state of being an agent together with calculation,
knowing, and a sleep-like condition with regard to the portion of objects that is to be rejected:
in this way, for one established in unity with <s>Śiva</s>, this set of six sheaths too
is pure; the person, having attained the state of <s>Śiva</s>, is purified.
In the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Vidyeśa</s> there is no impurity at all.
Thus, through the creation of the pure <s>tattvas</s>, the disciple too
becomes made of them; this is indicated in the revered <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>:
The wise have said that bondage and liberation are both these senses:
when restrained they lead to bondage, and when released they lead to liberation.

children.text: etāni vyāpake bhāve yadā syurmanasā saha
children.translated_text: When these, together with the mind, are in the pervasive state,

children.text: muktāni kvāpi viṣaye rodhādbandhāya tāni tu ||
children.translated_text: they are liberated; but when there is obstruction in any object, they lead to bondage.
Thus a twofold condition of the senses,
according to the distinction between purity and impurity, is taught in the doctrine of the <s>Siddhayogīśvara</s>.
But the revered <s>Vidyāguru</s> says, in the exposition of the <s>Pramāṇastuti</s>:
This rule is taught for initiation with all mantras.

children.text: māyāntaśuddhau sarvāḥ syuḥ kriyā hyaparayā sadā
children.translated_text: In the purification that ends with <s>māyā</s>, all the actions should always be performed with the lower,

children.text: dvyātmayā sakalānte tu niṣkale parayaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: which is twofold in nature; but at the end of the <s>sakala</s> and in the <s>niṣkala</s>, with the higher alone.
And at the end of <s>Īśa</s>, the formulas beginning with <s>pivana</s> are used; at the end of the <s>sakala</s>, the set of five limbs is used.
Having considered the rule in this way, the best guru should perform the rite.
The number of oblations that was stated earlier in the <s>adhvan</s> for the <s>tattvas</s> and phonemes,
he should double that same number on the path of words, and make it fourfold there.
In due order, on the paths of mantra and <s>kalā</s>, it is doubled and doubled successively,
until, in the purification of the three <s>tattvas</s>, it becomes twentyfold from that.
In the rite for the three <s>tattvas</s>, there should be sixty oblations for each action.
In the rite for one <s>tattva</s>, they teach one hundred and eight oblations.
The complete oblations that are remembered along with the reverse rite,
in the purification of all the <s>adhvans</s>, have no different number at all.
Thus this <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), furnished with rites beginning with generation, has been taught.
Now this condensed <s>dīkṣā</s>, said to bestow attainment of <s>Śiva</s>-hood, is described.
Here there is no colored powder, no preliminary consecration, and no taking possession of ground or ritual field.

children.text: yatra tatra pradeśe tu pūjayitvā guruḥ śivam ||
children.translated_text: In whatever place he may be, the guru should worship <s>Śiva</s> there,
and, having mentally contemplated the <s>adhvan</s>, he who has crossed beyond the <s>tattvas</s> should initiate.
The guru performs it without the rites beginning with generation, by whatever <s>adhvan</s>,
down to the single <s>tattva</s>, while he is wholly intent upon the one state of <s>Śiva</s>.
Then, with the supreme mantra, saying, 'Now I purify this <s>tattva</s> of his,'
and ending with 'svāhā,' he should do this for each <s>tattva</s>; when it is purified, he should cast the complete oblation.
Thus he may perform it with other mantras, or with all of them as stated.
The name, enclosed by the <s>Parā</s> mantra, ending in 'svāhā,' and ending in the nominative case,

children.text: śataṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭaṃ vā tena śaktyaiva homayet ||
children.translated_text: he should use to offer one hundred, one thousand, or one hundred and eight oblations, according to his power alone.
After that, having purified with the formula 'complete,' what is deficient becomes excellent in this way.
Such is the initiation rite taught here and there in the scriptures by <s>Maheśin</s>.
He should purify the <s>tattvas</s> one by one with pairs of letters from the <s>Mātṛkā</s>,
or else with the compact mantra; this rule applies to all mantras.
In whatever way the guru, through well-practiced knowledge, is of the nature of identity with that,

children.text: gurustathā tathā kuryāt saṃkṣiptaṃ karma nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: in just that way he should perform the condensed rite, and not otherwise.
And in the revered <s>Brahmayāmala</s> it is said that even in the condensed rite he should contemplate

children.text: vyāptiṃ sarvādhvasāmānyāṃ kiṃtu yāge na vistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the general pervasion of all the <s>adhvans</s>; but in the worship there is no elaboration.
Thinking, 'It has not become identical with that,' he brings together the dispersed rite;
since it reaches identity gradually, he should perform the dispersed procedure.
This condensed procedure has been taught out of compassion by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: dīkṣottare kairaṇe ca tatra tatrāpi śāsane ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Dīkṣottara</s>, the <s>Kairaṇa</s>, and likewise here and there in the teachings.
Now the <s>dīkṣā</s> that grants immediate upward departure is described.
'At that very moment, or after enjoyment, at the fall of the body he goes to <s>Śiva</s>':
with these words in the <s>Mālinī</s> scripture, <s>Maheśin</s> has indicated it.
When the fall of the body is near, because the descent of power is manifest,
after obtaining the <s>Śāṃkarī</s> initiation, from that very moment of initiation onward
he goes to <s>Śiva</s>. This is the meaning here, from considering what precedes and follows,
as explained by our revered guru, <s>Śambhumūrti</s>.
For when, at the approach of death, the descent of power arises,
then, if it is weak, his life may come to an end through service to the guru and the like,
or else this descent of the Lord may fall upon him through relatives, friends, and others.

children.text: pūrvaṃ vā samayī naiva parāṃ dīkṣāmavāptavān ||
children.translated_text: Previously he may not even have been a <s>samayin</s>, nor have obtained the higher <s>dīkṣā</s>;
or, though he has obtained initiation, he may desire to give up his breaths without distress.
Then, at the end, the guru should perform for him the initiation of immediate upward departure.
But he should not perform upward departure for one whose impurity is unripe, nor for one whose karmic body still remains,
as is explained in the revered <s>Gahvara</s>.
Seeing the disciple overcome by old age and afflicted by disease,
he should cause him to depart upward and then assign him to the supreme <s>tattva</s>.
By the relation of qualifier and qualified, and according to the rule of free procedure,
the revered <s>Śambhu</s> has explained here the whole matter previously stated.
Having performed the entire procedure stated before, in accordance with the purification of the <s>samaya</s>,
he should place for him the blazing <s>kṣurikā</s>, the knife that cuts the vital points.
Having performed the previously stated <s>nyāsa</s>, with a brilliance like the fire of time,
and together with the pair beginning with 'sṛkchindi,' in the order of withdrawal,
he should make the fiery visualization, burning all the vital points,
and fill the body with breath from the big toe up to the head.
Then, drawing him upward from the big toe to the upper limit by the method to be stated,
he should cut the vital points up to the aperture and release him through <s>Kālarātrī</s>.
Joined by this yogic sequence, without oblations,
even a <s>samayin</s> attains that initiation: so it is in the revered <s>Mālinī</s> doctrine.
From the sixteen supports, the six wheels, the three targets, and the five voids,
entering one or another at some point, as in the previously stated rite for the bound soul,
and cutting the root from the bulb and so on through the contemplation of unity,
he should, by the application of the complete oblation, assign him to his chosen abode.
Having imagined the blazing trident of knowledge, shining with three blazing wheels,
with this he should repeatedly perform for him piercing, awakening, whirling,

children.text: dīpanaṃ tāḍanaṃ todaṃ calanaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: kindling, striking, pricking, and moving, again and again,
through the wheels from the bulb onward, especially in the lotus of the heart.
Then, having brought him to the twelve-finger limit, he should cast him into the pair of <s>bindus</s>,

children.text: nirlakṣye vā pare dhāmni saṃyuktaḥ parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: or into the signless supreme abode, joined with <s>Parameśvara</s>.
He should perform no further consecratory rite for him: thus says the deity in the <s>Gahvara</s>.
'What need has this perfected one of rites such as <s>śrāddha</s>?' This is the intended meaning.
In the revered <s>Dīkṣottara</s>, however, this procedure is enclosed in the fire.
The <s>haṃsa</s>, the male principle, is below it, joined with the <s>Rudra</s>-drop.
Having placed this in the disciple's body, he should, undisturbed, recite it one hundred times.
Having passed out upward in the space of a blink, the disciple thus reaches the supreme.
This very procedure is also found in the revered <s>Siddhayogīśvarīmata</s>.

children.text: iyam utkrāmaṇī dīkṣā kartavyā yogino guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>utkrāmaṇī dīkṣā</s> should be performed by a guru who is a yogin.
How will one who has not practiced the movement of the breath perform this
complete <s>brahmavidyā</s>, to be taught below, which is connected with the <s>niṣkala</s>?

children.text: karṇe 'sya vā paṭhedbhūyo bhūyo vāpyatha pāṭhayet
children.translated_text: Or he should recite it into his ear again and again, or else have him recite it repeatedly.

children.text: svayaṃ ca karma kurvīta tattvaśuddhyādikaṃ guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: The guru himself should perform the rite, beginning with the purification of the <s>tattvas</s>.
By the power of mantra and ritual action, at the full oblation, he should thus join him to the supreme;
even without practice of yoga, the guru can grant immediate departure.
He is able to accomplish it by the power of knowledge, mantra, ritual action, and meditation.
By this, the disciple is made to pass out by force, in a single instant.

children.text: kālasyollaṅghya bhogo hi kṣaṇiko 'syāstu kiṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: For his experience, having overstepped time, is momentary; what follows from that?

children.text: sadya utkrāntidā cānyā yasyāṃ pūrṇāhutiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: There is also another initiation that grants immediate departure, in which, at that time, he should give the full oblation
when that person's breaths are certainly desirous of departing.
Even without ritual action, by the power of the impending <s>brahmavidyā</s>, the guru
through the practice of recitation in the ear, draws him out from the net of <s>tattvas</s> and coverings.
As desired, in the <s>sakala</s>, the <s>niṣkala</s>, in both,

children.text: tattve vā yatra kutrāpi yojayetpudgalaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: or in any <s>tattva</s> whatsoever, he should join the individual soul in sequence.
A <s>samayin</s> or a <s>putraka</s> may likewise recite this <s>vidyā</s>.
From reciting it, however, joined with the <s>samaya</s>, he obtains attainment of a portion of <s>Rudra</s>.
For both of these are authorized for recitation and study.
They are not authorized for teaching or instruction; this is only study.
Yet when these two recite, by the very nature of the thing, that result is his.
Just as one who is forbidden from rites concerning spirits and the like, while himself remembering a mantra,
does not incur a lapse even in some case of possession, because he has relinquished agency,
and just as a <s>samayin</s> having scripture read aloud in an empty house
does not lapse, because it benefits the class of living beings situated within it,
so too, when this person himself recites the <s>vidyā</s>, by the nature of the thing,

children.text: tasminmukte na lupyeta yataḥ kiṃcitkaro 'tra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he does not lapse when someone is liberated through it, since here he does perform something.
But, it may be objected, he should not utter the scriptural procedure before an uninitiated person.
Well then, is a prohibition stated for him even in front of a wall?
By exclusion, only one who is capable of hearing and understanding
is prohibited here, not worms in a wall or birds.
Then, one may say, that person is like a stone, with the activities of his senses dissolved.
How is there any transgression of the prohibition for someone reciting before him?
But by the nature of the thing, even when his faculties have fallen away, he understands
inwardly, through self-luminous consciousness-power, without dependence on the faculties.
Desiring, indeed, to abandon the former body, he has not yet taken possession of the later one.
In between, the individual soul awakens through the power of the awakener.
Mantras are made of sound and are themselves of the nature of pure reflective awareness.
And, shining forth as meaning, they awaken one to that meaning.
Therefore, for this person whose faculties have fallen away, awakening arises of itself
because of the presence of contact with mantras homogeneous with his own consciousness.
For just as a wind of slight speed, when mixed with one of the same kind,
becomes swift, so the self whose reflective awareness is asleep awakens in this way.

children.text: prabuddhaḥ sa ca saṃjāto na cādīkṣita ucyate ||
children.translated_text: And when he has awakened and has been brought into being, he is not called uninitiated.

children.text: dīkṣā hi nāma saṃskāro na tvanyatso 'sti cāsya hi
children.translated_text: For what is called <s>dīkṣā</s> is a consecratory transformation, and nothing else; and that exists for him.

children.text: ata eva nijaṃ śāstraṃ paṭhati kvāpi sāmaye ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason a <s>samayin</s> may somewhere recite his own scripture.

children.text: tacchrutvā ko 'pi dhanyaścenmucyate nāsya sā kṣatiḥ
children.translated_text: If some fortunate person hears it and is liberated, there is no harm to him.
Let him not revile the scripture, which would bring fallenness upon both.
This is the ultimate purport of the rule, 'he should not recite before an uninitiated person.'

children.text: yathā ca samayī kāṣṭhe loṣṭe vā mantrayojanām ||
children.translated_text: And just as a <s>samayin</s>, applying a mantra to a piece of wood
or to a clod of earth, does not incur a lapse if it moves, so it is here.
For this <s>samayin</s>, who desires to attain conviction

children.text: pravṛttasya svabhāvena tasminmukte na vai kṣatiḥ
children.translated_text: and has thus proceeded by nature, there is indeed no harm when that person is liberated.
But a <s>sādhaka</s>, because of the constraint of destiny upon the fruit to be accomplished,
should perform the proper expiation even if his mantra has been heard by a fly.
Thus immediate departure has been explained; at the command of the guru,
even a <s>samayin</s> and the others, at the stated time, for the accomplishment of the stated aim,
may perform it himself, if he has practiced the going and coming of the movement of the breath.
Or a guru whose authority has not been fully established may do it for the purification of the <s>samaya</s>,
if he is situated on a lower level, but not one whose consciousness is kindled by knowledge.
Thus this immediate departure is indicated in the <s>Mālinīmata</s>,

children.text: svayaṃ vā guruṇā vātha kāryatvena maheśinā ||
children.translated_text: as something to be performed either by oneself or by the guru, according to <s>Maheśin</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ bhogaṃ virūpaṃ tu matvā dehaṃ tyajedyadi
children.translated_text: If, regarding all enjoyment as distorted, he should abandon the body,

children.text: tadā tena krameṇāśu yojitaḥ samayī śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, quickly joined by that sequence, the <s>samayin</s> becomes <s>Śiva</s>.
This immediate departure has been stated; the wise should guard it like their own life-breath.
Now I shall teach an initiation that gives reassurance to foolish people.
In the triangle, in the abode of fire, blazing all around with the color of fire,
in the brightly blazing left hand, purified from the airy city,
having taken up a certain seed, likewise within the heart
and in the hand, one should meditate on it as burning, intent solely on its recitation,
tormented by the burning mass of fire-kindled <s>phaṭ</s>-sounds.
the seed becomes seedless, incapable of producing its own sprout.
When it has been burned, it is not fit to sprout; by that very conviction,
the actions called impurity, <s>māyā</s>, and karma, through the power of mantra, meditation, and ritual action,
having been burned, do not serve their own effect. But this conviction of seedlessness
the glorious and very gracious <s>Śambhunātha</s> set forth to me.

children.text: bījasyāpyatra kāryā ca yojanā kṛpayā guroḥ
children.translated_text: Here too the guru, out of compassion, should make an application concerning the seed,
because <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), by being intensely kindled, may liberate even immobile beings.
The guru who, knowing in himself the accomplishment of recitation, oblation, worship, and meditation,

children.text: jñātvā dīkṣāṃ carettasya dīkṣā sapratyayā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: performs <s>dīkṣā</s>, his initiation is remembered as accompanied by conviction.
But this rule does not apply to an <s>avadhūta</s>, one beyond prescribed conduct, who knows reality.
The initiation that is accompanied by visible conviction is performed by those who observe ritual conduct.
In initiation by one beyond ritual conduct, however, no sign of conviction is stated,
since knowledge is its own assurance and does not require another result.
Meditation and the rest, however, are to be proved from their fruit; thus the established doctrine has taught.
Or he may perform the examination called purification by the balance, which is joined with signs of conviction,
as it was taught by <s>Parameśin</s> in the glorious <s>Tantrasadbhāva</s>.
And this too was indicated by <s>Parameśin</s> even in the glorious <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>:

children.text: ānanda udbhavaḥ kampo nidrā ghūrṇiśca pañcamī
children.translated_text: 'Bliss, emergence, trembling, sleep, and, fifth, reeling,'
with such words, which declare the gradation of powers.
Emergence consists in lightness, because the grasping of the body is concealed;
for the body is principally earthy, and at that time it abandons that predominance.
Having meditated on the disciple as having leapt upward by the mantra of future lightness,
the guru should perform there all the rites previously stated.
This, then, has been stated: the <s>dīkṣā</s> of purification by the balance, which gives conviction.
Now the ritual of initiation for one who is situated out of sight is taught.
'For the accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation he is led toward the true guru':
in this statement of the <s>Mālinī</s>, the word 'toward' denotes facing toward him.
And this disciple's facing toward him has the nature of being an object of that guru's compassion.
The phrase 'having propitiated him' indirectly marks the cause of compassion.
Because of connection with that, someone is released immediately,
and this too is the meaning of that jewel-like statement from the <s>Mālinī</s>.
'Immediately' means that there is no further moment such as an intention to go on his part;
rather, in just this way, being subject to compassion, the guru should raise him up.
For one whose body has been worn away by service to the guru, and who has reached death without obtaining initiation,
or again for one in whom such a disposition has arisen by itself at the moment of death,
or for one who has received the consecration of initiation from lower tantras and the like,
or for one who has obtained the rank of a <s>sāmayika</s> but has not found the higher initiation,
for one struck by a <s>ḍimba</s>, devoured by <s>Yogeśī</s>s through hostile magic,
or killed by a guru through yantra, tantra, and the like,
or again for one who has fallen from his own <s>samaya</s>, even though he had already obtained initiation,
because of the intense entreaty of relatives, wife, friends, or sons,
or because of the power of compassion that has arisen in himself regarding that person,
when he has understood the nature of the portion of <s>śaktipāta</s> that has come through that person's face,
the guru should perform the initiation that raises the dead and bestows <s>Śiva</s>hood.
In the glorious <s>Mṛtyuñjayasiddha</s> and other scriptures, that was taught by <s>Parameśin</s>:
'For an uninitiated person, for a king and the like, for the indolent, the fallen, or the dead,
and for a child, the sick, a woman, or an elder, one should prescribe the raising of the dead.'

children.text: vidhiḥ sarvaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ sa tu saṃkṣipta iṣyate
children.translated_text: The whole procedure has been stated before; but here it is desired in abbreviated form,
since it is without worship of the guru and the rest, and since externally it is for enjoyment.
The consecrated lodging, the ritual gruel, the ground, the bed, and the construction of the maṇḍala
are of no use here for the consecration of that disciple or for the vision in a dream.
But the maṇḍala here is for the sake of satisfaction through the presence of mantras,
and the worship of the deity on the following day does not directly help this person.
Through ritual action, implements, place, maṇḍala, form, and mantra,
through union in meditation, single-minded devotion to him, knowledge, and becoming absorbed in him,
for anyone who has entered into him, and likewise for the disciples and the guru,
these eleven have been taught as causes of presence.
Each later one is superior to the previous, and also according to the necessity of their mixture.
Ritual action is especially abundant; flowers and the like should be excellent and endowed with the proper marks.
The place may be a single-liṅga shrine and the like, where the self becomes serene.
The maṇḍala is the triple-trident lotus-wheel that appears in the mantra-maṇḍala.
When seen even without invitation, it brings about the state of a <s>samayin</s>.
This is stated in the <s>Mālinītantra</s>: 'the accomplished <s>samaya</s>-maṇḍala.'
From the two words 'merely seen' and 'accomplished,' this is established.
The form is one of blazing appearance, and the mantra likewise is very blazing.
The remainder is clear; therefore it is not explained here again at length.
Having made the maṇḍala and worshiped the deity there, then with kuśa grass
and cow-dung he should make a figure and place it there as though it were the disciple.
Then, into that figure, after depositing the one course to be purified by the visualization of pervasion
as far as <s>prakṛti</s>, he should again perform this procedure.
By means of the <s>mahājāla</s> practice, from the midst of all the courses,
he should draw forth the consciousness and place it there; its procedure is stated:

children.text: mūlādhārādudetya prasṛtasuvitatānantanāḍyadhvadaṇḍaṃ vīryeṇākramya nāsāgaganaparigataṃ vikṣipan vyāptumīṣṭe
children.translated_text: Rising from the <s>mūlādhāra</s>, seizing with force the widely extended staff of the path of the countless spreading channels, passing through the space of the nose, and casting it forth, he seeks to pervade it,
until, with a network of still more massed flames made lovely by smoke, he covers the wheel of the course; this is the practice called the Great Net, the bringing of the desired soul.

children.text: etenācchādanīyaṃ vrajati paravaśaṃ saṃmukhīnatvamādau paścād ānīyate cetsakalamatha tato 'pyadhvamadhyādyatheṣṭam
children.translated_text: By this, what is to be covered over first comes under control and becomes turned toward him; if it is then brought near, everything follows, and thereafter even the middle of the <s>adhvan</s> and the rest, as desired.

children.text: ākṛṣṭāvuddhṛtau vā mṛtajanaviṣaye karṣaṇīye 'tha jīve yogaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthāgamaparigamito jālanāmā mayoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In attraction or in lifting up, when a dead person is to be drawn, or then a living being, the yoga called <s>jāla</s>, learned from the āgama of <s>Śrīśaṃbhunātha</s>, has been stated by me.
