children.text: ciravighaṭite senāyugme yathāmilite punarhayagajanaraṃ svāṃ svāṃ jātiṃ rasādabhidhāvati
children.translated_text: Just as, when two armies long separated have met again, horse, elephant, and man eagerly run each toward his own class,
so too, when the organs, breaths, and wheels of the nāḍīs have come together, they are to be unified according to their own respective relish, brought under control by one's own net.
The jīva drawn by the great net by one endowed with knowledge
at that very moment abandons heaven, ghosthood, animal birth, and hell.
And this person, reached by that yoga of knowledge and mantra,
then gives up the artificial identification with the heart of the sādhya, as a yogin does.
That he should abandon various states beginning with immobile existence and states of sharing or nearing those worlds

children.text: tyajecceti na citraṃ sa evaṃ yaḥ karmaṇāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: is no wonder for such a one, even by means of ritual action.
But when he has entered a human body, since it is a body fit for qualification,

children.text: na tadā mucyate dehāddehānte tu śivaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: he is not then released from that body; at the end of the body he goes to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tasmindehe tu kāpy asya jāyate śāṅkarī parā
children.translated_text: In that body, however, some supreme devotion belonging to <s>Śaṅkara</s> arises in him,
from the growth of knowledge, or even from an ācārya who has not been attended upon.
Although this jīva remains established in that body, by the power of the <s>jāla</s>
he pervades this body made of darbha and the like, without making it conscious even by his own presiding presence.
Again, through the superior power of yoga, mantra, ritual, and knowledge,
he at that very moment quickly gives up even the human body.
Even a jīva who is as if asleep and even bodiless, when drawn by the <s>jāla</s>,

children.text: ākṛṣṭo dārbhamāyāti dehaṃ phalamayaṃ ca vā ||
children.translated_text: comes into a body made of darbha, or into one made of fruit.
Whatever there is, such as nutmeg and the like, a body may be fashioned with that;
because it is appropriate both inwardly and outwardly, that is called superior here.
Then that jīva, brought by the procedure of the <s>jāla</s>, remains like one asleep,
because he has not obtained the equipment of a body and so on distinguished by mind.

children.text: na spandate na jānāti na vakti na kilecchati
children.translated_text: He does not move, does not know, does not speak, and indeed does not desire.
For just such a one, all the saṃskāras should be arranged as before.
Having done everything previously taught by means of seedless initiation,

children.text: vidhiṃ yojanikāṃ pūrṇāhutyā sākaṃ kṣipecca tam ||
children.translated_text: one should cast that yojanikā rite, together with the full oblation, into him.
When the body of darbha and the like has been offered into the mantra-fire together with the full oblation,
he, his bonds released, goes to <s>Śiva</s>, free from return.

children.text: sapratyayā tviyaṃ yatra spandate darbhajā tanuḥ
children.translated_text: But where this is accompanied by awareness, the body born from darbha trembles;
there it occurs through the union consisting in the offering of breath, mind, and mantra.
That too has been stated for one who has practice; it is not for one who merely relies on force.
For his sake, it should be done by the causes taught in the raising of the dead, as far as possible.
Initiation of a living person who is absent is also to be performed; but that is seedless.
In that case, when a form mostly made as an image of darbha has been imagined through <s>jāla</s>-yoga,
the attraction of the jīva occurs by mere resolve, because of his fear of death.
The rest is as before, except for the burning away of the form produced from kuśa and the like.
Because of limitation, lack of lordship, and the constraint of necessity upon what is to be accomplished,
attraction by the <s>jāla</s> does not arise without practice, because of attachment and aversion.
If, while absent, he has been initiated by dissimilar initiations,
there the later one should be stronger, while the lower one serves for consecratory formation.
But when a bhukti-yojanikā has likewise been performed by many gurus,
there is variety in enjoyment because of connection with varied causes.
In indirect initiation beyond <s>Māyā</s>, one should join him for enjoyment,

children.text: bhogānīpsā durlabhā hi satī vā bhogahānaye ||
children.translated_text: for non-desire for enjoyments is rare; and if it is present, it leads to the loss of enjoyment.
For it has been said: between one's own cognition and another's cognition, one's own cognition is stronger.
When there is obstruction it is the obstructing one; so too in cases of equality or indifference.
The venerable <s>Dharmaśiva</s> also says in the indirect karmapaddhati:
in indirect initiation, if, in the rite of the full oblation properly performed,
the fire emits a ciṭiciṭā sound together with smoke,
takes on the color of a blue cloud, repeatedly blazes up and subsides,
becomes expanded and terrible in form, and even runs downward along the ground,
or there is an inauspicious sound such as that of crows, then the guru should examine him.
At that time, because of sins such as brahmanicide and the secondary sins connected with them,

children.text: tadā tasya na kartavyā dīkṣāsmin akṛte vidhau ||
children.translated_text: initiation is not to be performed for him while this rite remains undone.
The <s>Navātman</s>, placed within the enclosure of phaṭ and puṭa, and again accompanied by five phaṭs,
followed by the eight phaṭs after the words, 'I burn the sins of so-and-so,'
thus a thousandfold homa should be performed with sesame seeds and rice grains.

children.text: ante pūrṇā ca dātavyā tato 'smai dīkṣayā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end the full oblation should be given; then, by initiation, the guru should for him
perform the purification of the tattvas up to the limit of the supreme yojana.
Even for a sinful limited soul who is present directly,
if he has obtained the highest power consisting of the Lord, one should perform just this procedure.

children.text: yadi vā daiśikaḥ samyaṅ na dīptastasya tatpurā ||
children.translated_text: Or, if the initiator had not been properly kindled for him before that,
having performed purification through expiations, gifts, and prāṇāyāmas,
and also having done this rite, he should perform the initiation without hesitation.
In whatever state he may be, a knower of the tattvas liberates bound souls
by mere will, since he is directly <s>Śiva</s>; therefore one should always worship him.

children.text: śāṭhyaṃ tatra na kāryaṃ ca tatkṛtvādho vrajecchiśuḥ
children.translated_text: No deceit is to be practiced there; having done that, the pupil would go downward.

children.text: na punaḥ kīrtayettasya pāpaṃ kīrtayitā vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one mention his sin again; the one who mentions it goes
to hell. Therefore one should avoid that. Such is the rule in the <s>Dīkṣottara</s>.
This indirect initiation has been taught in two ways, according to the distinction between the living person and the other one.
Now we shall state what is called <s>liṅgoddhāra</s>, prescribed solely in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>.
It is said in the venerable <s>Mālinītantra</s>, after teaching the fixing of the earthly principle:

children.text: uktvā yo yojito yatra sa tasmānna nivartate ||
children.translated_text: Wherever a person has been joined, from that he does not turn back.
The discipline that has arisen for someone, by force of fitness, in whatever place it has arisen,
there alone he is to be appointed at the time of <s>dīkṣā</s>; then that person,
having obtained every fruit, is joined to <s>Śiva</s> and is released.
Even if he has not been joined, after attaining upward purification from the lords of the worlds,
he becomes pure, comes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>, and his bondage to <s>saṃsāra</s> is burned away.
And after setting forth the fixing of the person, I said that this is Vedāntic;

children.text: kapilāya purā proktaṃ prathame paṭale tathā
children.translated_text: it was formerly taught to <s>Kapila</s>, likewise in the first chapter.
By this orderly sequence he attains the supreme state,

children.text: na bhūyaḥ paśutāmeti śuddhe svātmani tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: does not again become a bound soul, and remains in his own purified self.
Therefore this meaning is indeed suggested: even among the principles below <s>Śivatattva</s>,
one who has been joined to the principles is capable of being lifted out again.
The <s>Śivāgama</s>, which grants discrimination of the matters taught in all scriptures,
is superior to all other scriptures.
And without knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, there is once again the arising of bound-soulhood.
The sequence is: descent of power, destruction of impurity, the wish to depart,
<s>dīkṣā</s>, awakening, abandonment of what is to be rejected, and the dissolution of what is to be appropriated,
the abandonment of the bond of enjoyership, the cessation of the lord's agency,
and abiding in one's own self. Thus, because of being established in another system,
the need of being lifted out has been taught for one impelled by <s>Śiva</s>'s power.
Now, for those who stand in the lower sphere of other tantras such as Vaiṣṇava and Buddhist ones,
when the lotus of the heart has been opened by masses of rays from the sun that is <s>Śiva</s>,
then first there is <s>liṅgoddhṛti</s>, removal of the prior mark, and afterward the rite of <s>dīkṣā</s>.
Even one formerly established in another <s>liṅga</s>, through <s>dīkṣā</s>, may reach the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
In that matter, after making him fast, on the next day, by means of a common mantra,
one should worship the Lord on a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> and make that person hear the procedure:
'This man formerly bore a <s>liṅga</s>; now, however, he has been directed by you.
Since you are gracious, therefore bestow complete favor upon him.
And let there be no expiation for him arising from fear over abandoning his own former <s>liṅga</s>.
May he quickly become one with you and attain enjoyment and liberation.'
Then, having received the command, 'So be it,' and having taken up that vow of his,
one should remove it, cast it into water, and bathe him suitably.
After he has bathed, one should next sprinkle him with water from the argha vessel.
Then one should give him the five products of the cow and a tooth-stick.
Then, blindfolding him, one should lead him in and make him bow down.
<s>Praṇava</s>, <s>Mātṛkā</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vyomavyāpī</s>, the six-syllabled mantra,
<s>Bahurūpa</s>, and then the mantra called <s>Netra</s>: these seven are common mantras.
From among them one should assign one mantra to him.
He too should recite it for exactly a day and night, eating little or not eating at all.
After assigning the mantra to him, in the fire consecrated by the common rite,
and after satisfying that mantra, one should perform purification of the vow.
With that very mantra worshipped, having enclosed this person's name within it,
one should adapt the formula, 'I purify the expiation, <s>phaṭ svāhā</s>.'

children.text: śataṃ sahasraṃ vā hutvā punaḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: After offering a hundred or a thousand oblations, and again the full oblation,
and, according to the rite, casting in the formula ending in <s>vauṣaṭ</s>, one should summon the lord of the vow.
With <s>tāra</s>, saying 'to the lord of the vow' and 'obeisance,' one should worship him.
And one should make him hear: 'By <s>Śiva</s>'s command, you have no further business with this person.'
Then the lord of the vow is to be satisfied with a formula ending in <s>svāhā</s>; then he,
after being asked for forgiveness, should be dismissed, and then the fire too should be dismissed.
The announcement of that to the deity and the dismissal are with the words, 'Forgive me.'
Then on the third day, the whole procedure is remembered as before,
beginning with the preliminary residence and ending with the rite of one's chosen <s>dīkṣā</s>.
For former bearers of another <s>liṅga</s>, the <s>dīkṣā</s> for liberation is without eligibility for office.
They, as reborn ones, are not fit for the path of becoming a <s>sādhaka</s> or an <s>ācārya</s>.
Yet even reborn ones, kindled by knowledge, may become seats of guruhood.
This is for liberation alone, not for enjoyment; or for enjoyment too only by way of an auxiliary means.
So spoke the teacher <s>Īśānaśiva</s> in his own manual,
he who fully understood the principle taught in the <s>Yāmala</s> of the venerable Goddess.
Even for one whose guru is at the end of the lineage but lies under a lower view,
after performing this consecration, one should teach the secret; not otherwise, as is said in the <s>Kāmika</s>.
Even to one consecrated in another tantra, one should not reveal the secret.
Even if established in his own tantra, a final-lineage guru who has resorted to an ignorant guru,
and afterward has no confidence there, should in that case too perform the rite.
The mantra that this person has recited, coming from the mouth of an ignorant teacher,
is without potency; and that guru is not qualified here, because of the stated defect.

children.text: tato 'sya śuddhiṃ prākkṛtvā tato dīkṣāṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Therefore, first performing purification for him, one should then perform <s>dīkṣā</s>.
If someone was formerly initiated by a guru established in a lower view,
and afterward, by force of intense power, he goes to a true guru,

children.text: tadāpyasya śiśorevaṃ śuddhiṃ kṛtvā sa sadguruḥ ||
children.translated_text: then that true guru too, after purifying that pupil in this way,
should perform the whole rite beginning with <s>dīkṣā</s>, according to the prescribed rule.
Even if he has reached a true guru, if the guru does not know this person's state of fitness,
then, when knowledge is being given, that disciple should show his own fitness.
But in every case, if he does not speak, or if he speaks the opposite,

children.text: ajño vastuta eveti tattyaktvetthaṃ vidhiṃ caret
children.translated_text: then he is in fact ignorant; abandoning him, one should perform the rite in this way.
No fear of concealment should be entertained here by an intelligent person.
Being touched by what is lower is concealment, not the discernment of a higher means.
Those who have been initiated in the <s>Siddhānta</s> tantras, divided into ten and eighteen varieties,
and in the sixty-four <s>Bhairava</s> tantras, he should initiate those bound souls into the <s>Trika</s>.
In the <s>Siddhavīrāvalīsāra</s>, in the <s>Bhairavīya</s>, and also in the <s>Kula</s>,
the initiation obtained through the sequence of five initiations is called <s>Anuttara</s>.
Therefore everyone, even one established below, is favored after the raising of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Even one who, through the prompting of <s>Maheśāna</s> dwelling in the heart,
wishes to understand scriptural knowledge in full detail should go to many gurus.
And he should receive their initiations also, culminating in consecratory sprinkling,
for those initiations strengthen knowledge when performed by those who possess each particular knowledge.

children.text: uktaṃ ca śrīmate śāstre tatra tatra ca bhūyasā
children.translated_text: And this has been said in the venerable scripture, and often in many places:
just as a bee seeking fragrance may go from one flower to another,
so a disciple seeking knowledge may go from one guru to another.
Among many gurus, the one from whom the highest knowledge has been obtained

children.text: prāptaṃ so 'sya gururdīkṣā nātra mukhyā hi saṃvidi
children.translated_text: is his guru; for in consciousness <s>dīkṣā</s> is not the principal thing here.
But when he has reached a guru who is the storehouse of all knowledge and is firmly established,
the wise man, intent on inquiry into each matter, should worship him alone.
Thus the procedure of <s>dīkṣā</s> has been taught, culminating in the raising of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Now the remaining discipline, useful for those who remain alive, is taught.
This initiation that has been described, with its many kinds and ending with the funerary rite,

children.text: sā saṃskriyāyai mokṣāya bhogāyāpi dvayāya vā ||
children.translated_text: is for consecratory transformation, for liberation, for enjoyment, or for both.

children.text: tatra saṃskārasiddhyai yā dīkṣā sākṣānna mocanī
children.translated_text: There, the initiation that is for the accomplishment of consecratory transformation is not directly liberating.
But the one that directly liberates through the force of intentional connection is with seed.
For those who have been initiated by both of these,
the lifelong conduct of the <s>putraka</s> and the others must be stated, so that identity with that may become established.
Whether for one who desires enjoyment or for one who desires liberation, from one's own awareness, the guru, and the scripture,

children.text: pramāṇādyā saṃskriyāyai dīkṣā hi guruṇā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: an initiation based on valid authority is performed by the guru for consecratory transformation.

children.text: tataḥ sa saṃskṛtaṃ yogyaṃ jñātvātmānaṃ svaśāsane
children.translated_text: Then, knowing himself to be consecrated and fit within his own teaching,
he follows the practice of the realities taught there for enjoyment and for liberation.
Even for one who would obtain enjoyment and liberation solely through confidence in the teacher,
one should state his conduct in order to destroy the arising of obstacles to that.
Even one who shares equal certainty from his own awareness and from the guru's awareness
should be instructed in the remaining discipline for the pacification of obstacles and the like.

children.text: yaḥ sarvathā parāpekṣāmujjhitvā tu sthito nijāt
children.translated_text: But one who, having entirely abandoned dependence on another, stands from his own
certainty, and also one who stands solely from the teacher's certainty,
those two are naturally perfected and seedless; who would prescribe a remaining discipline for them?
Yet, in due sequence, those two are devoted to identity with that, to the means, and to worship of the guru.
For the sake of the remaining discipline of these persons, the daily and occasional rites are fixed.
Desire-based rites are excluded, because desires are various and have various means for their accomplishment.
There the daily rule is the performance of twilight worship, worship among the host of deities,
together with the guru, fire, and scripture, and compassion toward beings.
The occasional rule for all festival days is worship and recitation,
and, according to particular circumstance, the sequence of the <s>pavitraka</s> rite.
This initiation of the teacher has been analyzed in many divisions,
and explanation and the like are certainly its additional occasional observance.

children.text: tatrādau śiśave brūyād gurur nityavidhiṃ sphuṭam
children.translated_text: There, at the beginning, the guru should clearly explain the daily rule to the pupil,
after considering the pupil's fitness for expanded and unexpanded forms.
Having seen in the disciple his fitness for the potency, pervasion, and so on
of the principal and other mantras, he should bestow that very root mantra upon him.
For this person, though initiated in that scripture, is suspected of unrestricted conduct.

children.text: na mukhye yogya ityanyasevātaḥ syāttu yogyatā ||
children.translated_text: He is not fit for the principal mantra; but through service to another, fitness will arise.
But for a <s>sādhaka</s> who desires enjoyment, or for one who is to become a <s>sādhaka</s>,
a mantra proved by the falling of flowers should be bestowed for the accomplishment of what is to be accomplished.

children.text: vitate guṇabhūte vā vidhau diṣṭe punarguruḥ
children.translated_text: When an expanded or subordinate procedure has again been prescribed, the guru,
knowing his fitness, should perform for him the essential procedure in concise form.

children.text: tatraiṣa niyamo yadyan māntraṃ rūpaṃ na tadguruḥ
children.translated_text: In this matter the rule is this: whatever form belongs to mantra, the guru should not
write it down and disclose it to the disciple, especially in the higher teaching.

children.text: mantrā varṇātmakāste ca parāmarśātmakāḥ sa ca
children.translated_text: Mantras consist of phonemes, and those are of the nature of reflective awareness;
if that awareness is not different from the guru's consciousness, then it passes into the pupil.

children.text: lipisthitastu yo mantro nirvīryaḥ so 'tra kalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: But a mantra that remains in writing is here regarded as powerless.
By the force of convention, its radiance does not spread from a book.
Thus it is said in the <s>Siddhāmata</s>, 'those whose knowledge was learned from books.'

children.text: ye tu pustakalabdhe 'pi mantre vīryaṃ prajānate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those who recognize power even in a mantra obtained from a book
are said to be <s>Bhairavīya</s> consecrated ones, naturally perfected.
Knowing this correctly, the guru, trembling with supreme bliss,

children.text: tādṛśe tādṛśe dhāmni pūjayitvā vidhiṃ caret
children.translated_text: should perform the rite after worshiping in such and such an abode.
The guru should act so that the observance of one disciple
is not understood by another disciple, since loss of secrecy carries fault.
He should declare the pure triad of goddesses, or, through the union of the pair,
one pure goddess, or else one whose nature is the pair.
There, having grasped the mantra clearly, urged in a low voice
from the guru's mouth at the beginning, he should practice it himself mentally.
Then, with care, he should perform the well-taught triad of purification of place, body, and interior,

children.text: nyāsaṃ dhyānaṃ japaṃ mudrāṃ pūjāṃ kuryātprayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>nyāsa</s>, meditation, recitation, <s>mudrā</s>, and worship.

children.text: tatra prabhāte saṃbudhya sveṣṭāṃ prāgdevatāṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: There, waking at dawn, he should remember his desired, previously prescribed deity.
Having performed the necessary duties and become pure, then, in the house,
taking his place facing north, in the triad of place, body, and inner domain,
he should perform purification and install the mantras in their proper places,
show the <s>mudrā</s>s, and meditate on their nature as both differentiated and undifferentiated.
There he should also worship mentally in the body, the nectar, the intellect, the ether, and the earth,
and perform recitation according to his ability, dedicating this to the deity.
He should practice this at every twilight for the attainment of identity with that deity.
Others, however, say that the four twilight rites are to be performed toward the east, north, west, and the ten directions;
but this is a tantric procedure, and it is not our view.

children.text: yāsau kālādhikāre prāk sandhyā proktā catuṣṭayī ||
children.translated_text: That fourfold twilight rite which was previously taught in the section on time
should itself be internalized, and then one should perform the twilight observance.
Or the disciple may perform the work belonging to the four twilight rites in a single one,
being intent on recitation, understanding, the duties toward the guru, and so on.
Because of the method of identity taught in the meditation on twilight,
through the force of that impression he becomes identical with it at all times.
Then, at whatever time he wishes, the disciple should perform worship with flowers, wine, and the like
on a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> or similar place, in accordance with his resources and capacity.
Being thoroughly purified, and having performed the whole rite up to its end in internal recitation,
the wise person should first prepare the vessel of <s>argha</s> as before, with his chosen mantra.
With that he should sprinkle the <s>sthaṇḍila</s>, flowers, and everything else.
Then, having there mentally arranged the sequence of door-deities, seats, and gurus,
he should worship, entered by <s>Śiva</s>, beginning with the worship of his own body.
Then he should behold that <s>sthaṇḍila</s> as stainless like space and crystal,
as consisting of awareness, and there he should see his own host of deities
as reflections, and, from the standpoint of awareness, as the original image.
This is the principal invocation, like winds called forth by a fan.
For just as wind, though all-pervading, is made serviceable by a fan,
so too the all-pervading circle of mantras becomes effective through established convention.
This same principle is stated by the <s>Catuṣkapañcāśikā</s>.
And in the venerable <s>Nirmaryādaśāstra</s> this very point was taught by the Lord.

children.text: devaḥ sarvagato deva nirmaryādaḥ kathaṃ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: When asked, 'O god, since <s>Śiva</s> is without boundary and all-pervading,
how is he invoked, or how is he dismissed?', the Lord replied:
'O goddess, it is the mental impression that is invoked, and the mental impression that is released.
In ultimate reality there is no invocation or dismissal of the deity.

children.text: āvāhito mayā devaḥ sthaṇḍile ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The deity has been invoked by me and established on the <s>sthaṇḍila</s>;

children.text: pūjitaḥ stuta ityevaṃ hṛṣṭvā devaṃ visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: he has been worshiped and praised': rejoicing in this way, one should dismiss the deity.
For unawakened living beings this is indeed for the generation of satisfaction.
Otherwise, how would they enter into practices such as invocation?
But in time, having entered the Lord's teaching, they come to understand,
step by step, the attainment of the deity, beginning with the worlds.
Their whole accumulation of ignorance has been destroyed by the radiance of the lamp of knowledge:

children.text: kuto vānīyate devaḥ kutra vā nīyate 'pi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: from where could the deity be brought, or to where could he be led away?
For by distinctions such as gross and subtle, he is established everywhere.
When the host of mantras has been invoked, satisfaction should be offered with gifts of flowers and wine,
and with incense, in keeping with the strength of faith and devotion.
For the blazing mantras of <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Nāda</s>, and the rest, satisfaction should first be made with wines, flesh,
and red substances, and afterward with abundant flowers, incense, and the like.

children.text: āgatasya tu mantrasya na kuryāttarpaṇaṃ yadi ||
children.translated_text: If one does not make a satisfying offering to a mantra that has arrived,
it takes away half the body: so, indeed, <s>Śambhu</s> has said.
Whatever gives expansiveness to this person's mind,
with that very thing he should perform worship: this is <s>Śambhu</s>'s settled conclusion.
For practitioners who desire enjoyment, the rule is governed by restriction;

children.text: mumukṣūṇāṃ tattvavidāṃ sa eva tu nirargalaḥ
children.translated_text: but for knowers of reality who desire liberation, that same rule is unrestricted.
One who wishes to bring about a particular effect should touch a particular cause,
just as someone desiring red cotton fiber uses a heap of seeds corresponding to it.
And in enjoyment there are varied particular effects, impelled by their causes,
through attention to place, time, quality, substance, action, and so on.
An action may be small or abundant, fashioned with external factors
or with those born of intention, factors that give delight to the heart.
For one who seeks liberation, however, this makes no particular difference with respect to the method of the highest good.
For in <s>brahman</s> they do not praise the sorry distinctions of abundance and scarcity.
Because consciousness has freedom as its essence, and because it is a mass of bliss,
the rite should be for becoming identical with it, by means that delight the heart.
The rasa which the class of states lets flow, because it is filled with non-difference from <s>Śiva</s>,
that very rasa the wise person should offer for worship in the supreme abode.
I have also stated this in many ways among the hymns in my own daily liturgy:
Resting upon the unfolding radiance of the ultimate state, there shines forth
that vision of supreme nectar by which the knowers of the secret worship you.
Having made the sustaining base, washed in an instant by the sprinkling of the rasa of wonder, with mental flowers taken up, fragrant from their own nature,

from the sequence of the priceless <s>argha</s>-vessel that is one's own heart filled with the nectar of bliss, I worship you, together with the goddess, day and night in the temple of the body-deity.
This three-world realm, made of the rasa of many tastes, placed upon the yantra of the heart-wheel, being pressed down by the heavy weight of discriminating insight laid above...

children.text: yatsaṃvitparamāmṛtaṃ mṛtijarājanmāpahaṃ jṛmbhate tena tvāṃ haviṣā pareṇa parame saṃtarpaye 'harniśam ||
children.translated_text: By that supreme nectar of consciousness which unfolds and removes death, old age, and birth, with that highest oblation I satisfy you, O supreme one, day and night.
Thus, inwardly contemplating the meaning contained in the three verses,
he should satisfy the host of deities with whatever disposition he has.
Afterward he should display the <s>mudrā</s> (ritual gesture), whether mentally through yoga,
by speech through union with the <s>mantra</s>, or with the body through proper arrangement.

children.text: kṛtvā japaṃ tataḥ sarvaṃ devatāyai samarpayet
children.translated_text: Having performed recitation, he should then dedicate everything to the deity.
And that was stated earlier in the procedure for determining the reality of agency.
Then the dismissal should be performed through the practice of identity with awakened consciousness,
or after producing the satisfaction of the <s>mantra</s> in the fire according to the prescribed procedure.
Except for the offering dedicated to the doorway, the altar-seat, and the group of gurus,
he should eat the rest himself, or else cast it into deep water.
Aquatic creatures were formerly initiated by <s>Śambhu</s> himself
through the future rite, when he was incarnate as the glorious <s>Mīnanātha</s>.
But whatever is eaten by cats, mice, and other uninitiated beings
leads, by producing doubt and alarm, to disease and to hell.
Therefore even a learned knower of reality, though his doubt and alarm have been destroyed,
should not do such a thing openly, out of a desire to benefit people.
In the venerable great scripture of the doctrine, that was said by the Lord himself:
one should oneself be intent on driving out the contraction of doubt,

children.text: bhavettathā yathānyeṣāṃ śaṅkā no manasi sphuret
children.translated_text: yet in such a way that doubt does not arise in the minds of others.
Then, after wiping clean, he should bathe, and afterward worship with a flower.
He should cast all the flowers and other things present there into that deep water.
This <s>sthaṇḍila-yāga</s> (altar-ground worship) in the daily rite has been taught by <s>Śambhu</s>.
